"Definitely. That'll be ground-breaking. That'll be the next level for me," Dubois told Sky Sports.

"I've fought everyone then really from this era. I've fought them all. Fury's the last one.

"Fury's a fighting man, I'm sure he would want it. Let's see how he does with AJ. Let's see. I'm sure Frank [Warren, who promotes Fury and Dubois] would love to make that fight."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua come together in a face-off ahead of their fight on December 11.

Dubois has twice headlined at Wembley Stadium against Anthony Joshua and then Oleksandr Usyk. Fury versus Dubois would fill any stadium.

"This is what boxing is. This is the highest level really, this is it at the highest level. This is what it looks like," Dubois said.

Fury and Dubois do have a past. They sparred briefly many years ago. "That was just when I was turning pro," Dubois said. "I went to spar his cousin Hughie and then he popped in for a few rounds. Great memories, great work."

It was when Fury was returning to boxing after ballooning in weight. "So he was massive then," he said, but added with a laugh: "He was elusive."

Dubois fell short in his undisputed championship fight with Usyk but he remains determined to scale the summit of the heavyweight division.

"To win all the belts. That's the main thing now for me, collecting all the other belts," he said. "It would mean everything to have all those belts. No one can take that away from me. That's what I'm after now.

"Amongst all the names of history, not just that, for myself and what's left to achieve in boxing as well."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBO heavyweight rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley. Video courtesy of DAZN

What next?

After only being taken two rounds in his last fight, Dubois wants to box again "soon, really soon. I want to be out soon, as soon as possible. Whenever the belts are ready, whenever the top challengers are ready, that's what I want. I want to fight".

Dubois is hoping his next opponent will be WBC titlist Agit Kabayel or IBF belt-holder Filip Hrgovic, whom Dubois has beaten before.

"Any one of them [next], Hrgovic, he was there on Saturday, maybe him or Kabayel," he said. "Hrgovic was tough as well, Kabayel, we'll see, we'll see what he's about. He ain't been in with a guy like me but he's a good fighter.

"Just anyone with a damn belt… Anyone who wants it."

Sports.title: Bavuma's Test-best ton has South Africa in dominant position vs Australia
Sports.content:
South Africa captain Temba Bavuma struck his Test-best score of 179 to see his side into a dominant position in the second Test against Australia, as they look to level the three-match series.

Bavuma's magnificent innings helped rescue the Proteas from a perilous position of 40-4, with Australia's bowlers on top during the first two rain-affected days in Gqeberha but Bavuma, along with vital lower-order contributions from Marco Jansen (85) and Simon Harmer (82) helped wrestle the match the home side's way.

Kagiso Rabada only added to their advantage by striking with his fourth ball back from a hamstring injury that has sidelined him since June, with Nic Maddinson poking an edge to third slip for his second duck in three innings since his own Test return.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kagiso Rabada's return to Test cricket for South Africa began with the 'perfect start' after he took a wicket with his fourth ball against Australia

Australia ultimately closed on 3-1, still trailing South Africa by 422 runs on first innings, though with so much time lost to wet weather already in the Test match, the hosts are up against the clock over the final two days in their push for victory and force a series-decider in Cape Town from October 27.

South Africa resumed the third morning on 97-5 and swiftly lost a sixth wicket as Wiaan Mulder (13) was bounced out by Mitchell Starc for his 450th Test wicket.

Score summary - South Africa vs Australia, second Test, Gqeberha South Africa 425-9 declared after 127.1 overs in first innings: Temba Bavuma (179), Marco Jansen (85), Simon Harmer (82); Scott Boland (5-81), Mitchell Starc (3-89) Australia 3-1 after 4 overs in first innings: Scott Boland (2no), Travis Head (1no); Kagiso Rabada (1-0)

But Bavuma continued to battle, notching a 140-ball fifty, before he and Jansen provided the perfect counter-punch in a 132-run partnership for the seventh wicket, one which was only bettered by the 183 put with Harmer - a new South African record stand for the eighth wicket.

Scott Boland (5-81), who had torn through the Proteas' top order over the first two days, secured a well-deserved five-for with the dismissal of Jansen, while Harmer and Bavuma's resistance was finally broken with back-to-back deliveries to trigger a declaration on 425-9.

Marnus Labuschagne first bowled Harmer, before Starc was the one to finally draw an error from Bavuma as he nicked off for 179.

Rabada added to Australia's woes with his early dismissal of Maddison, though he was restricted to just the one over as the deteriorating light resulted in three subsequent overs of spin prior to stumps.

Former Australia batter David Warner has hit out at the "pathetic" attendances in the ongoing Test series in South Africa.

South Africa lost the first Test match by 214 runs in Durban, with large sections of the Kingsmead ground empty, and the crowds haven't really picked up through the first two rain-affected days of the second Test in Gqeberha.

Sports.title: PSG v Barcelona, Manchester City v AEK Athens, and more: Champions League – live
Sports.content:
Hello world! Another busy night lies ahead in Europe and in the English Football League, with much attention destined to be focused on Paris, scene in recent days of violence and looting but host tonight of one of the prestige fixtures of the group stage as the teams sitting first and second in the nascent table after two fixtures, five-time champions Barcelona and double reigning champions Paris Saint Germain, meet at the Parc des Princes.

Manchester City, meanwhile, may be without Erling Haaland for the visit of AEK Athens, who are promising not to go all-out defensive for a trip to a side Marko Nikolic, the Greek side’s Serbian coach, described as “one of the best teams in the world of football”. “We must bring our identity, not change much and be strong on the pitch,” he said. “If you change and go defensive and try only to survive, it will not work. We have to stick to the challenge. We want to do it with our game. We can be a decent opponent for everybody. I have a lot of confidence in our team.” You can get a decent idea of how much any kind of good result would mean to AEK by the scenes of jubilatory bedlam that greeted yesterday’s 1-1 draw in the Uefa Youth League.

View image in fullscreen Players of AEK Athens celebrate securing a draw against Manchester City in the Uefa Youth League. Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty Images

Beyond the best two teams in the tournament so far tonight also sees the worst, in the shape of Slovan Bratislava, who visit Roma. Slovan, who last failed to win the Slovakian title in 2018, are currently fourth in their domestic league but their position at the bottom of this table is largely down to them having had the misfortune to come up against PSG, who thumped them 6-1, a goal difference hit from which they are yet to recover.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany may miss Bayern’s clash with Arsenal due to legs-affecting virus
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany is touch and go to be in the Bayern Munich dugout against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday night as he battles a debilitating virus that has affected his legs. Kompany was unable to attend his team’s training session on Tuesday before the Champions League tie, ceding the responsibility for the pre-match press conference to his assistant, Aaron Danks.

Kompany has been told to rest after he struggled through Bayern’s 6-1 home win over RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga on Saturday, after which the club’s sporting director, Max Eberl, addressed the media instead of him. There have been reports in Germany that Kompany needed to lie down on his sofa at home after the Leipzig game and that the viral infection had affected an existing hip problem which meant he could hardly walk.

“It has affected his legs at times,” Danks confirmed. “He’s felt some pain in his legs. I’m not sure about the reports about him lying down on the couch. I think we can all have a lie down on the couch after a game. It’s just a virus. The doctors and experts know way more than I do. The most important thing we have encouraged is that he rests; he takes the time he needs – however long that may be.

“Unfortunately, I can’t give you any more – whether that’s tomorrow or whether that’s two or three days’ time. I don’t know. We just take it day-by-day and see how he is. Getting Vince to rest is a challenge. You know him as a person. He’s a real leader. He works hard.”

Danks will take the team against Arsenal if Kompany cannot make it, just as he did last season during the epic Champions League semi-final, first-leg against Paris Saint-Germain when Kompany was suspended. PSG won 5-4 at the Parc des Princes that night before progressing 6-5 on aggregate. They beat Arsenal in the final on penalties.

Birmingham-born Danks, who briefly took caretaker charge of Aston Villa in 2022 and has coached at various clubs including Anderlecht and Middlesbrough, said he would be in communication with Kompany “in some shape or form” if the manager was not able to come to the stadium.

Sports.title: How Brazil’s election result could shape women’s football in the country
Sports.content:
The day before the first round of Brazilian elections, the Estádio do Morumbi hosted the second leg of the Brazilian Women’s Championship final, in which São Paulo drew 1-1 with Corinthians to win 3-2 on aggregate and secure the Brasileirão Women’s title.

It had been an incredible final but after the game the goalkeeper Carlinha used an interview to appeal to her fans: “Never again Bolsonaro in power,” she shouted to a record-breaking TV audience of 23 million people.

Having lost her grandmother during the Covid-19 pandemic, Carlinha recalls the challenges faced by hundreds of thousands of Brazilian families when the far-right president Jair Bolsonaro spread fake information about the virus while ignoring public appeals for the government to buy and distribute vaccinations. More than 700,000 Brazilians died during the pandemic. Now his son, Flávio, is standing against the 80-year-old incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

“I didn’t just think of [my grandmother] when I gave that interview, I think about her and miss her every single day,” Carlinha tells Moving the Goalposts. “I felt relieved after talking about my personal opinion in such an important moment of Brazilian democracy. I’m a journalism student and I know the impact if the right wins the elections.”

Carlinha is one of several female football players who have used social media and their visibility to speak up before and during the presidential election, which will come to an end on Sunday with a second-round vote. The father of the Bolsonaro dynasty is currently under “humanitarian house arrest”, serving a 27-year sentence for a coup attempt.

Carlinha’s club and international teammate, Tayla Carolina, went viral the weekend after discussing her family’s background and how public policies implemented during Lula’s government were important for her mother and grandmother, who have worked as cleaners throughout their lives and have since passed. “I’m from a very humble family, I’m a Black woman. I’ve studied in public schools and used the national healthcare system … my mum, dona Dora, worked for over a decade for someone who never paid her labour rights … and she worked until she couldn’t walk any more due to the cancer that took her from us. She never saw me play because she never had the time, she never rested,” she wrote. Her story resonates with many Brazilians who fought for shorter working weeks, approved earlier this week in congress.

View image in fullscreen The Brazil international Tayla Carolina has expressed her support for Lula’s policies. Photograph: Aude Alcover/Icon Sport/Getty Images

Tayla elaborates her point: “I’m from a country where most of the people are poor but the country is not seen as poor. It shows there are huge inequalities, which come from exploitation. Years have passed and there’s still a lot of inequality and I come from it … as a public figure, and someone who has lived similar lives to the majority of Brazilians, I feel the responsibility to speak up.”

The player organisation Fifpro has just released a new study showing that nearly half of female football players think of early retirement owing to the psychological and financial pressures of the women’s game (800 professional players took part). With the Women’s World Cup being staged in Brazil next year both Carlinha and Tayla feel the election will have a huge impact on the game going forward.

“There is one side that makes it quite clear how they feel about women’s rights,” says Carlinha, referring to, among other things, politicians such as Eduarda Campopiano, one of the most voted members of the São Paulo Assembly, who calls herself an “enemy of feminists” and has said she does not believe in femicide – that women and girls can be killed because they are women. Tayla also feels the need for policies to support the women’s game at a crucial moment. “We still need government incentives, so it may not be immediate, but the game will be affected, positively or negatively, depending on how the elections go.”

Lula approved the World Cup law in June 2026, which regulates many aspects of the tournament, including how ministries, the Brazilian FA (CBF), state federations and clubs will commit to developing a legacy and supporting the women’s game in the country. The legacy plan, divided into four strands, proposes supporting access and permanence of girls and women in football, developing and professionalising the game, fighting gender- and racial-based discrimination, and enhancing the economic and cultural aspects of women’s football in Brazil. The commitment to the tournament is stated in Lula’s government plan. Bolsonaro’s proposals for women’s sport do not mention the World Cup; instead, he proposes “ensuring that women’s categories, from youth to elite, are played by athletes of the female sex, protecting women and tournaments from ideological agendas”.

Brazilian football, men’s and women’s, has been heavily politicised for decades, and the rise of social media has led to an increase in players publicly supporting their political candidates. In the men’s game, the far right is often championed by the Santos and Brazil forward Neymar, who has showed support for the Bolsonaro family on many occasions. Tottenham’s Richarlison, meanwhile, is positioned on the left and this week accused Flávio Bolsonaro of “taking possession” of an island he says he bought a few years back.

The country’s female players do not have the same number of followers on social media and cannot influence a big audience in the same way as the men. However, it is true that the result of the election is likely to have more of an impact on the women’s game than on the men’s.

View image in fullscreen Brazilian students and activists march in downtown Rio de Janeiro to support Lula and protest against the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro. Photograph: Ellan Lustosa/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

Kely Nascimento, the daughter of late football legend Pelé and founder and executive director of the Nascimento Foundation, says: “Female players, female athletes, they don’t have the protection of wealth. What feeds the brilliance of Brazilian football are the players, and they mostly come from communities, favelas and other places that are going to be hugely affected by these elections. Women are more affected by all this, right?”

Carlinha, who played in one of the two recent friendlies against Argentina, says playing for the national team at home is “one of the best feelings ever”. At both stadiums, in Porto Alegre and Recife, the crowd predominantly chanted in support of Lula, which could be heard over the TV commentary during the broadcast.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The politicisation of women’s football is not new, as Brazilian women’s football historian and author Aira Bonfim explains. “This is a hundred-year-old history, because we have episodes of women playing football in Brazil since 1915, and the women’s game reveals different perspectives of gender inequalities, racial inequalities, class, territory, which will affect the progress of the women’s game,” she says. “By knowing women’s football history, we can look at episodes which are equally as political, such as the ban on the women’s game [between 1941 and 1979], the persecution of women, and lies that were told so that female players would give up on it.”

One of the pieces of history that she has uncovered in her research became a short film, which debuted earlier this month at the Rio Film Festival, The House of Dona Carlota, produced by Mymama Entertainment and directed by Lili Fialho and Bruna Linzmeyer, which tells the story of a woman who was arrested and persecuted because she led a women’s football team, Primavera Atlético Clube.

It shows women’s football as a space of socialisation, sport and resistance to the Estado Novo dictatorship in the late 1930s and early 1940s. The women’s game was banned in Brazil for decades, and the World Cup in 2027 is where many hope its renewed development will be consolidated.

“What’s at risk [in this election] is a waste of all of the human investments in building social legacy plans. There is also the risk of dismantling all political communication that has been done to support [the World Cup] through the ministries, cities and state governments. If you elect someone who did not make any commitments towards it, who did not commit to the World Cup or what it represents to women, it can be a huge loss,” Bonfim says. “Just the fact that during Jair Bolsonaro’s government he removed the status of the ministry of sports reveals how he feels about the sector.”

The hosting of a Women’s World Cup is key in developing public policies and attracting investment and support. As Nascimento says: “There are girls all over Brazil for whom football is not just their dream, but it’s also how they get out of very awful situations. And there are amazing people doing God’s work all over Brazil just to get girls to play, to be educated in another way … for some reason, Brazil just makes football magic, and that’s not gender-specific. And there’s an enormous Brazil that is being ignored and taken advantage of.”

There are many reasons for the international community to look closer at the second round of Brazil’s elections on Sunday, from how it can affect climate change, foreign policy and financial markets to many other issues. Women’s football, and all it represents, is one of them.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Kulusevski and Maddison return to form but are Tottenham also back?
Sports.content:
MAD FOR IT

As Tottenham edged to victory over Coventry, a familiar face among the post-match salutations. Could that be Dejan Kulusevski? For it was he, playing 526 days since his last Spurs appearance. Much has changed though still much stays the same. Ben Davies’s deflected late clincher catapulted Spurs up to … 16th. When Kulusevski last played on 11 May 2025, Tottenham were 17th, the position in which they finished both that season and in 2025-26.

So what has changed? Ange Postecoglou was tinned that summer despite winning the Flamin’ Bigger Vase. Thomas Frank was an appointment the soccer sensibles agreed was smart. A coach with impeccable credentials in improving players, willing to work in tandem with club suits, an ideal apex for an org chart. With lovely hair, too. Frank was sent packing in February, his popularity ratings plunging to depths unseen since Alan Sugar had the bright idea of appointing George Graham, who had paid his gardener to shape his lawn into the Arsenal crest. In football’s world of irrelevant but interesting (you sure? – Football Daily Ed) coincidences, the last time Spurs beat Coventry in the league, when Sergiy Rebrov’s goal completed a 3-0 stroll in 2001, the manager’s programme notes had been written by Gorgeous George, who the day previously had been the recipient of Sugar’s “you’re fired” flex.

Igor Tudor’s tenure resembled a slasher movie, an appointment on the nod from a sporting director, Fabio Paratici, who had already left. Classic Spurs. What could possibly go wrong? Everything, it turns out. Or close to, until Roberto De Zerbi was handed the keys and a control none of his predecessors commanded. The transfer spend has been heavy, and when Kulusevski arrived in the 87th minute on Monday, the game not yet won, he did so following an absence where Spurs signed 20 players either permanently or on loan, at a cost of £530m.



Scoring Spurs’ opening goal on Monday was James Maddison. Football’s king of the oche was absent for almost as long Kulusevski. Last season, as De Zerbi attempted to arrest the slide towards relegation, ‘Madders’ initially sat on the bench on a vibes-only basis and closed out the season with not much more than 30 minutes of play, and had little time to do Maddison things like his arcing beauty against his hometown club on Monday, which opened the scoring for Spurs.

Good feelings at last, following a sunshine break in Marbella where, according to De Zerbi, his players became less a squad than a family. “You have to play for your friend and your brother, not like 11 robot players on the pitch,” he cooed. With two of his stars back in tandem, De Zerbi’s enforcer intensity brought a first league win of the season, to help Tottenham off the bottom. “With them in the dressing room there is another atmosphere,” De Zerbi roared. Jam tomorrow? Glory, glory? Lads, it’s etc …

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Scott Murray from 8pm BST for Liverpool 2-1 Villarreal in the Bigger Cup action while Simon Burnton is on clockwatch action to bring you updates from PSG 3-3 Barcelona, Manchester City 4-1 AEK Athens, and more.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“People still call me a ‘party boy’. That stigma has been overused and has followed me since I retired from football. I’m not saying I didn’t enjoy myself as a player. You never hear that I didn’t turn up for training or wasn’t fit … now I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time. I’m a manager” – Dwight Yorke speaks to Morgan Ofori from his home in Dubai about his career ambitions, having been linked with the vacant Ghana job.

Sports.title: Animal rights group urges Crystal Palace to retire bald eagle mascot
Sports.content:
A leading animal rights group has urged Crystal Palace to retire their American bald eagle mascot because, it says, the matchday experience can leave the bird “frightened, disoriented and panicked” and put spectators at risk.

In a letter to Palace’s chief executive, Sharon Lacey, People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) called on the club to end Phoenix’s appearances at Selhurst Park and commit never to use a live animal mascot again.

Palace, known as the Eagles since 1973 after the then manager Malcolm Allison changed their nickname from the Glaziers, introduced a pre-match display from Kayla the Eagle in 2010. She died in 2020 after a decade’s service but Kayla’s replacement, Phoenix, made her debut before the game against West Ham in August 2024 at four months old, meeting supporters in the fanzone and being introduced at half-time with her handler.

Phoenix is based at the Eagle Heights Wildlife Foundation in Kent, and its website said at the time that she “had been carefully prepared for her prestigious role as Crystal Palace’s official live mascot since hatching”. Phoenix is not at every game but it is understood plans for her to make a maiden flight across the pitch before kick-off – a ritual Kayla for which was renowned – were abandoned at a match this season.

In the letter seen by the Guardian, Peta said bright lights, loud noises and boisterous crowds mean stadiums are “no place for animals” and potentially put animals and spectators at risk. It detailed incidents of eagles that have collided with walls or glass windows and a falcon that landed on a spectator’s head, embedding its talons in the man’s scalp. Peta also referred to an incident involving Kayla in 2015 when a Charlton fan was found guilty of trying to punch her during a League Cup tie marred by crowd trouble.

View image in fullscreen Kayla the eagle, who died in 2020, in flight before a Crystal Palace game in 2014. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Dr Carys Bennett, Peta’s senior corporate projects manager, said: “Bald eagles are revered as symbols of freedom, yet Phoenix is being used as little more than a prop to entertain football fans. Crystal Palace already has a human mascot to energise supporters, so there’s no reason to drag a wild animal into a noisy, crowded stadium. Peta is urging the club to let Phoenix spread [her] wings and retire from matchday duties for good.”

Palace did not respond to Peta’s letter or to a follow-up request last week. They have been contacted for comment. The Guardian sent a number of questions to Eagles Heights to ask about Phoenix’s welfare and did not receive a reply.

Peta’s letter argued that eagles’ natural behaviours make the stadium environment unsuitable for them. In the wild, the birds can travel across vast territories and typically avoid close contact with humans. The organisation said even birds raised in captivity retain their natural instincts and may experience frustration and stress when unable to engage in natural behaviours.

Benfica’s home matches feature appearances from a bald eagle called Águia Vitória – a custom that the Portuguese club started in 2003 when their new Estádio da Luz opened.

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag accuses Cristiano Ronaldo of ‘letting down’ Manchester United
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo “let the team down” during their time together at Manchester United. Ten Hag has also alleged that promises made by United’s owners went unfulfilled, leading to his sacking by the club in October 2024.

Ronaldo returned for a second spell at United in August 2021 and was already at the club when Ten Hag was appointed in April 2022 as Ole Gunnar Solskjær’s successor. The relationship between the pair quickly broke down, however, with Ronaldo refusing to come on as a substitute in a win against Tottenham in October 2022 before he then publicly criticised the club in a TV interview. The forward’s contract was mutually terminated the following month.

“He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” Ten Hag said in an interview with the Athletic. “He’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in.”

Ten Hag claims Ronaldo did not complete the full run that players were set after they were beaten 4-0 by Brentford early in his reign. “I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say: ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score.’”

Ten Hag was sacked only five months after he won the FA Cup and then signed a contract extension. The Dutchman claimed in the discussions with the club’s owners about his new deal that he was made promises which were not kept, and he was left “embarrassed” when Scott McTominay was sold to Napoli without his consent. He said: “They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.

“I said: ‘No selling Scott McTominay.’ And in the end they sold him. I got, of course, very embarrassed and disappointed.”

Sports.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
Sports.content:
Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.”

The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media.

He is tired of the shorthand way he is described during these high‑profile job hunts. People focus on his playing accolades, including calling him the treble winner, a label he says belongs to one season in a run of three Premier League titles at Manchester United from 1999-2001. “I’m a manager,” he says.

Over the past four years, Yorke has quietly built a coaching résumé far removed from Old Trafford. His first taste of management came in May 2022, taking charge of Australia’s A-League All Stars against Barcelona in front of more than 70,000 people in Sydney. They lost 3-2. “I realised then that I enjoyed it,” he says.

Macarthur, based in Sydney, followed that July. “We went to a relatively unknown team in the A‑League and managed to win the cup.” The Australia Cup success, three months into his spell, was the club’s first trophy.

It did not last. Macarthur sacked him in January 2023, with the club sixth, after a post-match address when he reportedly called the club a “pub team” run by “muppets”.

A Fifa chamber found Macarthur had dismissed him without just cause. The court of arbitration for sport upheld that in 2024 and ordered the club to pay AU$212,500 (£111,300 at current exchange rates).

“I wish I’d had the opportunity to finish what I started,” Yorke says. The job taught him communication and the importance of being transparent. “There was a disagreement. It was resolved amicably and I’ve moved on.”

Between Macarthur and his next role, he kept his hand in. He worked as a pundit for beIN Sports and on the Saudi Pro League and travelled the world watching coaches at work.

In November 2024, Trinidad and Tobago came calling. The Soca Warriors finished third in their World Cup qualifying group behind Curaçao and Jamaica, missing out on the finals tournament, and Yorke’s tenure ended soon after. The Trinidad and Tobago Football Association said talks over revised terms had not produced an agreement and the contract was ended by mutual consent, announced in March. “The decision to end things was out of my control,” Yorke says.

View image in fullscreen Dwight Yorke smiles on the sidelines as he leads the A-League All Stars to a narrow friendly defeat by Barcelona in May 2022, his first taste of management. Photograph: Rick Rycroft/AP

He does not accept that missing the World Cup defines his time in charge. “People can be blind to success because they focus on whether you qualified.”

He lost once in six qualifiers, 2-0 in Jamaica in September 2025. He had been handed a brief: make people care about Trinidad and Tobago again, boost recruitment and qualify. “I was given three tasks and completed two,” he says.

With Yorke as the head coach, crowds came back and a number of US-born players with Trinidadian and Tobagonian heritage, such as the CF Montréal winger Dante Sealy and Real Salt Lake’s Kobi Henry, opted in and made their debuts. Yorke gave a new generation a fighting chance to emulate the team he captained to the finals in 2006. “I left Trinidadian football in a far better place than I found it,” he says.

The TTFA president at the time described Yorke’s mandate as qualification alone. The team were ranked 102nd by Fifa when Yorke was hired, behind Curaçao (91st) and Jamaica (62nd). “I miss management,” Yorke says. “I miss what we were creating.”

View image in fullscreen Dwight Yorke says he tends to fast for nearly 20 hours a day and eats one meal: ‘I’m a fitness fanatic who trains every day.’ Photograph: Christopher Pike/The Guardian

The players are understood to want him back because his successor, Derek King, is struggling with two draws and eight defeats from his 10 games. Ghana, though, is the live opportunity. “It’s a job I’d be interested in, given Ghana’s history and the players available.”

The Ghanaian FA has not confirmed any approach. The team are bottom of their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying group with no points, after a 2-0 defeat in Côte d’Ivoire and a 4-2 home loss against the Gambia in which they led by two goals. It is a sharp decline for a side that reached the last 32 of the World Cup this summer, losing 1-0 against Colombia.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“You look at the squad and your eyes open even wider,” Yorke says. He says an agent called to tell him Ghana were interested. “The conversation started there and then reached the media before I really knew it.”

From the outside, he says, Ghana “sometimes looks disjointed”. The GFA has said its women’s head coach, Kim Björkegren, will take temporary charge of the men’s qualifying double-header against Somalia next month. In Yorke’s view, outside noise unbalances things, from the administration to the players. So how would he fix it? Organisation, transparency and everyone speaking the same language. “The talent is there. Build the culture and get the players to buy in and the football will follow.”

double quotation mark Pep said that I can’t be him or any other manager – I have to be myself Dwight Yorke

He has considered the effect that diaspora players could have in the role, pointing to Ghana’s Antoine Semenyo and Brandon Thomas-Asante as proof that countries can benefit immensely from UK-born talent. It reflects a broader trend: at the World Cup, 23.6% of the 1,248 squad players represented countries outside their place of birth. For Yorke, the approach is simple: identify the players, establish their heritage and quality and sell them a vision. “I’d make sure that what I say is what I do.”

Older managers might have screamed and shouted to get messages across, but he says: “I’m not sure that approach can last in the current environment.” He would not berate a player in public. “That can be done behind closed doors, while still being assertive.” Respect and punctuality are non‑negotiable. He has sat in dressing rooms with big egos and says nobody gets special treatment. “Everyone starts equally.”

He borrows, but he does not copy. Sir Alex Ferguson, who managed him at United, is the shadow over any such comparison. Among contemporary managers, Pep Guardiola offered him the best advice. “He said, in effect, that I can’t be him or any other manager. I have to be myself.”

View image in fullscreen Dwight Yorke fends off Dominic Matteo in Manchester United’s FA Cup fourth-round win against Liverpool in January 1999. Photograph: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto Ltd

Other labels have stuck anyway. “People still call me a ‘party boy’. That stigma has been overused and has followed me since I retired from football. I’m not saying I didn’t enjoy myself as a player.” But he says: “You never hear that I didn’t turn up for training or wasn’t fit.”

In Dubai, he tends to fast for nearly 20 hours a day and eats one meal. “I’m a fitness fanatic who trains every day.”

Ask Yorke how he wants to be remembered as a coach and he sits up and answers with a list. Committed. Transparent with players. Decisions made for the team, never for an individual. “I’m straightforward. I don’t mess around, take shortcuts or do the job halfway.”

Yorke has the interest and, by his own account, the answers. “If anyone doubts me, I can prove them wrong.”

Sports.title: Barcelona forced to wear old kit in bizarre change for Champions League showdown
Sports.content:
Barcelona forced to wear old kit in bizarre change for Champions League showdown

Barcelona will wear their 2025/26 season third kit against Paris Saint-Germain due to a colour clash.

The European heavyweights meet in the French capital on Tuesday night for a huge Champions League tie, live on talkSPORT 2.



2 Barcelona will reuse their third kit from last season against PSG tonight in a late change of attire Credit: Getty

Barca famously wear a blue and dark red colour combination on their home strip.

This season's away shirt is purple and black, whilst the third kit mixes two shades of blue.

However, Barcelona will recall their orange third kit from last season when they take on PSG at the Parc des Princes.



Why are Barcelona wearing an old kit?

The decision was confirmed by Barca under two hours before kick off.

It's thought that none of their 2026/27 kits have been deemed to be wearable for the match by UEFA.

They teased the kit they will wear via social media earlier on Tuesday as Lamine Yamal, Anthony Gordon and Pedri posed in the attire.



The changed has been made due to the television broadcasting criteria, with both clubs' kits needing to be distinguishable.

Barca's latest kits are adjudged to be too similar to PSG's home shirt, and so they have made a last-minute change.



However, they trained in blue during the lead-up to the Champions League blockbuster.

Kick-off is still going ahead despite the recent riots in Paris and other areas in France.

2 None of Barcelona's current kits are allowed to be worn in the match due to broadcasting rules Credit: Getty

Over 2,400 arrests have been made as protesters clashed with police.

The cost of living, rising oil prices and declining public services are the cause of the protests.



Some cities across France were issued curfews on Monday night, but the PSG v Barca match is unlikely to be affected.

This is a developing story and is being updated.

Sports.title: Dele Alli offered shock return at EFL club as star goes a year out of football
Sports.content:
Dele Alli offered shock return at EFL club as star goes a year out of football

Dele Alli's former boss Karl Robinson has revealed he offered the midfielder a route back into football at Salford City this summer.

Ex-Tottenham star Alli has now been without a club since September 2025 after having his contract terminated at Como.

5 Alli was last on the books at Como - featuring just once for the Italian outfit Credit: Getty

Once regarded among the best young midfielders in the world, the 30-year-old has been targeting a return to the game this summer.

He was first linked with a move to Barnet after using the League Two side's training facilities, but a deal never materialised, and was later pictured training with semi-professional side Windsor & Eton.

However, Alli currently remains without a club, having last played a competitive game in March 2025 - when he was sent off just nine minutes into his Como debut.

It's a far cry from the ex-England star's glory days at Tottenham, where he won PFA Young Player of the Year award twice.

Alli turned down football return

While finding a club has proved challenging for Alli, his first ever manager has revealed he previously offered him a chance at Salford.

Ex-MK Dons boss Robinson gave Alli his senior debut as a 16-year-old at Stadium MK, before overseeing his development that eventually earned him a move to Tottenham in 2015.

Until earlier this summer, Robinson was in charge of League Two outfit Salford, where he looked to reunite with his former protégé.

Speaking to Boyle Sports and Footy Accumulators’ podcast No Tippy Tappy Football, he shared: “If a job comes up, Dele Alli is always more than welcome to come anywhere I go, if he wants to.

“All I can say is that I hope he’s well, I hope he’s healthy, and I hope he’s in a good place.

“If he ticks all those boxes, I don’t care about whether he’s a footballer. I worry about Dele as a young man – he is someone that I will always be there to pick up the phone to.

5 Alli scored 24 goals in 88 games for MK Dons - all of them coming under Robinson Credit: Getty

5 Robinson was sacked by Salford in June after two seasons in charge Credit: Getty

“I would 100 per cent give him a chance.

"I saw him in the gym in June, and I told him to come to Salford. But he probably looked at me and went, ‘gaffer, come on, I’m not doing that.”

While Robinson's sacking by Salford this summer now rules out a straightforward move for Alli, he will surely be keeping an eye out on wherever his old boss goes next.

But the 46-year-old coach also claimed that the midfielder will still have the self belief that he can play at the highest level.

Naming Manchester United as an example - who are currently struggling under Michael Carrick - Robinson insisted Alli would back himself to transform the club's fortunes.

He continued: “The reason these players are these players is because they have a self-belief and a poorly-developed sense of fear.

5 Alli was one of the Premier League's star players during his time at Tottenham Credit: Getty

“I guarantee if you sit down now, he would probably say he could turn around the fortunes of Man United.

“Because that’s how those real top players who produce their moments of magic think.”

Given Alli's rapid rise in his early career, it isn't hard to see why he would still believe in his ability to make an impact at the highest level.

He previously starred in a Spurs side that reached the 2019 Champions League final and recorded a second place Premier League finish in 2017, scoring 67 goals in 269 games for the club.

The two-time PFA Young Player of the Year was also part of England's run to the 2018 World Cup semi-finals, but things later started to unravel.

After leaving Spurs in 2022, a rapid decline followed with Alli enduring failed stints at Everton, Besiktas and Como.

5 Alli has not played in the Premier League since 2023 - during his spell at Everton when he played just 13 times Credit: Getty

In 2023, Alli opened up on the mental health struggles and childhood trauma which halted his progress, while injuries have also played a part.

Robinson discussed his recent struggles, admitting that despite this, Alli's undeniable talent should have seem him find a club by now,

He said: “When this boy left MK Dons at 18 to go to Spurs, he was getting compared to Lionel Messi, David Beckham, Zinedine Zidane, James Rodriguez.

"To see his rise with the national team and with Spurs, and looking to where he is now – and I hope he listens to this – I don’t know why he’s not playing football.

"He is a tremendous young man who has come through a lot of situations that he’s struggled through, but he’s risen above it to become the person he is.”

Sports.title: Former Man United star released on free transfer would be their best defender right now – ‘A revelation’
Sports.content:
Former Man United star released on free transfer would be their best defender right now – ‘A revelation’

Gabby Agbonlahor believes that Victor Lindelof would be Manchester United's best defender if he was still at the club.

The Sweden international is into his second season at Aston Villa after joining the club for free in the summer of 2025 and has gone on to become a key player for Unai Emery.

4 Man United have problems in various areas of the pitch, while Lindelof is a key player these days Credit: Getty

He started the Europa League final in midfield as Villa beat Freiburg 3-0 to secure a place in the Champions League and claim a trophy.

Lindelof has played every minute of every match this season, bar Villa's victory over Coventry in the Carabao Cup, where he was left on the bench.

And with his contract set to expire next summer, reports suggest he will be offered a new deal after impressing so much.

And Agbonlahor was full of praise for Lindelof, telling Jeff Stelling on talkSPORT Breakfast: "There is one defender who Aston Villa have got who would be Manchester United's best defender right now, and that is Victor Lindelof. He has been a revelation.

"He's been a great pro as well, last season, he wasn't getting as many starts because Ezri Konsa was there.

"But he was fantastic, and I think Taylor Harwood-Bellis has got a long way to get Lindelof out of the side.

"He would be Manchester United's best defender now."

Lindelof's resurgence

Speaking about Lindelof last season, Emery praised his leadership and experience.

He said: “He has experience and he is a very good professional. He has qualities too. He is still being young to play football.

“We signed him in the last moments of the transfer window, because when we identified that possibility, I wanted in that moment everything that he did last week [vs West Ham].

4 Lindelof spent eight years at Man United Credit: Getty

4 Man United are shot of defensive options at the moment with injuries and suspensions causing all sorts of problems Credit: Getty

“In 90 minutes he did everything I expected from him. He was really fantastic.

“Every day it is easy how we are working because his adaptation is so quick, and everything we need, through his experiences, he can give us.

“He gave us experience before, but maybe the best moment he had until now with us was the match at West Ham. He played a fantastic match.

“Now, he has shown us his level. He can’t stop now, and he must keep it! He is very mature, of course. This is very important.

“He is responsible too, and he has experiences, and hopefully he can help us a lot for the rest of the season.”

From that moment on, he hasn't looked back, and he looks to be thriving away from the pressure cooker that is Man United.

4 Lindelof always put everything he had on the line for Man United Credit: Getty

Lindelof's Man United departure

The centre-back joined Man United in the summer of 2017 from Benfica.

At the time, he was considered one of the best young defenders around, and he joined while Jose Mourinho was manager.

However, he never quite lived up to the expectations, but he still managed 284 appearances and penned a heartfelt goodbye when he departed.

He said: "It's been a lot of ups and downs.

"But I mean, for me to be able to represent this club for eight years, it's been an honour and a privilege, and a dream come true.

"I've had so many good memories here. Just looking at the Stretford End here, I mean, I'm going to miss it a lot.

"They're [the fans] with us through absolutely everything, and it doesn't matter the result, every single week, they come here and they support us and they sing their souls out.

"I just want to say thank you so much for taking me in."

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel’s long-time assistant Anthony Barry could land Premier League job
Sports.content:
Anthony Barry could become a managerial target for Premier League clubs in a potential blow to the England national team.

Barry has worked as assistant to the Three Lions head coach Thomas Tuchel since January 2021 when the latter joined Chelsea.

2 Barry is a key member of the England coaching team, but could soon become a candidate for a Premier League job Credit: Getty

He followed the German to Bayern Munich in April 2023 and was then announced as part of the England coaching staff 18 months later.

The 40-year-old former midfielder has also worked in the Republic of Ireland and Belgium coaching teams.

Barry extended his England deal through to Euro 2028 with Tuchel in February after a successful 2026 World Cup qualification run.

However, as reported by The Sun, Tuchel's right-hand man is keen on managing in the Premier League.

He is also likely to be in contention for a top flight job as a number of clubs already face questions over their incumbents.

Which Premier League managers face the sack?

As talkSPORT reported on Sunday, Pierre Sage is fighting to save his job at Crystal Palace just four months after moving to Selhurst Park.

Palace were thumped 5-0 by rivals Brighton on Sunday and sit above the Premier League relegation zone by just one point.

Alvaro Arbeloa has been under intense pressure at Fulham as they went winless in their opening six matches of the season.

They beat Hull City 1-0 at the weekend, but still find themselves in the bottom three.

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner has had his future questioned, whilst Matthias Jaissle is struggling at Newcastle.

2 Barry is a trusted aide for Tuchel and has plenty of experience in coaching at international and club level Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, Michael Carrick remains under the microscope at Manchester United having gone winless in their past six matches.

However, if a managerial change was to be made at Old Trafford, the club would likely go for an experienced replacement.

Antonio Conte is understood to be interested in succeeding Carrick if need be, having left Napoli in the summer.

The Italian won the 2016/17 Premier League title at Chelsea but may be an option for his former club Juventus in Turin, where he lives.

Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler is admired by the United board, and former Germany boss Julian Nagelsmann is also an option.

Sports.title: Harry Kane and Michael Olise decisions mean Liverpool star would get games at Bayern Munich amid surprise transfer rumour
Sports.content:
Harry Kane and Michael Olise decisions mean Liverpool star would get games at Bayern Munich amid surprise transfer rumour

Bayern Munich could easily 'find a place' to fit Rio Ngumoha in - he wouldn't play second fiddle.

That's according to European football broadcaster Andy Brassell, who has commented on the 18-year-old's situation at Liverpool with his contract to expire in 2029.

3 Ngumoha has already won three caps for England at 18 Credit: Getty

Despite the Reds' desire keep the talented teenager in Merseyside, a new deal for Ngumoha does not necessarily mean it's a forgone conclusion he will stay at the club.

Arsenal have been linked with a move for Ngumoha in recent weeks, while Bayern were reported to have targeted the winger in the summer.

Bayern's interest reportedly went as far as manager Vincent Kompany holding productive discussions with Ngumoha's representatives, only for Liverpool to slam the door shut on any prospective deal.

But the Bavarians could come knocking for Ngumoha once again, especially if contract negotiations reach an impasse.

Of course, there's every chance Bayern's name is being used as leverage by Ngumoha's representatives to negotiate a better contract.

After all, they've already been burned in the past by Florian Wirtz and Nick Woltemade, who both appeared destined to join Bayern, but ended up at Liverpool and Newcastle respectively.

How Harry Kane and Michael Olise could help pave the way for Rio Ngumoha at Bayern

Yet Bayern's need to bring in fresh talent on the wing coupled with a string of intriguing moves both within and outside of the club could pave the way for Ngumoha to join.

One of those would be Harry Kane, who is poised to sign an extension with Bayern.

"If you told me he'd (Kane) end up in midfield in a couple of seasons for Bayern, I think I'd probably believe you. I can definitely see that happening," Brassell told talkSPORT.com.

"Kane's passing range is just ridiculous, he's not just restricted to dropping 20, 30 yards off and making passes, he is genuinely someone with the passing range, the technical capability and the positional sense to be a midfielder.

3 Kane already has 15 goal contributions in just ten games for Bayern this term Credit: Getty

"Luis Diaz is knocking 30, Serge Gnabry, they're not going to persevere with him forever.

"Then there's a question over Michael Olise, the fact is, he is someone I don't think is a Bayern lifer.

"I think he'll go to Real Madrid at some point and then probably from there, find a way back to the Premier League at some point, but I think Real Madrid in the medium-term seems quite likely, maybe even at the end of this season.

"Then you factor in questions over Jamal Musiala's health and fitness."

Would Rio Ngumoha instantly go into Bayern's starting line-up?

All of those elements have Brassell adamant Ngumoha would not be stuck in a 'massive queue' to break into Bayern's line-up.

"Obviously, the talent is there and they're absolutely right to be interested in him," Brassell said.

3 Ngumoha has revealed his representatives are in talks with Liverpool over a new contract Credit: Getty

"I don't think it is a case of stockpiling players, even though we associated Bayern with star wingers.

"I think they will find a place for him, without too much of a problem, to play plenty of games."

Sports.title: Ousmane Dembele gone and Pau Cubarsí replaced in combined PSG and Barcelona XI
Sports.content:
The Champions League's two favourites will go head-to-head in a clash for the ages on Tuesday evening.

The competition's reigning champions will host European football's highest scorers this season in a blockbuster meeting in Paris.



8 PSG have won their last two games against Barcelona, and could join Bayern Munich as the only other team to do so three straight times in the Champions League Credit: Getty

Both teams boast a perfect winning record in the league phase thus far after two rounds of matches.

PSG have swept aside Slovan Bratislava and Manchester City, while Hansi Flick's Barca have downed Galatasaray and Feyenoord.

With such star power set to be on show at the Parc des Princes, picking a combined XI between the two teams is nearly impossible.



However, European football expert Andy Brassell has settled some of the sport's biggest debates when selecting his ideal team.

Who makes the combined XI?

"Joan García [in goal], it has to be," Brassell explained during an exclusive interview with talkSPORT.com. "And obviously the debate is always in England: why isn't David Raya in the Spain team?



"And it's almost a rerun of when David de Gea wasn't in the Spain team when he was at Manchester United, and he was probably the best goalkeeper in the Premier League at the time.

"But I think there's an argument that even if you take Unai Simón out of the picture, which, by the way, head coach Luis De La Fuente is not doing because he really trusts him, then I think Joan García has got an excellent shout. He's younger than both of them.



"He's Barcelona's keeper. He's been brilliant since minute one when he arrived. Great with feet, real presence in between the sticks as well."

The two full-backs almost choose themselves, with PSG pair Achraf Hakimi and Nuno Mendes both certainties.

8 Hakimi, bottom row second from left and Mendes, top row third from left, are among the best full-backs in the world and therefore have to be included in any combined XI with Barcelona Credit: AFP

The latter is actually missing the fixture through a thigh problem, but when fit, is one of the best left-backs in world football.



Barcelona are also set to be without Jules Kounde due to an injury sustained against Real Betis - but the Arsenal and Liverpool transfer target has been given the nod at the back over Pau Cubarsi.

"So look, Achraf Hakimi and Nuno Mendes are shoo-ins," Brassell continued to talkSPORT. "There's no doubt about that.

"I think what's interesting about Hakimi is that since he started playing with Nuno Mendes in a back four, the defensive part of his game has got better.

"I think really he stays more to allow Mendes to go more; I feel that works really well. Hakimi's quite judicious, chooses his times to sprint forward sparingly.



"William Pacho, I think you could argue that he's the best central defender in the world. He's pretty close anyway.

8 Kounde was handed a new five-year deal by Barca in 2025 and Brassell believes he is the best in that position at the club Credit: AFP

"PSG are absolutely peerless with him involved. I think you could say either him or Gabriel [Magalhães] are the best left-footed centre-back in the world.

"Maybe Pacho's that little bit better defensively. And then for the other centre-back, I've gone for someone who often gets cast as a right-back, but I still think he's Barcelona's best defender in that: Jules Kounde - Because he is someone who is an amazing defender, an amazing athlete.



"Definitely works in a three as well because he can shift across from right-back, or he can shift across to right-back or a right-sided hybrid role when Hakimi goes.

"He's an underrated right-back and a really underrated centre-back because he doesn't get to play there that often anymore.

"I've gone for him really in this line-up just because he's more experienced and accomplished than Cubasi.

"And Marquinhos is still very good but not quite what he was, which is why I've put Kounde in."



Rodri's Barcelona move has been a smart one

PSG's midfield has regularly been hailed as the best in Europe, but the Catalans have now added a Ballon d'Or winner to their ranks.

Rodri left Man City after seven years of stellar service to seal a return to his homeland with Barca for a fee in the region of £65.3m.

The 30-year-old was one of Brassell's two Barcelona selections in his three-man midfield alongside his club and countrymen, Pedri.

"It was a really difficult choice," the Trans Europe Express podcast host continued to talkSPORT.com.



"I just feel that with Rodri, he's good enough for any team in the world, really. I think already the move to Barcelona has proved to be a smart one.

"I think Barcelona and La Liga will extend his career, as I've said before.

"He's looking very good, despite the fact that there is definitely part of moving into Barcelona in the fact that Hansi Flick's teams, and this team in particular, is sometimes defensively chaotic.

8 Rodri joined Barcelona after being named the player of the tournament in Spain's World Cup win Credit: Getty



"Pedri is just one of the very best in the world. I don't think any midfielder has an understanding or an appreciation of space that he has. He can receive the ball under pressure better than anyone since Tony Kroos. He's got such an incredible range of passing.

"He's excellent if he's deeper in midfield or if he's pushed all the way up; he can create. It had to be him as well.

"Then I've gone for Vitinha, because Vitinha as well is a little bit of a unicorn, really. Again, someone who's primarily a defensive midfielder, but he's not 6ft4 and a tackler.

"Someone who's got an incredible range of passing, again very good at receiving the ball and giving accurate passes under pressure.



"He's contributed more to the attacking side of the game in the last year or so. It's remarkable to think that he's one of the best midfielders in the world and he's still getting better.

"For that reason, I've had to leave out Joao Neves, who's having a little dip at the moment....We've had to leave out Fermin Lopez!"

8 Since the start of the 2024-25 season, Fermin is one of only two Barcelona players who have averaged 1+ involvement per 90 in the UEFA Champions League (min. 900 minutes played) - and is 'definitely a sub for one of these three', Brassell says Credit: Getty

Yamal is probably the best player in the world

Lamine Yamal has been tipped to win this year's Ballon d'Or, an award currently held by Ousmane Dembele.



Yet it's the reigning holder of the Golden Ball who has to make way in a star-studded attack between his current and former teams.

Instead, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia - last year's Champions League player of the season - has been given the nod to join Yamal in attack.

Brassell explained: "Cards on the table, I've had to leave him [Dembele] out. It's been really hard.

"But I think with the way they've played in the last year and a half, two years, I don't think you can leave out Lamine Yamal, who's probably the best player in the world at the moment.



8 Yamal's World Cup triumph may give him the edge in the Ballon d'Or race Credit: Getty

"Or Raphinha, who's a player you could actually argue is more important for Barcelona.

Raphinha, who we know, is very good as a left winger, who's brilliant as an inside left, and it turns out brilliant as a centre forward as well.

"We've seen this season. Incredible on and off the field. He's a great leader in the dressing room as well.



"But if we're talking about who could possibly be the best player in the world, Kvaratskhelia has got to be in the conversation as well.

"The best player in the Champions League last season. Last of the authentic wingers, I think we can say, could also wreak havoc in central areas.

"So, all this has led to poor Dembele getting bumped from the team, but the front three for me, and I've no problem with it, are Lamine, Raphinha, Kvaratskhelia."

8 Kvaratskhelia has been a huge player for PSG Credit: Getty



Hansi Flick over Luis Enrique

The surprises don't stop at the combined XI - the matter of picking between two of Europe's elite managers has also been decided.

Brassell admitted: "I know it's sacrilege to go against Luis Enrique...

"But what I've always loved about Hansi Flick is his ability to take players and get them to adapt to a completely different role that they don't think is theirs and thrive in that role.

"He's done it time and time again.

8 Hansi Flick has both the best goals per game ratio (3) and worst goals conceded per game ratio (1.6) of any Barcelona manager to take charge of 5+ games in the Champions League Credit: Getty



"For that reason, I'd love to see him work with some of these PSG players and see what more he can bring out of them.

"What do you reckon he would do with a year and a half or two years of Kvara? Maybe Nuno Mendes ends up being a midfielder.

"It could be anything, really. He's just got such an incredible vision. You think of someone like Luis Enrique or Pep [Guardiola] having an incredible vision of the game.

"Of course, they are authentic coaches. They are brilliant developers of players.



"But if we're talking about persuading top-level players to try something different and expand themselves in ways that they never could have imagined, Hansi Flick's the guy. There's no doubt about that."

Sports.title: Who are Aston Villa’s opponents Viking? Champions League debutants who once shocked Chelsea
Sports.content:
Who are Aston Villa’s opponents Viking? Champions League debutants who once shocked Chelsea

Aston Villa face a potential banana skin in the Champions League this week as they host Norwegian champions Viking.

Unai Emery's side will be hoping to continue their perfect start to their league phase campaign.



4 Villa continue their European adventure at home to Viking on Wednesday Credit: Getty

Wins over Club Brugge and Fenerbahce leave Villa third in the standings heading into matchday three.

Meanwhile, last week's 6-0 home victory over the latter represented their biggest-ever European triumph.

Viking will be hoping to avoid a similarly heavy defeat on Wednesday night.



Kick-off is scheduled for 8pm, with live commentary available on talkSPORT 2 from 7.45pm.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Who are Viking?

Founded in 1899, this season represents Viking's first-ever appearance in the group stage or league phase of the Champions League.

4 Viking are making their debut in the Champions League league phase this season Credit: Getty

Following their title triumph in 2025, the club beat Dinamo Zagreb in the play-off round in August to make it this far.



The Dark Blues, who hail from Norway's third-largest city Stavanger, play their home matches at the 15,900-capacity Viking Stadion.

In contrast, Villa Park currently holds almost 37,000 fans despite the North Stand currently being closed for redevelopment.

Last year's Norwegian title was the ninth in Viking's history and their first since 1991.

However, the six-time cup winners were playing in the second-tier as recently as 2019.



Despite that, they rescued a memorable draw at home to Bayern Munich last time out.

4 Viking snatched a 3-3 draw at home to Bayern last time out Credit: Getty

Having surrendered a 2-0 lead on home soil, Viking scored a 90th minute equaliser to snatch a 3-3 draw against the German giants.

It followed a 3-1 away defeat to Stuttgart in their league phase opener.



Prior to this season, their only previous appearance in a European competition proper came in the group stage of the 2005/06 UEFA Cup.

Viking's record against English clubs

Despite their lack of European pedigree, Viking can boast some famous wins against continental heavyweights.

Those include a shock triumph in their only previous meeting with English opponents.

Viking beat Chelsea 5-4 on aggregate in the first round of the 2002/03 UEFA Cup.



4 Chelsea were beaten in the UEFA Cup by Viking back in 2002 Credit: AFP

A 4-2 home win in the second leg secured their progression at the Blues' expense.

The Chelsea side that day, which was managed by Claudio Ranieri, included the likes of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Emmanuel Petit, Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink and Gianfranco Zola.

Meanwhile, Viking were captained by former Fulham defender Brede Hangeland and were aided by two goals from ex-Manchester United striker Erik Nevland.



Knocking Chelsea out is not the club's only notable European victory, though.

Viking previously dumped Sporting Lisbon out of the UEFA Cup at the same stage three years earlier.

A 3-0 home win over the Portuguese side saw them secure a 3-1 aggregate win in the 1999/00 edition of the tournament.

Aston Villa's Champions League fixtures September 8: Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa October 14: Aston Villa 6-0 Fenerbahce October 21: Viking (H), live on talkSPORT 2 November 3: Barcelona (A) November 24: Galatasaray (A) December 8: Paris Saint-Germain (H) January 19: Borussia Dortmund (H) January 27: Slavia Prague (A)

Have Villa played Norwegian opponents before?

As for Villa, Viking will be only the second club from Norway they have faced in a competitive fixture.



Their only previous clash with a Norwegian outfit came in the first round of the 1998/99 UEFA Cup.

On that occasion, Villa beat Stromsgodset 6-2 on aggregate after wins in both legs of the tie.

A narrow 3-2 home victory at Villa Park was followed by a comfortable 3-0 triumph in the second leg in Norway.

However, Villa would go on to lose to Celta Vigo in the second round.
