Sports.title: Louis Rees-Zammit is faster, stronger and more dangerous than ever. From special socks and 200kg squats to Marbella boot camp that burnt NFL bulk, this is how Wales flier can keep pace with an Olympic sprinter AND lift weights like a forward
Sports.content:
As Bristol Bears celebrated and dissected their impressive PREM win over reigning champions Northampton earlier this month, one surprising feature stood out in the mixed zone – Louis Rees-Zammit’s socks. While scrum-half Harry Randall went topless in Bristol's new post-match media area, Rees-Zammit – who has made a flying start this season with four tries in three matches – had taken off his boots. In doing so, he revealed one of the latest secrets to his success. On top of his usual long Bears match socks, Rees-Zammit now wears an extra pair of specially designed, shorter grip socks. Many other players, especially backs, do this. But as usual, Rees-Zammit has a point of difference in that on the end of his are individual holes for each of his toes. ‘I don’t know if they make me faster, but I feel a bit more control on my feet,’ Rees-Zammit said. ‘I feel being able to spread my toes within my boot helps me change direction and do what I do on the field. It’s a bit of a weird one to see, I can imagine!' It has now been 14 months since Rees-Zammit returned to rugby from his stint playing American Football, first with the Kansas City Chiefs and then the Jacksonville Jaguars. In his first season with Bristol, the now 25-year-old – by his own admission – took a while to adjust back to the sport he grew up playing. That was understandable. Rugby and NFL are two very different sports in terms of their physical demands, even if they share a common theme of physicality. Rees-Zammit was certainly not poor last season, but on the evidence of what we’ve seen this term, he looks back to his best. Louis Rees-Zammit has made a flying start this season with four tries in the first three matches One part of his success is down to the new grip socks he is using, with individual toes to add greater control while changing direction at his searing speeds

Your browser does not support iframes.

The Wales flier certainly hasn’t lost any of his trademark speed. But it is in other areas of his game that his development has been significant. His performance against Northampton was notable not only for two trademark tries and copying opposition flanker and friend Henry Pollock's 'pulse check' celebration, but a 50:22 kick and strong physicality both in the carry and at the contact area. His defensive work has improved, too. ‘What I love about all players, including Louis, is that if they put the work in, they get the reward,’ said Bristol director of rugby Pat Lam. ‘He’s kicking really well and has put a lot of time and effort into hitting 50:22s. Jordan Crane, our defence coach, does extra tackling work with our backs and Louis has been in for that. ‘He’s in such a great place mentally. He’s got a smile on his face, he’s enjoying the company of the boys here, the way we’re trying to play, and what we’re trying to do. You see the finishing stuff from him, but he’s banging into contact. He’s clearing players out at the ruck. There’s a lot of stuff in his game that I value as a coach.’ One of professional sport’s most genetically gifted athletes, Rees-Zammit’s point of difference has always been – and always will be – his speed. He once hit an eye-popping 24.2mph during a rugby match, which as it happens is faster than anyone has ever been recorded during an NFL game. But one of the biggest factors in his fine form has been his physical work. When trying to make it as a wide receiver or running back in the USA, Rees-Zammit upped his weight to fit NFL requirements, weighing in at about 16st 8lb. Now, he’s down to 15st 6lb, close to his weight from his first rugby stint. It is not a massive difference, but it has allowed Rees-Zammit to maintain his trademark pace with impressive power and explosivity. Jake Gillies, Bristol’s sports scientist, told Daily Mail Sport that in pre-season, Rees-Zammit was recorded running at 10.77 metres per second, again just over 24mph. He once raced Welsh Olympic sprinter Jeremiah Azu at Bristol’s training ground over 40 metres and was only just pipped to the post, clocking in at 4.59 seconds to Azu’s 4.54. Combined with his new power – Rees-Zammit can squat 200kg – it is little wonder that opposition defences are struggling to haul him in. ‘When everyone thinks about Louis, they think about his peak speed and rightly so because he's a freak,’ Gillies added. ‘But what impresses me most about him is how quickly he gets to that peak. His acceleration from a standing start is silly. He got to 10.77 metres per second in just over 4.5 seconds in training. 'But he's also strong in contact because the faster you are going into it, the harder you are to stop. At his weight, the momentum he carries into every contact, if he's running at full speed, is significant. He’s a really unique player.’ Rees-Zammit’s point of difference has always been – and always will be – his speed. He once hit an eye-popping 24.2mph during a rugby match His performance against Northampton was notable not only for two trademark tries, but a 50:22 kick and strong physicality both in the carry and at the contact area Rees-Zammit celebrates a try against Northampton with a 'pulse check' celebration - stolen from his friend and Saints flanker Henry Pollock (right) Last season, Rees-Zammit spent long periods playing full-back for both club and country. Now, he is back in his favoured wing position. Being dropped to the bench by a struggling Wales side in the summer was a reflection that Rees-Zammit wasn’t firing on all cylinders, and he acted upon it. In the off-season, he headed to Marbella with former Bristol team-mate Rich Lane and England women’s No10 Holly Aitchison to ensure he was fighting fit. ‘I was joking with him when I saw he was on holiday with Rich,’ said Lam. ‘Rich was very good at those kicks as well. I saw the video he posted from that trip online and I laughed and said: “Did you only put the good ones in there?” He said he didn’t and after he hit the 50:22 against Northampton, I said: “Fair play. You’re getting your reward for that."' In a World Cup season, Rees-Zammit looks determined to impress, and that can only be good news for Bristol as well as Wales, who named him in their 39-man Nations Championship squad for their autumn games on Tuesday. Dragons backs Aneurin Owen and Che Hope and Cardiff prop Rhys Barrett are the uncapped players in head coach Steve Tandy’s party, while Leicester flanker Tommy Reffell is absent due to a knee injury. His Tigers team-mate Olly Cracknell also misses out, as does No8 great Taulupe Faletau and young Scarlets centre Macs Page. Against Northampton, Rees-Zammit made 81 metres with ball in hand, beat six defenders and scored twice – and was only denied a hat-trick by a Tommy Freeman block. The more unseen parts of his game were just as good. Rees-Zammit also scored twice at Sale, showing a scintillating turn of foot to track escaping Sharks wing Arron Reed. He was then rested, like most of Bristol’s key men, for last weekend’s European trip to South Africa where the Bears were thumped 49-12 by the Stormers, but will return to face Exeter on Saturday. ‘In his first couple of months here, he was still getting used to being back in a stop-start game that isn't quite as stop-start as NFL,’ Gillies said of Rees-Zammit. ‘I don't think we saw his speed capabilities last year. I think we had a couple of times where he went 10.2, 10.3 and 10.4 metres a second, but you could see there was still room for him to develop that more. Now, he’s just lean mass. He’s so strong – one of our strongest backs. ‘He’ll squat the same as some of the forwards and that means he has the ability to produce an impressive amount of force which underpins his speed. Louis is very relaxed when he runs. His technical model of sprinting is brilliant, so smooth. It’s just poetry. In the off-season, Rees-Zammit headed to Marbella with former Bristol team-mate Rich Lane and England women’s No10 Holly Aitchison to ensure he was fighting fit In a World Cup season, he looks determined to impress, and that can only be good news for Bristol as well as Wales 'Louis is very relaxed when he runs. His technical model of sprinting is brilliant, so smooth. It’s just poetry' ‘We never want our players to stand still, so we’re looking at how we can get Louis’ peak velocity higher but also how we can get him there quicker. Our programme allows players to run fast often in training. I would love to see him over a longer track. 'I think if he had 80 metres to run into, he could get to 11 metres per second. He’s definitely the fastest I’ve worked with by some distance. But there’s not a lot of room on pitches in today’s game, so the fact he can also evade people, go round people, and use his physicality really makes him stand out. He can kick and chip, too.’ Even in a disappointing defeat by Saracens, Rees-Zammit showed flashes of promise. ‘I’m loving playing with this team,’ said the 25-year-old, who has two specific sprint training sessions each week and has called for a ban on rugby being played on artificial pitches after suffering horrid leg burns at Saracens. ‘We had a really good pre-season. Last season, we obviously didn’t make the top four in the PREM (Bristol finished sixth) and that was a bit painful. I’m working hard every day in training. If I can add more strings to my bow, that’s only going to help me be a better player.’

Sports.title: Awful moment Leeds United fan verbally abuses Sir Alex Ferguson, 84, as he watches his beloved Man United at Elland Road
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson was verbally abused by Leeds United fans during Manchester United's clash with the Premier League side at the weekend.

The legendary Manchester United manager was in the stands to watch his former side take on their bitter rivals Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday. Dominic Calvert-Lewin cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's opener as the match finished 1-1.

A video circulating on social media has shown the 84-year-old, who was carrying a walking stick, appearing to exit the stands when he was heckled by a fan.

'Fergie', was shouted at him repeatedly from above the stairs, causing him to look up.

The fan then shouted 'you ****,' which Ferguson appeared to ignore, before he headed down the stairs. Across the video was the caption 'hahahaha'.

Whether there will be any repercussions for the fan remains to be seen. Daily Mail Sport have contacted Leeds United for comment.

The legendary Manchester United manager was in the stands to watch his former side take on their bitter rivals Leeds at Elland Road on Sunday

The Leeds-Manchester United rivalry is typically fraught, and one that Ferguson experienced to its fullest during his 26 years in charge.

Reflecting in his autobiography, Managing My Life, Ferguson said: 'The (Elland Road) crowd invariably give us the impression that a lynching would be too good for us.

'I have always said Liverpool-Manchester United games are fierce in many aspects. But it never reaches the levels of Leeds United. Never.'

He described the atmosphere best after a defeat in Yorkshire where he wrote: ‘You can feel the hatred, the animosity. I said to the players afterwards, “Now you know what it’s like to lose here”.

‘The Leeds supporters were awful. I almost want them to be relegated because of their fans. I don’t think they deserve to be in the Premier League. Such hatred really is incredible.

‘A TV camera caught a woman screaming abuse at me. What chance have you got? You could understand the animosity better if it was Liverpool and United because they are just down the road from one another.

‘You can’t say the same for Leeds. You are expecting a pitch invasion at any moment.’

This past weekend's clash was positively friendly in contrast, with the post-match press conferences confined to talking about the action on the pitch rather than dealing with any situation off it - although the abuse of Ferguson had not been made apparent to either manager at the time.

The Leeds-Manchester United rivalry is typically fraught, and one that Ferguson experienced to its fullest during his 26 years in charge

After, Leeds boss Daniel Farke praised his side for their dominance in the 'special game'.

'It says a lot about how far we've come in the last three years that we are slightly disappointed it was just a point against Manchester United. Overall, it was not necessary to be in a losing position at half-time, I thought we were the dominant side.

'We lacked a bit in our decision-making in the first half, we added clarity in the second half. We had momentum completely on our side. We threatened them with physicality, maybe it wasn't the time for our more technical players.

'We are definitely on the right path. This is a special game. I wanted to go for it, it's a sign that we're doing many things in the right way.'

Sports.title: Why defiant Man City fans are going bananas: former forward Imre Varadi on his trademarked giant inflatable fruit based on his famous terrace nickname... with club set to order another 30,000!
Sports.content:
Why defiant Man City fans are going bananas: former forward Imre Varadi on his trademarked giant inflatable fruit based on his famous terrace nickname... with club set to order another 30,000!

Bananas are back in fashion, and Imre Varadi is a man in demand. 'The phone is ringing off the hook,' he explains and right on cue his device pings and lights up with another message.

This time it is a request for him to appear on a radio show coming his way via former team-mate Lee Chapman.

They, like the rest of us, want to know how at the age of 67, and 40 years after he first played up front for Manchester City, his cult status has been revitalised by giant inflatable bananas.

It is a twist of fate not only good for Varadi’s ego but good for his business as two years ago he acted upon the random fact that City supporters came to affectionately refer to him as Imre Banana back in the day by trademarking the name.

Call it a striker’s instinct. Or business acumen after 25 years working as an agent. He saw the opening and made his move.

Now he produces branded inflatable bananas, T-shirts and pin badges.

He sells them around the world and has a partnership with Manchester City, who are understood to be planning to order another 30,000 bananas.

City fans are embracing bananas all over again as a symbol of solidarity in the wake of criticism after the club was found guilty of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules.

Imre Varadi produces inflatable bananas with his nickname as well as T-shirts and pin badges

The bananas have become a symbol of City fans' defiance after the guilty verdict handed down by the independent commission

'I think it’s their way of saying that whatever happens we’ll be behind the team and the club, and we’ll still be having fun,' says Varadi. 'We’ve had bad times. We’ve been in the second and third divisions and never forget the history, but we love the club and we’ll always stick with them and support them.

'It is great fun and it has helped to galvanise everybody. The sea of bananas in the away end at Anfield was great to see and to be at the Etihad on Saturday [against Ipswich] and see all the Mums and Dads and kids carrying them to the game was incredible.

'I’m so honoured and proud to be such a part of it. I don’t think many of them know I was ever a footballer.'

Varadi was born in London with an Italian mother and a Hungarian father and came through the youth ranks at Luton Town.

'They released me and Kerry Dixon, and we both cried our eyes out,' he says. 'But you dust yourself down and get on with it. Kerry ended up playing at Dunstable and I went to Letchworth.

'After a year, Harry Haslam rang me and told me to come to Sheffield United, so I went up there played in a reserve game and scored a hat trick, played in another reserve game and scored again.

'He gave me a two-and-a-half-year professional contract and I never looked back. Kerry as we all know went to Reading, Chelsea and played for England and had a fantastic career.'

Imre Varadi scores City's second in a 3-1 win over Aston Villa in 1986

Varadi in action during a 1-1 draw against Manchester United at Maine Road in 1986

From left to right; Martin Hodge, Varadi, Mick Lyons, Gary Megson and Pat Heard at Sheffield Wednesday in 1984

Varadi did not stay anywhere for too long. He left Bramall Lane for Everton and scoring the winner in an FA Cup tie against Liverpool at Goodison Park remains one of his fondest memories.

'Everton hadn’t beaten Liverpool in years, and I lost it when I scored, running round the back of the goal to celebrate with the supporters. Within three or four seconds I realised these were the wrong supporters.

'It was the Liverpool supporters, and someone threw a meat and potato pie and hit me right in the middle of my face. I can still taste it today. I’ll never forget it.'

At Newcastle he wore the famous No9 shirt, scored goals at a rate close to one-in-two and spent a season playing alongside Kevin Keegan.

In the first of his two spells at Sheffield Wednesday, he won promotion to the top-flight before a season at West Bromwich Albion and the move to City in 1986.

He finished the season as City’s top scorer but could not do enough to stop them sliding back into the second tier. As the next season got under way at home against Plymouth Argyle, there was a supporter called Frank Newton who took an inflatable banana with him to Maine Road, basically for a laugh.

'I remember jogging out on the game and seeing a banana,' says Varadi. 'That was strange enough and then one banana became two or three and then eight or nine and then it went whoosh.' Fans started singing Imre Banana instead of Imre Varadi and the craze spread across the country.

Varadi with Kevin Keegan during his time at Newcastle between 1981 and 1983

'West Ham had inflatable hammers, Norwich had canaries, Grimsby had the fish, but we started it,' says Varadi. 'People have called me Imre Banana from there.'

He scored 31 in 81 games for City before returning to Wednesday in September 1988. There were then three years at Leeds, again with Chapman, but mainly as back up. He did not make enough appearances for a title winners’ medal in 1992.

There was a brief return to Luton, six games on loan, and two successful years at Rotherham among other ports of call before ending his career in non-league, coaching at Matlock Town and Stalybridge Celtic before taking his qualifications to become an agent.

'I just sort of fell into it,' he says. 'I always thought I’d go into coaching but because I had a lot of clubs, I had a lot of contacts and knew a hell of a lot of people. The opportunity came to go into an agency, so I took my exam and I’ve been a FIFA licensed agent ever since.'

For 16 years he worked at the Stellar Group agency, then struck out alone with a small group of clients. 'I’ll always do that,' he says. 'I love working, I work every day. I love interacting with players, speaking to clubs and watching games.'

Varadi was at home on his sofa recovering from a toe operation when he finally did something about an idea about the inflatable bananas.

'I’d thought about doing it years ago but never got round to it,' he says. 'And there I was, watching City winning the fourth title in a row and the bananas were coming out again to celebrate.

'I decided I’d take a closer look into the business and found inflatables were a multimillion-pound industry. I was sure there was a gap I could slide into. Some people think I’m jumping on the bandwagon but I’m the original story. I’m the original Imre Banana. That’s me.'

Sports.title: 'Boring' training sessions, four-hour meetings and annoying the owners: 'Crazy' Antonio Conte would be a 'DISASTER' at Man United, claims Ashley Young
Sports.content:
'Boring' training sessions, four-hour meetings and annoying the owners: 'Crazy' Antonio Conte would be a 'DISASTER' at Man United, claims Ashley Young

Ashley Young has claimed Antonio Conte would be a 'disaster' managing Manchester United - after the Italian revealed his desire to manage a fallen giant.

Conte, 57, is out of work after leaving Napoli at the end of last season following a two-year stint where he won Serie A and the Italian Super Cup.

Michael Carrick is still in post at Old Trafford and there are no immediate suggestions of that changing, but their struggles so far this season have raised alarm.

Young played under Conte at Inter Milan, where they won a Serie A title together, and says that Manchester United's players would be unhappy with his love for running and lengthy meetings - even if he is grateful personally to the Italian.

United's lack of running in matches this season has left them exposed and led to Gary Neville branding them an 'absolute disgrace'.

And Young told the Overlap Daily show: 'A lot of talk has been about Man United’s running stats. If they’re not going to run and Antonio Conte goes in there, it’s going to be a disaster, I think.

Antonio Conte would be a 'disaster' at Manchester United, Ashley Young has claimed

Young says Man United's players would not appreciate the level of running and long meetings

'He is throwing his name in the hat. Whether that is something that’s going to happen or not, I’m not sure whether the Man United players will be happy. I think you saw that when he went to Tottenham Hotspur.

'Speaking to a lot of Tottenham players – and I had spoken to Chelsea players before I went to Inter Milan and was like, "So what’s he like?" And they were like, "You’re gonna run a lot, you’ll be fitter than you’ve ever been."

'But do you know what? That was one of the things where I think that I was able to continue my career for so long because of the running, although it was crazy.

'The training sessions were a lot of 11 v 11, at times a little bit boring. Meetings were long. When I say long, I’m talking, if we lost the game, we could go in and do the meeting after the game and it’d stop literally everything.

'And you could be in there for three, four hours. I think that’s one of the reasons why he doesn’t last long at places, because not just the players – he tries to test mentally – but the board as well, and the owners, and I think that people get annoyed with him.'

Conte has a dazzling CV, having won league titles at Chelsea, Juventus, and Inter, but he is also known for his combustibility and not lasting long in jobs.

His longest gig was with Juventus between 2011 and 2014 but he is often too honest with people to retain relationships.

He was sacked by Tottenham in 2023 after a savage 10-minute rant where he branded them selfish, accused them of lacking 'fire in the eyes', and admitted the collective spirit had regressed.

Young played under Conte at Inter Milan and they won a Serie A title together in 2020-21

'They don't play for something important. They don't want to play under pressure. They don't want to play under stress. It is easy in this way. Tottenham's story is this,' he said.

'Until now, I try to hide the situation but there are 10 games to go and some people think we can fight. Fight for what? With this spirit, this attitude, this commitment? What? For seventh, eighth, 10th place?'

Conte's name is being mentioned around United after he did an interview with The Athletic earlier this month and told them of his ambition to restore a fallen giant.

He has been linked with the managerial role at Manchester United in the past and told The Athletic: 'If you go to a club where the history speaks for itself - a history made up of trophies, league titles and victories - you can only honour that history in one way: by having the ambition to bring that club back, if it isn't there today, to fight for those goals.

'I know full well that only one team can win every year, but I must carry in my heart, and instil in the hearts of the fans, my players and my directors, that spark, that hope that makes you say, "f***, we can win". You only make history by winning.

'There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history. I'd like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more.

'Clubs where there's pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you're not going there just to take part, but to compete.'

United continue to endure a tough period, with the club having not won the Premier League title since Sir Alex Ferguson's last season in 2012-13.

In the subsequent 13 years, United's only trophies have been the FA Cup (in 2016 and 2024), the EFL Cup (in 2017 and 2023), and the Europa League (in 2017), and they have rarely threatened to challenge for the biggest titles.

There does not appear to be much chance of that this season, with the Red Devils sat 13th in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Piers Morgan disagreed with me but Martin Keown was wrong to question my motives in branding Arsenal 'The Unwatchables'... I have a duty to call it as I see it, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE
Sports.content:
Piers Morgan disagreed with me but Martin Keown was wrong to question my motives in branding Arsenal 'The Unwatchables'... I have a duty to call it as I see it, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

It was around 2pm on Monday that I learned I was a lifelong Tottenham supporter who was desperate to move to London.

This certainly came as a shock to someone who follows another club entirely and has no plans to leave the Midlands. I also lived and worked in London for nearly 20 years.

Apparently, Martin Keown knows otherwise. Responding to my report of Arsenal’s 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest, Keown was quoted on talkSPORT’s X account as saying ‘I’m told he’s a Spurs fan… a journalist in the West Midlands looking to move to London.’

His anger was sparked by this paragraph in the piece. ‘Fans are disillusioned by the ongoing saga and the wider game needs a spectacular team to celebrate. Sadly, where once we had Arsene Wenger’s Invincibles, we now endure Mikel Arteta’s Unwatchables.’

Piers Morgan had his say later – with one crucial difference. Morgan disagreed with the article in every way but at no point did he speculate on my reasons for writing it.

Responding to my report of Arsenal’s 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest, Keown was quoted saying ‘I’m told he’s a Spurs fan… a journalist in the West Midlands looking to move to London'

Do Arsenal have a duty to entertain? No, and I expect them to win the title this year. Yet with their current approach, they are unlikely to be remembered in the same way the Invincibles were, or the way some of Alex Ferguson’s Manchester United teams or the Liverpool sides of the 1980s were.

Keown was a fine player and is a thoughtful pundit. He won 10 trophies in a hugely successful career with Arsenal and watches their progress with a keen eye. He disagreed with my analysis that the Gunners under Arteta are a tough watch – no problem.

When a journalist writes a forthright article, they know that criticism will follow. ‘You don’t know what you’re talking about’ or ‘What a load of rubbish’ – in the age of social media, these are some of the more polite responses.

Yet pundits should not try to guess why a journalist wrote a piece. A fair number of listeners might have heard that I was ‘a Tottenham fan’ and concluded I had written the piece because I was biased against Arsenal.

For the record, there are many Spurs fans in the media and none show bias, yet football is tribal and fans do not like their teams coming under attack.

That does not justify a pundit making statements – in this case incorrect – that could prompt listeners to doubt a reporter’s professionalism or credibility.

As always when we watch matches, we write about what we see. At Forest, I saw an Arsenal side put together at huge expense who registered a single shot on target, against a team who had yet to score at home this season and were without their best player.

In those circumstances, I thought they were disappointing and said so. But it will never be anything to do with the club I support - who, for the record, are not a member of the so-called big six, and nor do they play in London or the Midlands.

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez set to leave Man United next summer in defensive overhaul, how abusive Leeds fans got to Sir Alex Ferguson despite Elland Road police guard, Harry Amass heads for exit and Kai Rooney's rapid rise up academy ranks
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez set to leave Man United next summer in defensive overhaul, how abusive Leeds fans got to Sir Alex Ferguson despite Elland Road police guard, Harry Amass heads for exit and Kai Rooney's rapid rise up academy ranks

Manchester United’s defensive rebuild next summer is set to signal the end of Lisandro Martinez’s Old Trafford career.

The Argentine landed himself in hot water after last week’s 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid when he criticised his employers over United’s transfer policy in the summer window, saying he expected more of director of football Jason Wilcox, but sources insist that would not be the reason for the defender's departure.

Martinez was fined by the club and apologised for the timing of his comments in a statement that added: ‘Everyone at the club is doing everything they can to make the team successful.'

The 28-year-old started Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Leeds at Elland Road, but came off at half-time with a thigh injury having already spent 20 months out of action during his four-year United career. When he is fit, Martinez has been a regular on the left side of central defence since moving to United from Ajax for £57million in 2022, making 115 appearances and scoring four goals.

But he will be out of contract at the end of June and is unlikely to sign a new one. United would be very reluctant to let the 2022 World Cup winner leave as a free agent, so it’s more probable that the club would trigger a 12-month extension in his contract and try to sell him in the summer.

United retain an interest in Jarrad Branthwaite having had two offers worth up to £50m rejected by Everton in 2024, and could try again in the summer.

Lisandro Martinez is set to leave Manchester United next summer to begin the club's defensive overhaul

United retain an interest in Jarrad Branthwaite (centre) having had two offers worth up to £50m rejected by Everton in 2024, and could try again in the summer

Uncertainty also hangs over the futures of Luke Shaw and Harry Maguire. Shaw is out of contract after 12 years at Old Trafford and doesn’t have an extension clause in his current deal, unlike Maguire who has a 12-month option to extend the one-year contract that he signed in April.

United have a decision to make on both players, but it's understood there are no doubts over Matthijs de Ligt's future at the club even though the Dutchman has been out of action for almost a year with a back injury that required surgery. De Ligt, who has been an unused substitute for the last two games against Leeds and Atletico Madrid, is under contract until 2029 with the option of another year.

Fergie under fire

It’s a measure of the bad blood between Manchester United and Leeds that Sir Alex Ferguson’s chauffeur-driven car arrived at Elland Road on Sunday protected by four police outriders.

The two clubs were taking no chances with Ferguson’s safety at one of the most incendiary fixtures in the English football calendar, and made sure that the legendary United boss got into the ground without any incident.

The 84-year-old is using a walking stick at the moment as he recovers from an achilles problem that has also required him to wear a protective boot.

Despite the efforts of the police and Leeds security staff, however, Ferguson was verbally abused by one fan in a video circulated on social media as he made his way from his seat in the stands – where he was sat with his former kit man Albert Morgan – to the directors’ lounge at half-time.

Ferguson dominated the rivalry with Leeds during his time as United boss, winning 20 of his 36 matches against them and losing only five.

If further evidence of the animosity between the two clubs was needed, ex-Leeds boss and current Canada head coach Jesse Marsch referred to United as ‘the scum’ when he congratulated Daniel Farke’s side on their performance in the 1-1 draw in a post on Monday.

Ferguson dominated the rivalry with Leeds when he was United manager, winning 20 of his 36 matches against them - the last of which being this 3-0 League Cup win in 2011

No Carrick summit

Contrary to speculation over summit talks between Michael Carrick and Wilcox at Carrington on Monday, Confidential understands the two men did not meet at the training ground.

Even though the players were off after Sunday's draw at Leeds before training and travelling to Italy on Tuesday for the Champions League clash with Como, Carrick and Wilcox didn't have an opportunity to get together after a tough week for both men.

Wilcox came under scrutiny in the wake of Lisandro Martinez’s bombshell TV interview in Madrid, while United’s 2-0 defeat by Atletico and a pair of 1-1 draws with Tottenham and Leeds in the Premier League left Carrick without a win in six games.

However, insiders say that Wilcox still retains the trust of minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, and there is no appetite to change head coach despite Carrick overseeing United’s worst start to a league season in 40 years.

Amass heads for the exit

There is a growing expectation that Harry Amass will leave United in January after playing just 18 minutes of first-team football so far this season.

Even with a raft of injuries at left back, 19-year-old Amass has found himself on the outside looking in with right backs Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui and centre back Ayden Heaven all chosen ahead of him while Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu are sidelined through injury. His only appearance this season was a cameo off the bench in the 4-0 Champions League win over Sabah last month.

United were open to both a loan or permanent move for Amass in the summer, but their inability to recruit a new left back meant the club’s hands were tied. Burnley were among the teams who held talks before choosing not to proceed, and Confidential understands around a dozen Championship clubs are ready to come back to the negotiating table with the January window fast approaching.

Amass, who joined from Watford's academy three years ago, thrived on loan at Sheffield Wednesday last season, and with United out of the Carabao Cup and seemingly reluctant to use Amass even when stretched to the max in his position, expect movement for the youngster in the next eight to ten weeks.

Harry Amass is expected to leave United in January after only making one appearance this season, off the bench in the Champions League against Sabah

Tavernier a target?

United are one of the Premier League clubs being linked with a move for Bournemouth winger Marcus Tavernier in January.

However, Old Trafford sources say they are not proactively tracking the 27-year-old, who is also said to be attracting interest from Liverpool and Chelsea four years after he moved to the Vitality Stadium from Middlesbrough in a £10m deal.

Tavernier has been in fine form to start the season, scoring four times in seven league games including in Bournemouth's 2-0 win over Sunderland on Sunday that secured the Cherries their first three points of the campaign.

It’s understood rival clubs have been encouraged by Bournemouth’s willingness to consider selling players at the right price in January. England midfielder Alex Scott – who was on United’s radar before they signed Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos as part of a midfield rebuild in the summer – may be one of them if clubs offer between £80-100m.

Marcus Tavernier scored in Bournemouth's 4-4 draw at Old Trafford last season

While Wayne Rooney generates plenty of headlines behind a microphone these days, it was son Kai who made a statement on the pitch over the past week

Kai strikes right chord

While Wayne Rooney generates plenty of headlines behind a microphone these days, it was son Kai who made a statement on the pitch over the past week.

Injuries have been a source of real frustration for the 16-year-old, but he is fit again and back in the fold. Rooney made his UEFA Youth League debut for the Under 19s away to Atletico Madrid, and followed that up three days later with his Under 21s debut against Nottingham Forest.

He dropped back down to the Under 18s, also against Forest, to get himself back on the scoresheet but things are heating up nicely for Rooney who remains one of the only true centre-forward options in the academy.

Chido Obi is out on loan while Louie Bradbury has joined Stoke City. It means that Rooney takes on huge significance across the age groups, not least with United having used a false-nine system to this point in the Under 19s and Under 21s.

Sports.title: Graeme Souness labels Bukayo Saka a CHEAT: Liverpool legend claims Arsenal star 'dives all over the place' - leaving Piers Morgan in shock
Sports.content:
Graeme Souness has accused Bukayo Saka of being a 'cheat' who 'dives all over the place'. And the Liverpool legend believes Arsenal have a strategy of ganging up on referees to convince them that a 'screaming' Saka has been fouled. It is an accusation commonly levelled at the England man, 25, who is often among the most-fouled players in a given Premier League season. Fans may remember the controversy that erupted in the Champions League quarter-finals in 2024 when he tried to buy a last-minute penalty against Manuel Neuer in a tie which Arsenal eventually lost. And Souness dug into the winger on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored show, leaving his host outraged. 'Your man Saka dives all over the place. I don't want to hear about him. The minute he looks like losing possession, he's down,' he said. Graeme Souness has accused Bukayo Saka of being a 'cheat' who 'dives all over the place' Fans may remember his 'dive' against Bayern Munich in the Champions League in 2024 Souness says that Saka 'screams' when he goes down and that Arsenal's players work to convince the referee 'He simulates a foul. Anyone who simulates a foul in my book would be a cheat. 'He dives when he should be staying on his feet. He's not alone. So Saka gets tackled, he screams as he's going down. 'The referee thinks there's nothing in that but wait a minute, he's stayed down. And then worse than that, everyone in the immediate area - all Arsenal players - put their hands up and scream foul. 'The referee at that point panics and blows his whistle when it wasn't a foul - his first instinct was the right one. 'But he blows a foul because he's thinking, wait a minute, something I'm not understanding here. 'Simulation is a form of cheating, yes. But it's all over football today. 'If you asked 100 people what is it you dislike about the modern game, 50 per cent would say simulation, another 50 per cent would say VAR.' With the game moving at such speed, it is difficult to always know exactly how hard a player has felt contact, or how a tiny amount of contact may genuinely throw them off. Piers Morgan was unhappy with Souness' suggestion, saying: 'I wouldn't call him a cheat Saka's notoriety for diving has lasted for years, but he is far from the only player to have that criticism levelled at him. The incident with Bayern in 2024 attracted a lot of attention and debate. It initially looked as if the goalkeeper had brought him down, and the winger had got to the ball first. However, replays showed Saka moving his leg in Neuer's direction to collide with him to try and buy a penalty - a move which backfired. Some pundits came down on him with disapproval, with Paola Di Canio telling Sky Sports Italia: 'He moves blatantly the leg towards Neuer, it’s never a penalty. 'He didn’t behave as an experienced player. He behaved like a baby with no experience.' But Rio Ferdinand took Saka's side, saying: 'I can’t believe that’s not been given! That is a penalty, I’m in disbelief.'

Price, 19, joined the Fury family when he married Venezuela, 17, in May on the Isle of Man. The pair have already moved from social media stars to mainstream television after signing up for an I'm a Celebrity spin-off.

And his fame may yet allow Price to earn some cash by taking to the ring. The teenager already has extensive amateur experience and is open to seeing how he fares in the influencer fighting promotion Misfits.

Sports.title: Dele Alli had offer from Gary Neville's Salford City as wait for a club goes on
Sports.content:
Dele Alli had offer from Gary Neville's Salford City as wait for a club goes on

Ex-England and Tottenham star Dele Alli remains without a club but did have a surprise offer to join Salford City after bumping into then-manager Karl Robinson by chance

View 2 Images Dele Alli's last club was Como, but he's been without an employer for an extended period

Former Salford City boss Karl Robinson has revealed that he extended an invitation to bring Dele Alli to the club, with the former Tottenham star still looking for his next challenge.

‌



‌



Dele, a two-time PFA Young Player of the Year winner, has endured a stunning decline having come through the ranks at MK Dons and then shone for a Tottenham side that had challenged for the title under Mauricio Pochettino.

‌



A loss of form and continued injuries has seen him leave north London and he's since headed to Everton, Besiktas and then Como, but he's now on the lookout for a club and was offered a return by Robinson when he was in charge of the League Two outfit.

‌



He said on the No Tippy Tappy Football podcast: “I would 100 per cent give him a chance. I saw him in the gym in June, and I told him to come to Salford. But he probably looked at me and went, ‘Gaffer, come on, I’m not doing that’.”

Dele would never respond to the offer and the ex-Salford manager, who was sacked after losing the play-off final last season, concedes that his mindset will see him miss out on opportunities.

“The reason these players are these players is because they have a self-belief and a poorly-developed sense of fear. I guarantee if you sit down now, he would probably say he could turn around the fortunes of Man Utd. Because that’s how those real top players who produce their moments of magic think.”

‌



Dele is a year without a club but Robinson maintained: “I don’t know why he is not playing football. This is a tremendous young man. He’s struggled through and rose above it and became the person that he is.”

View 2 Images Karl Robinson was prepared to bring Dele Alli to Salford City

‌



The demise of the former Tottenham man has been stark and he was once cited as the player Jose Mourinho should sign at Manchester United by Sir Alex Ferguson.

Dele's latest stint was a false dawn as he left Como prematurely after signing an 18 month deal with the Italian side, who are managed by Cesc Fabregas. The 37-cap England international made just one appearance and lasted only 10 minutes as he was shown a red card for a dangerous challenge on Ruben Loftus-Cheek during a 2-1 defeat to AC Milan.

Sports.title: Man Utd set to admit Lisandro Martinez was right as chiefs draw up transfer plan
Sports.content:
Man Utd set to admit Lisandro Martinez was right as chiefs draw up transfer plan

Lisandro Martinez was fined after slamming Manchester United's hierarchy for not making enough signings in the summer transfer window, but the club appear to have accepted that he was right

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez wanted Michael Carrick to be given a stronger squad (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Manchester United plan to address their issues in defence next summer - and have added Bournemouth left-back Adrien Truffert to their list of targets. United have conceded a concerning 15 goals in their first seven games of the season and manager Michael Carrick has been dealt several injury blows in his backline.

‌



‌



As a consequence, club chiefs such as director of football Jason Wilcox have come under fire for not signing a defender in the summer transfer window. Lisandro Martinez poured fuel on the flames last week when he accused United of not doing enough to bolster Carrick's squad on their return to the Champions League.

‌



His decision to heavily criticise his employers - including calling out Wilcox - divided pundits and supporters, with some arguing that the Argentine shouldn't have spoken out. Most agreed, however, that his comments had merit.

‌



United's failure to sign a left-back has been exposed two months into the new season, with an injury to Luke Shaw forcing Ayden Heaven and Diogo Dalot to play out of position. Shaw is notably one of the eight players who are set to miss Wednesday's trip to Como.

The i Paper report that senior figures at Old Trafford recognise they should've addressed their defence in the summer. United were keen on signing Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall, but the England international proved to be out of their price range.

That's why Truffert, 24, is now on the Red Devils' shortlist, with United said to be long-time admirers of the Frenchman. Truffert is enjoying his second season at Bournemouth after the Cherries paid Rennes £14.4m to sign him in June 2025.

‌



Centre-back is also a position which United will focus on, with Martinez and Harry Maguire in their final year of their deals. The report states that they'll sign at least one central defender and could target a second if Martinez leaves amid interest from Atletico Madrid.

De Ligt's first start since last October could come against Como, with Daniel Armer the only other recognised centre-back spotted in training before United flew to Italy on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Newcastle's major Mikel Arteta offer failed months before Arsenal appointment
Sports.content:
Newcastle's major Mikel Arteta offer failed months before Arsenal appointment

Newcastle made a play to hire current Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta as their new manager back in 2019, with owner Mikel Ashley prepared to back him with a rarely seen contract

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta was offered a long-term deal to lead Newcastle, even though he'd never held a top job before

Newcastle almost landed Mikel Arteta in the summer of 2019 - months before he joined Arsenal - with the Spaniard tempted by the role.

‌



‌



The Magpies had just seen Rafa Benitez depart, which greatly angered fans given his popularity at St James' Park, and Ashley was keen to give Arteta a lengthy deal that showcased his desire to have him on board.

‌



The Newcastle boss was willing to hand out the type of contract that is not normal for a rookie coach, given Arteta's only managerial experience was as a No.2 at Manchester City.

‌



He was genuinely tempted, reports the Telegraph, and made moves to assemble a backroom staff to aid him in the north east. Having never worked as a No.1 he didn't have previous assistants to fall back on, and those he wanted were unable to join him at the time, leading him to turn down the role.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Newcastle had finished a modest 13th in Benitez's final year and would've, in theory, provided Arteta with the ideal start to his life as a manager. The situation at St James' Park was tense given Benitez's popularity and Ashley's immense unpopularity among the fanbase.

The Magpies had also seen Ayoze Perez and Salomon Rondon leave after the duo had combined to score 23 of the 42 goals that Newcastle scored in previous campaign. They would instead hire Steve Bruce after Arteta's rejection, finishing 13th once again.

‌



Arteta has ultimately proved himself to be among Europe's top managers, ending Arsenal's wait for a Premier League title, but in the years after he was appointed he endured some notable frustration at the hands of Newcastle.

View 2 Images Mike Ashley was determined to hire Mikel Arteta when he was still at Manchester City (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



The 2021-22 campaign was the first in the Arteta era during which Arsenal were clearly competitive, and they recovered from a horror start to challenge for the top four. They had their destiny in their own hands in the final weeks but lost at a resurgent Newcastle in the penultimate game of the season, which saw Tottenham pip them.

In 2025, when Arteta was being mocked for his inability to get over the line, Arsenal were favourites to make the final of the Carabao Cup, but fluffed their lines against Newcastle. Eddie Howe's side would win both games 2-0, securing a 4-0 aggregate win.

Sports.title: Value Scope Extra: Three jumps trainers with horses ready to strike first time out
Sports.content:
The jumps season is starting to go through the gears and it goes up another notch with Cheltenham’s opening meeting of the season this weekend.

As the winter performers start emerging from their summer holidays, it often pays to latch onto trainers who have their horses fit to strike first time out.

Lambourn-based Jamie Snowden is certainly one. In the last couple of weeks he has bagged six winners from 20 runners at an impressive strike-rate of 30 per cent. Those stats improve to four winners from ten runners for horses having their first run of the season. That’s a 40 per cent strike-rate.

Ralph Fiennes to star as Sir Henry Cecil in biopic of legendary trainer READ MORE :

Ombudsman confirmed for Breeders' Cup Turf after Champion Stakes triumph READ MORE :

Legendary Luke is an interesting chase debutante due to run at Ffos Las tomorrow, while Wilde’s Legacy could have his first start over hurdles at Market Rasen on Sunday.

‌



Snowden’s bumper runners are always worth a second look. He operates at around 25 per cent with his runners in National Hunt Flat races and he has point-to-point winners Lady Jetfire and Ballycrystal Boy entered at the weekend.

View 3 Images Stuart Edmunds: runners should be respected (Image: PA)

Flying high

Stuart Edmunds’s Leighton Buzzard stables are also flying high Since the start of September, he has recorded eight winners from just 24 runners. That has returned a level-stakes profit of more than 14pts.

His last four winners were all either making their debuts or having their first start of the season, which underlines how fit his horses are.

‌



Both his runners at Ffos Las on Thursday are of interest. Fireball Frenzy returns from nearly two years off the track and consistent One Eye On Vegas will attempt to record career victory number five.

Court Cian has an entry at Aintree on Sunday and could have his first start for more than 18 months. With Edmunds in such terrific form, those lengthy absences are not a worry.

View 3 Images Charlie Longsdon: does well during the autumn (Image: PA)

Fruitful Autumn

Charlie Longsdon is traditionally very strong at this time of year. The autumn months tend to be fruitful for the Cotswolds-based trainer and this year is no different.

‌



Three of his four winners this month – from 16 runners – have come on their first start since returning from their summer break.

Molto Bene would be of particular interest if taking up her entry at Aintree on Sunday. She has won first time out in each of the last two years. Realisation and New Order also catch the eye. They are both entered at Kelso on Saturday.

Sports.title: Dejan Kulusevski opens up on 'impossible' comeback after 526-day injury nightmare
Sports.content:
Dejan Kulusevski opens up on 'impossible' comeback after 526-day injury nightmare

Tottenham midfielder Dejan Kulusevski made an emotional return to the pitch in the 3-1 win over Coventry on Monday night, ending a staggering spell on the sidelines

View 3 Images Dejan Kulusevski made his long-awaited return on Monday (Image: Harvey Murphy/Getty Images)

Dejan Kulusevski overcame his own “impossible” job after telling his loved ones he might not play again.

‌



‌



Kulusevski made his first appearance for Tottenham since May 2025 as a late substitute in their 3-1 win over Coventry City on Monday night. Tottenham midfielder Kulusevski received a hero’s welcome on the pitch and was greeted by his family after the game with one of his kids wearing a shirt with “526 days - my hero” printed on the back.

‌



That was how long it took for him to come back from a serious knee injury and the Sweden international revealed just how tough it was to come back at times and he even warned his family he might not make it.

‌



Kulusevski said: “The journey felt impossible. It was the most difficult it could be, but I had a feeling I was going to come back to play football. I just had to believe and that is what I do.

Sports.title: Erik ten Hag blasts Cristiano Ronaldo and reveals real reason for Man Utd bust-up
Sports.content:
Erik ten Hag blasts Cristiano Ronaldo and reveals real reason for Man Utd bust-up

Cristiano Ronaldo quit Manchester United after a bust-up with Erik ten Hag, and the club's former manager has now blasted him four years on from their public row

View 2 Images Erik ten Hag has spoken out on what went wrong with Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United (Image: ANP, ANP via Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo let Manchester United down by not being fit enough during the final months of his second stint at Old Trafford, according to Erik ten Hag. The club's former manager claims that he pulled out of training sessions and did not work for the team or sufficiently prepare to run during matches.

‌



‌



Ronaldo left United by mutual consent in November 2022, months after Ten Hag took charge. He said at the time that his manager did not respect him.

‌



Four years later, the Dutchman has shared his version of events. He recalls challenging Ronaldo about his lack of professionalism.

‌



Ten Hag has told The Athletic: "I confronted him with this. Many times I say, 'Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can't bring yourself in the box, you can't score'.

"He was not capable to do this. It's the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he's exhausted. But he couldn't. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn't prepare himself. Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team.

"He was telling the players, 'Save your legs at the training'. I understand it when you are top fit; you have sessions, you can save the legs. But first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels."

‌



Ronaldo said in an interview with Piers Morgan Uncensored days before his departure was eventually announced: "I don't have respect for him (Ten Hag) because he doesn't show respect for me."

He added on the same subject: "If you don't have respect for me, I'm never gonna have respect for you. Not only the manager, but the other two or three guys who are around the club.

‌



View 2 Images Ten Hag and Ronaldo rarely saw eye to eye (Image: Matthew Ashton - AMA, Getty Images)

"I felt betrayed. I don't care; people should listen to the truth. Yes, I felt betrayed. I feel that some people didn't want me here, not only this year but last season too."

‌



Ten Hag has also addressed fresh criticism from Fred, who opened up on the Charla Podcast, saying: "Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of c***. He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with [Marcus] Rashford... he wouldn't put me in to play; sometimes it got stressful.

"Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with. He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was] older. He took Cristiano out, and then there was a falling out."

Ten Hag said: "I'm not mad at Fred. You fight with your players when they are showing inefficient and unprepared standards. But it's always with respect. You want to push them; you want to get the best out of them."
