Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: Gareth Davies Believes Tyson Fury Will Fight Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury could face Daniel Dubois after Anthony Joshua, according to Gareth A. Davies, who believes Fury possesses the skills to neutralize the newly crowned WBO heavyweight champion.

Davies floated the possibility following Dubois’s second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley. Although he now rates Dubois as the world’s best heavyweight, he still sees a route to victory for Fury through movement and ring intelligence.

“He’s got the skills to nullify Daniel Dubois, but he’s got to be at his very best,” Davies said to iFL TV. “He needs to be elusive, and he needs his movement, and I think that will be key in the fight. He’s certainly got the IQ to do it.”

Fury would give Dubois a different fight than Wardley did. His movement could force Dubois to keep turning and chasing him, making it harder to plant his feet and land his power shots.

Whether Fury can actually pull that off inside the ropes at this stage is a massive question mark.

Knowing the blueprint to mess with Dubois’ offense is one thing, but dragging those thirty-something legs through twelve rounds against a younger brawler constantly walking him down is another test entirely. Davies thinks a dominant win over Joshua might tempt Fury into stepping in with Dubois, though he floated it purely as speculation rather than a done deal.

“I can see the winner of Fury and Joshua, or either Fury and Joshua, fighting Daniel Dubois,” Davies said. “It’s probably because I want to see it.”

Davies also pointed to Dubois growing as a ring craftsman. He liked the composure Dubois showed while closing the show against Wardley, picking his spots without walking into incoming right-hand counters.

That added discipline makes life tough on Fury. Dubois wouldn’t have to outbox him minute by minute if relentless heat drains the gas tank and leaves Fury carrying concrete in his boots.

Gareth’s theory hinges entirely on Fury having the wheels to dictate where the action happens. If those legs are spent, keeping Dubois off his chest turns into a brutal fight.

Fury has shown zero real appetite to get anywhere near Daniel Dubois, and the reasons are obvious.

Dubois is in his physical prime, throws heavy artillery with both hands, and walks opponents down without blinking. For an aging Fury whose legs are not what they used to be, taking on a puncher like Dubois is high risk with little appeal.

Fury is looking for massive paydays against names that match his era, like Anthony Joshua, or manageable outings where he can control the terms without taking life-altering punishment. Getting cornered by Dubois, taking shots to the body, and being forced into a grueling trench battle simply does not fit Fury’s career plans at this point.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Faces WBA Appeal Rejection Over Catterall
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is convinced Teofimo Lopez will not wiggle out of facing Jack Catterall. Matchroom holds stack after stack of written promises from the WBA guaranteeing the mandatory order stands.

Teofimo’s camp wants an exception so they can chase a unification scrap with Ryan Garcia. Hearn is betting the WBA refuses to play along, forcing Teofimo to either step into the ring with Catterall or give up the welterweight crown.

“Teofimo has pushed back and said, ‘We don’t think we should have to fight Jack Catterall. We’d like to try and make another fight,’” Hearn told iFL TV. “Basically, the WBA are going to say no because we’ve had multiple dozens of assurances in writing through the resolution.”

The WBA ordered the fight on September 22, giving the sides until October 22 to negotiate. That deadline does not guarantee a ruling on Teofimo’s request that day. Failure to reach an agreement could lead to purse bids, depending on how the sanctioning body handles the pending petition.

Hearn claims Matchroom holds ironclad written guarantees from the WBA locking in the Catterall defense, leaving him convinced the sanctioning body will shut down Teofimo’s petition to steer elsewhere.

“Teofimo Lopez will have the decision to fight Jack Catterall or vacate the belt,” he said.

Hearn knows Teofimo would earn more fighting Ryan, but says that doesn’t give him a pass to skip Catterall.

“I get it. It’s not a fight that pays you as much money as Ryan Garcia, but it’s a good fight that pays you a lot of money,” Hearn said. “Do as champions should do and make the fight.”

Right now, Catterall sits on hold while Teofimo chases the bigger fight against Ryan. Enforcing the mandatory would give Catterall clarity, but it might not actually hand him the fight he wants. Teofimo can still chase the Ryan fight, but Hearn says he’ll have to give up his WBA belt to do it. He doesn’t expect the WBA to let him keep Catterall waiting.

If Teofimo vacates his WBA belt, fans will not call it a shrewd business maneuver, though. Many will call it a duck. It becomes Ryan defending his WBC title against a challenger who showed the boxing world he didn’t want to face a Catterall, who fights a lot like Shakur Stevenson.

For the Ryan Garcia bout, it knocks a massive dent in the promotional luster. More importantly, it destroys Teofimo’s bargaining power at the negotiation table. Without a belt, Teofimo loses any claim to parity. Ryan will dictate the purse split, the ring walks, the poster placement, and the rules of engagement. The moment Teofimo drops the title, the event gets downgraded.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Celebrates Shakur’s Zuffa Departure Without Addressing Cost
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn called Shakur Stevenson leaving Zuffa Boxing an outright embarrassment, but he skipped over the core financial question. How much money was Zuffa supposed to put up for the matchups Shakur demanded?

Hearn openly questioned how any promoter could lock down an elite talent, only to let him walk without staging a single fight.

“How can you sign your most high-profile fighter and then he leaves you without even fighting?” Hearn said to iFL TV about Shakur.

Optically, that hurts Zuffa. Still, it does not mean holding onto Shakur made sound business sense.

Reporter Sean Zittel reported that Shakur sought at least $15 million per outing, even for a bout against Rayo Valenzuela, with an even steeper price tag for Devin Haney. Those numbers matter when evaluating what ended this partnership.

Hearn praised Shakur for walking away, hinting he could join Haney over at DAZN.

“Of course we’re going to dine out on it, aren’t we? Because they would do the same thing,” Hearn admitted.

The real test is whether Matchroom can satisfy that reported price tag. If Shakur sticks to those demands, Hearn faces the exact math problem Zuffa chose to avoid.

Bringing up Conor Benn’s paydays misses the point. Benn commands a massive following across Britain. Shakur has not shown that kind of commercial pull in America. Pure ring skill does not automatically generate the ticket sales needed to justify a $15 million purse before covering the opponent’s guarantee or card production.

Zuffa letting him walk says plenty about where they drew the line. The promotion simply decided the cost outweighed the return. Until contract paperwork surfaces, neither party holds the full truth.

Hearn can celebrate a rival stumbling all he wants. Actually signing Shakur fight by fight takes serious cash. If that $15 million asking price stands, someone has to absorb that risk, and Hearn hasn’t explained how he plans to make the numbers work.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Claims He Can Dominate Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster insists he has Emanuel Navarrete completely figured out ahead of their October 24 unification bout in San Antonio. Foster plans to outclass him, take his belt, and force critics to treat him like an elite name at 130 pounds.

Foster claimed he could turn this into a one-sided blowout if he simply sticks to the outside and picks Navarrete apart.

“I believe not only that I can beat Navarrete, I believe that I can do it in a dominant fashion, a super dominant fashion,” Foster said to Bradley’s channel. “I can make it an easy night and just box his head off.”

At the same time, Foster called this matchup a nine out of ten in difficulty and admitted it represents the biggest threat of his career. Navarrete throws wild, looping bombs from angles nobody learns in the gym. Foster insists none of that will rattle him. He points to past rounds with Rey Vargas, Robson Conceicao, and Jon Fernandez as proof that he knows how to handle height, awkward attacks, and long-range pressure.

Navarrete brings chaos, not textbook mechanics. Surviving separate elements from past opponents does not guarantee Foster can absorb the non-stop pressure Navarrete brings from opening bell to the final seconds. Foster cannot afford to run and let rounds slip away on activity alone.

He claims he wants to dominate, yet talking about an easy night while hunting for a highlight reel finish creates immediate risk. If Foster gets trapped between cruising on points and trying to look spectacular, Navarrete will make him pay with relentless volume.

“I’m looking to come in to make a statement,” Foster said. “I’m coming in to put on a dominant performance, show the world who I really am.”

Trying to invent power and aggression at age 31 against Navarrete is playing with fire. If Foster wants to leave San Antonio with the belts, he has to accept who he is, ignore the crowd, use his legs, and be content with a disciplined, ugly points win. Anything else plays right into Navarrete’s hands.

Foster has his sights set on undisputed status before jumping up in weight. Talking about blowing through Navarrete is bold talk, but a flat decision win will not deliver the respect he expects. Foster made big promises, and on October 24, he has to back them up against a puncher who never stops coming forward.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Plans His Own Promotional Company
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is launching DB Promotions to guide his own career once his contract with Sampson Lewkowicz wraps up in December. Even with the change, he intends to keep working alongside PBC and his existing inner circle.

Benavidez revealed his upcoming December bout marks the end of his decade-long deal with Lewkowicz. He treated the decision as a natural progression, making sure to acknowledge the promoter who helped build him into an attraction.

“This is the last fight on my contract,” Benavidez said to Brian Custer. “You know, I’ve honored the contract. The contract has been 10 years.”

Benavidez spoke carefully about the shift, never downplaying Lewkowicz while making it clear he is ready for independence.

“Sampson, he’s did a wonderful job,” Benavidez said. “He’s one of the greatest promoters of all time. But, you know, it’s just my time to do my own thing.”

When questioned about the venture’s name, he confirmed it will be DB Promotions, serving as his primary promotional banner starting early next year.

Stepping out on his own gives him significant leverage over the business side of his fight nights. Still, key details like equity splits, bankrolling, and operational responsibilities remain unstated, meaning the precise financial upside is impossible to calculate right now.

Putting his name on the banner gives Benavidez a chance to pocket more of the promotional money. That’s an obvious reason to make the move. But he still wants Al Haymon and TGB running the show alongside him. Having his own company won’t make the television money his, and he’ll still need those partners to get fights funded and dates booked.

Benavidez also aims to look past his own headline slots, expressing interest in signing boxers who train alongside him and his father, Jose Benavidez Sr.

“There’s a lot of great fighters I could take under my wing and put them under the promotion company,” he remarked.

Signing prospects gives DB Promotions life after Benavidez hangs up the gloves, yet building an actual stable turns a fighter into a financier. The expenses add up quickly with club show site rentals, airfare, hotel blocks, and purse guarantees that rarely turn a dime. Promoting his own headlining dates is one thing, but bankrolling young talent is a financial drain that devours capital long before a prospect ever sniffs a television date.

The move could let Benavidez pocket more of the money from potential fights with Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev or Oleksandr Usyk. But with Haymon and TGB still involved, putting DB Promotions on the banner hardly means he’s going it alone.

Sports.title: Lucas Bahdi Seeks Schofield Rematch Over Knockdown Calls
Sports.content:
Most Valuable Promotions has formally challenged Lucas Bahdi’s defeat against Floyd Schofield III, petitioning the WBA for an immediate rematch after claiming uncalled knockdowns cost their fighter the vacant lightweight world championship.

The promotional outfit submitted video footage alongside detailed documentation to the WBA following the October 10 clash in Chicago. MVP maintains that if the referee had correctly recognized and scored the disputed incidents, Bahdi would have emerged with a majority decision win instead of leaving the ring empty-handed.

Schofield took the vacant belt by unanimous decision, capturing wide margins on the official cards with scores of 116 to 110, 115 to 111, and a steep 119 to 108. Bahdi’s side now wants the sanctioning body to grant another title opportunity, arguing that multiple officiating blunders corrupted those final numbers.

“The video evidence demonstrates multiple significant officiating errors that directly impacted the outcome of the fight,” MVP said in its statement. “Our review shows that had these knockdowns been properly ruled and scored, Lucas would have won the WBA lightweight world championship by majority decision.”

That claim sounds bold on paper, yet MVP failed to provide the necessary receipts to back it up. The public release never identified which specific rounds contained the uncalled drops, nor did it offer an adjusted scorecard breakdown to illustrate how Bahdi overturned an eleven-point deficit on the widest card.

Rather than rehashing standard complaints about judges favoring the house fighter, MVP pinned the blame directly on the third man in the ring. The core of their protest argues that referee mistakes prevented the judges from scoring mandatory 10 to 8 rounds, skewing the overall totals.

“We have submitted our findings to the WBA and requested an immediate rematch,” MVP said.

Securing a second fight remains an uphill climb. A rematch forces Schofield to revisit an opponent he already officially conquered, and lodging a protest never guarantees the WBA will order the boxers back into the ring. The sanctioning body has not issued a ruling on the video review, leaving MVP’s victory claim as promotional posturing until officials deliver a verdict.

Sports.title: Does Oleksandr Usyk Need Daniel Dubois Again?
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois’ second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley gives Oleksandr Usyk another possible opponent for his farewell fight. It also raises a harder question: how much would Usyk gain by beating someone he has already stopped twice?

Dubois retained his WBO heavyweight title on Saturday in London, rebuilding interest in a third meeting with the unbeaten Ukrainian. Usyk stopped him in nine rounds in 2023 and five rounds in their 2025 rematch. Those results leave Dubois needing the fight far more than Usyk does.

At 39, Usyk is choosing how to finish his career rather than working his way toward another championship opportunity. He has already become undisputed champion at cruiserweight and heavyweight, with two victories apiece over Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury and Dubois.

That leaves a shortage of unfinished business.

A proposed Deontay Wilder fight would have offered a recognizable opponent Usyk had never faced. However, those negotiations have reportedly collapsed, with Fury and David Benavidez emerging as alternatives for a possible final appearance.

Fury’s appeal depends heavily on his December 11 fight with Joshua. A strong victory would give promoters something fresh to sell: Fury returning from that British heavyweight clash to take another run at the man who beat him twice in 2024. A defeat would make a third Usyk fight considerably harder to justify.

Dubois has strengthened his own case by stopping Wardley twice this year. Yet beating Wardley does not answer the technical questions Usyk posed in their previous meetings. Dubois would still need to show he can land consistently against Usyk’s movement and avoid being drawn into a fight where the Ukrainian controls the pace.

Benavidez would offer a different opponent and a fresh style, although his ability to compete with Usyk at heavyweight remains untested.

Usyk’s next fight needs more than a famous name or another belt attached to it. A Dubois trilogy would give the younger man a chance to overturn two defeats. The challenge for its backers is explaining why Usyk should spend his final appearance giving him that opportunity.

Sports.title: Artur Beterbiev Targets David Benavidez In Risky Cruiserweight Jump
Sports.content:
Artur Beterbiev wants David Benavidez next. He has spent over twenty months sitting on the sidelines, hoping for a trilogy clash with Dmitry Bivol that never materialized. Jumping up to cruiserweight offers a fresh target, but it also threatens to drag out his inactivity even longer.

Beterbiev dropped fresh training clips online this Monday, poking fun at his age while calling out the new division player. He joked about his physique looking like a man of forty-five, scaring people off. In reality, he sits at 41, turning 42 this coming January. That birthday will likely pass before he steps inside a ring again, especially since talks for a clash with Benavidez point toward 2027.

“Hope nobody was scared off by my 45-year-old physique,” Beterbiev wrote on social media.

Benavidez revealed the interest himself on Inside The Ring earlier this month. The former undisputed light heavyweight ruler reached out to his camp about meeting at the 200-pound limit. Benavidez sounded open to giving him the shot.

Chasing Benavidez hands Beterbiev a sensible target after the Bivol pursuit hit a wall. His February 2025 rematch with Bivol stands as his last sanctioned outing. Wasting nearly two years on that stalled trilogy took away precious championship time he can never get back.

The workout clips prove his muscle hasn’t vanished, but raw power was never the concern. The real test is sharpness under fire. Sitting idle chips away at reflexes, punch rhythm, championship stamina.

Benavidez brings relentless punch output that gym sessions cannot duplicate. Stepping up to 200 pounds also forces Beterbiev to show his heavy knockout power can hurt naturally larger men.

At the same time, Benavidez cannot sleep on the veteran. Beterbiev still carries sledgehammer power on the inside, creating real danger for anyone willing to stand in the pocket.

Sitting around waiting for Dmitry Bivol is pure career poison at this stage. Beterbiev is burning daylight he simply doesn’t have.

Turning 42 in January means every single idle month takes a bite out of his remaining sharpness. If the Benavidez camp can actually nail down a firm date for early 2027, fine, he can target that window. But if those talks drag out into vague promises or get pushed deep into the summer, Beterbiev cannot afford to sit in a training camp doing nothing.

The Bivol ship has sailed. Bivol went through back surgery, took other obligations, and showed zero urgency to jump straight back into a grueling trilogy war. Beterbiev spent the better part of two years holding out hope for that rubber match while his prime years slipped right out from under him.

If Benavidez isn’t locked in for Q1 2027, Beterbiev needs a stay-busy fight by late spring at the absolute latest. Even taking a mid-tier cruiserweight test to acclimatize to the 200-pound frame would do wonders for his timing. Heavy bag work and sparring with headgear can never replicate live incoming fire, especially against relentless combination punchers like Benavidez

Ghana News.title: 100 Black Men of Ghana holds free breast cancer screening for Osu residents.
Ghana News.content:
About 70 women and a man benefited from a free breast cancer screening exercise at The Trust Hospital’s Osu branch on Saturday in Accra.

The five-hour event, held under the theme "Health is Wealth," forms part of the 100 Black Men of Ghana's Breast Cancer Awareness Month programme.

The screening was hosted by Maurice Cheetham, CEO of Diaspora Bridge Consulting, who is considering a bid for the presidency of 100 Black Men of Ghana.

He was joined by the Adontemhene of Osu, Nii Nortey Nsuro Oquaye, who was among the key traditional leaders who played various roles to ensure the success of the programme.

Medical officers from The Trust Hospital conducted the screenings.

The event was supported by Diaspora Bridge Consulting, Jaleaa and Duncan's as partners and sponsors.

Beyond the health checks, the day was also family-friendly. Nii Nortey Oquaye donated a bouncy castle, which kept children entertained while their parents were being screened.

The turnout was significant as breast cancer remains a major public health challenge in Ghana.

Breast cancer is the country's most common cancer among cancer-related diseases. According to GLOBOCAN 2022 data from the International Agency for Research on Cancer, Ghana recorded 5,026 new cases and 2,369 deaths.

At the national launch of Breast Cancer Awareness Month this year, an oncologist at the Korle-Bu Teaching Hospital, Dr. Mary-Ann Dazie, puts the national burden at more than 5,000 cases and 2,695 deaths annually.

Health officials say over 80 percent of cases in Ghana are diagnosed at advanced stages, when treatment is more difficult, more expensive and survival rates are lower. Experts also note that most women diagnosed have no family history of the disease, making regular screening essential for all women.

Mr Cheetham said initiatives like the free screening should not be limited to awareness months but should run throughout the year to encourage early detection and save lives.

He disclosed that his team is preparing to consult with members of the diaspora who want to invest and give back to Ghana this December.

They announced that the next health outreach too will be held in Osu in partnership with Top Up Pharmacy at its new Osu branch opposite the Osu.

Nii Nortey Nsuro Oquaye said he is committed to building lasting relationships with the people of Osu to serve and protect the community.

Ghana News.title: Afenyo-Markin refiles defamation suits against Sammy Gyamfi, Eric Adjei
Ghana News.content:
Afenyo-Markin and Sammy Gyamfi

Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin has filed fresh defamation suits against Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi and National Entrepreneurship and Innovation Programme (NEIP) CEO Eric Adjei following developments in earlier cases involving the two officials.

The new suits were filed at the Accra High Court after an earlier defamation case against Mr Gyamfi was set aside over a defective writ, while a separate case against Mr Adjei was withdrawn at the Achimota Circuit Court before fresh proceedings were initiated.

According to a statement issued by Mr Afenyo-Markin’s counsel, F. Paa Kwesi Abaidoo, on Tuesday, October 20, the suit against Mr Gyamfi, numbered GJ/0045/2027, was filed on Thursday, October 15, 2026.

Mr Abaidoo said the legal team had complied with the High Court’s latest interpretation of the applicable rules, although it disagreed with the decision to set aside the earlier writ.

“Although we disagree with the High Court’s earlier decision setting aside our client’s previous writ, this new writ has been issued against the Defendants in accordance with the Court’s latest Interpretation of the rules,” the statement said.

The dispute with Mr Gyamfi stems from comments made during the Government Accountability Series, following Mr Afenyo-Markin’s criticism of GoldBod and its chief executive over alleged losses of $1.9 billion under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme.

The High Court last week set aside the Minority Leader’s earlier defamation suit against Mr Gyamfi on grounds that the writ was defective.

Fresh suit against NEIP boss

Meanwhile, Mr Afenyo-Markin has also filed a fresh defamation suit against Mr Adjei at the Accra High Court, hours after withdrawing an earlier case against him at the Achimota Circuit Court.

The new suit, numbered GJ/0061/2027, concerns alleged defamatory statements Mr Adjei made on Peace FM, according to the statement from Mr Afenyo-Markin’s counsel.

The earlier case was withdrawn following engagements between the parties. Counsel for the Minority Leader informed the Achimota Circuit Court of the decision, which was confirmed by Mr Adjei’s lawyer before the presiding judge struck out the case as withdrawn.

Speaking after Tuesday’s proceedings, Mr Adjei’s counsel, Gideon Koku Abotsi, said the withdrawal followed an appeal by the High Court judge for the parties to resolve their differences amicably outside court.

However, Mr Abaidoo stressed that the withdrawal did not amount to an end to the legal action.

“Following the discontinuance of the suit of Osahen Alexander Afenyo-Markin against Mr Eric Adjei, Chief Executive of the National Entrepreneurship and Innovation Programme (NEIP) at the Achimota Circuit Court this morning, a fresh writ, Suit No. GJ/0061/2027, has been filed at the Accra High Court this afternoon on the substantive matter of defamatory statements made by Mr Adjei on Peace FM,” the statement said.

The dispute with Mr Adjei arose after he repeated allegations of extortion against Mr Afenyo-Markin, following the Minority Leader’s criticism of GoldBod and Mr Gyamfi over the gold purchase programme.

The fresh filings indicate that Mr Afenyo-Markin intends to pursue his defamation claims against both officials. The allegations at the centre of the suits have yet to be determined by the courts.

Ghana News.title: NAGRAT accuses NDC of delaying action over Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations
Ghana News.content:
The President of the National Association of Graduate Teachers (NAGRAT), Jacob Anaba, has accused the ruling National Democratic Congress (NDC) of failing to act promptly on alleged abuse at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), despite claims that party officials knew about the matter before it became a national scandal.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Top Story on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Mr Anaba described the party’s decision to direct the school’s headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, to step aside from the Juaben Constituency Chairmanship race as “very, very late”.

He argued that action should have been taken when the allegations first emerged, rather than after the issue attracted widespread public attention.

Mr Anaba cited details he said were contained in an investigative video by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni, alleging that the Municipal Chief Executive (MCE) had visited the school at night to collect a girl who had reportedly been assaulted.

He said the housemistress had invited the student.

“So, the NDC was aware of the actions of this man in the school. So, they should have taken immediate steps to stop this thing when it started happening,” he said.

Mr Anaba accused the party of waiting until the allegations became a major public issue before responding, particularly after the headmaster had filed to contest the constituency chairmanship position.

“We cannot allow people like this to be in charge of our kids in our school. The school must be safe for all of our kids, boys and girls,” he added.

The claims about prior knowledge and the alleged assault have not been independently established in the information provided.

Mr Anaba also alleged that 38 teachers at the school, including a teacher who reported the concerns, were targeted for transfer by the district director following the events that led to the school’s closure in August.

He said the students were sent home on August 4 and a committee was subsequently established to investigate the matter.

According to him, the committee exonerated the headmaster after a few weeks of investigation.

Mr Anaba said the assistant headmaster later informed the teachers that the district director had directed their transfers.

“One of them is the focal person in the school who actually picked up this issue and made a report,” he said.

He added that the teachers remained at post while the issues were under investigation.

The NAGRAT president said some students had spoken to teachers they trusted about their experiences, while others had written letters to the district director, regional director and housemistress.

His comments add to calls for accountability over the handling of the allegations and for measures to protect students who report abuse in schools.

The Obuasi SHTS case has generated national concern, with 16 students reportedly alleging abuse involving the headmaster.

The Ghana Education Service (GES) has directed the Ashanti Regional and Obuasi Municipal Education Directors to step aside pending investigations. The headmaster remains interdicted, while the Education Ministry has directed the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) to investigate the allegations.

The NDC has also directed Mr Abdulai to step aside from the Juaben Constituency Chairmanship race while the matter is investigated.

The investigations are ongoing.

Ghana News.title: AG must not be seen as mouthpiece for political projects – Yaw Nsarkoh
Ghana News.content:
Former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has called for reforms to Ghana’s prosecutorial system.

The executive warned that the Attorney-General must not be perceived as a mouthpiece for the political agenda of the government in power.

He says the current arrangement, under which the Attorney-General is a member of Cabinet and appointed by the President, creates concerns about the independence of prosecutorial decisions, particularly in politically sensitive cases.

Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event in Accra on Tuesday, October 20, Mr Nsarkoh called for the establishment of an independent prosecutor at Cabinet-rank level or its equivalent to strengthen accountability and reduce the risk of political interference in criminal prosecutions.

He argued that the Attorney-General’s position within the Executive could fuel suspicions that decisions on which cases to prosecute, or discontinue, are influenced by political considerations.

“Our Attorney General (AG) is a member of cabinet, appointed by the president, living in that role at the pleasure of the president. He or she is usually, in a Santa Claus democracy, as partisan as they come,” he said.

Mr Nsarkoh warned that the arrangement could create the impression that prosecutorial powers are being deployed against political opponents rather than exercised independently in the public interest.

“ It is deeply important that no AG is allowed to look like a veritable megaphone of the contemporary incarnations of partisan political projects,” he said.

He maintained that such concerns could not be adequately addressed by relying solely on the personal integrity of individuals occupying the office, arguing that institutional reforms were necessary to safeguard prosecutorial independence.

Mr Nsarkoh stressed that the problem was not limited to a particular political party, saying successive governments had contributed to the wider governance challenges he outlined in his address.

He called for constitutional and systemic changes to protect the prosecutorial process from partisan influence and strengthen public confidence in the administration of justice.

His remarks formed part of a wider argument that Ghana’s democratic institutions need stronger safeguards against the concentration and possible abuse of executive power.

Ghana News.title: Yaw Nsarkoh questions judiciary’s use of contempt powers, calls for independent prosecutor
Ghana News.content:
Former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has questioned the judiciary’s use of contempt powers, arguing that the authority should not be used to discourage legitimate scrutiny of judicial decisions.

Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event in Accra on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Mr Nsarkoh said judicial authority, like any other form of power, must be subject to critical examination and accountability.

“If judges sit in court, and this happened, I'm not making it up, it's not AI, if judges sit in court and write into judgment that we have freedom of speech, but not freedom after speech, why on God's earth should we be unsure whether such wanton abuse of power can be described as professionally irresponsible?” he asked.

“Power corrupts; judicial power is power too,” he added.

His remarks questioned whether contempt proceedings could discourage public criticism of judicial conduct and decisions, raising broader concerns about accountability within the justice system.

Mr Nsarkoh also called for the establishment of an independent prosecutor at cabinet rank or an equivalent level, arguing that such an office could strengthen accountability for wrongdoing involving senior political figures.

He questioned the independence of Ghana’s Attorney-General, who is appointed by the President and serves as a member of Cabinet.

“Our Attorney General is a member of cabinet, appointed by the president, living in that role at the pleasure of the president,” he said.

He argued that Ghana needed a “really muscular” independent prosecutor capable of pursuing cases involving even the most powerful people in government.

The proposal forms part of his broader argument for institutional arrangements that can strengthen accountability and public confidence in the exercise of state power.

Mr Nsarkoh also criticised what he described as performative aggression within the legal profession and Parliament, questioning why disagreements among public officials often involve shouting and displays of hostility.

“Why is it impossible to turn down the aggression routinely shown towards each other? With so many lawyers ending up in Parliament, that orientation is carried into those chambers. Why must that be the case? Is it impossible to make laws without all this shouting and feigned acrimony we sometimes see?” he asked.

He questioned whether such conduct was beneficial to the mental wellbeing of public officials or conducive to serious deliberation.

Mr Nsarkoh argued that parliamentary and judicial institutions could conduct their work with greater restraint and respect without compromising robust debate.

“There are judicial and parliamentary cultures in the world that have moved past this performative boisterousness that we are normalizing in some aspects of our political culture. What we need is the will to learn from those and even our own history of governance, especially in traditional communities,” he said.

Ghana News.title: A state that can’t contain galamsey, now turning full aggression on ‘hate speech’? – Yaw Nsarkoh
Ghana News.content:
Former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has questioned the state’s approach to alleged speech offences, arguing that the apparent urgency in pursuing people over social media posts contrasts with its continued struggle to contain illegal mining.

He challenged the authorities to justify the use of state power against individuals over online expressions while galamsey continues to threaten water bodies, forest reserves and livelihoods across the country.

Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event in Accra on Tuesday, October 20, Mr Nsarkoh criticised what he described as the state’s misplaced priorities in addressing the country’s pressing governance challenges.

He said the authorities appeared unable to stop illegal mining but were willing to direct significant attention towards people who make controversial comments on social media.

“But what is happening when the state which cannot contain illegal miners, Galamsey, now turns its full aggression on people who make one impolitic post on Facebook?” he asked.

Mr Nsarkoh also expressed concern about what he described as the loose application of serious criminal charges in response to public comments.

“How can we rationalise these sometimes very loose uses of serious charges like treason?” he questioned.

His comments formed part of a broader critique of Ghana’s governance system, which he said appeared unable to address major threats to the country while becoming increasingly aggressive towards certain forms of public expression.

Mr Nsarkoh acknowledged the need for discipline in society and said reckless defamatory statements should be discouraged. However, he argued that such efforts must not undermine legitimate criticism or distract the state from more pressing national challenges.

“I am all for discipline in society and the discouragement of reckless defamatory talk. Democracy is not the same as disorder,” he said.

He warned that citizens’ legitimate concerns risk being ignored when the state focuses on punishing controversial expressions while failing to address problems such as illegal mining.

The former corporate executive further cautioned against a situation in which people become afraid to criticise those in authority, arguing that institutions that do not accommodate feedback and critical scrutiny risk stagnation.

Mr Nsarkoh’s remarks come amid wider national debates over the limits of freedom of expression, the handling of alleged offensive or unlawful speech, and the state’s response to illegal mining.

He urged a governance approach that balances lawful accountability with the protection of legitimate criticism and a stronger commitment to addressing the country’s persistent environmental and social challenges.

Ghana News.title: Judicial funding and operational reforms needed to speed up justice delivery – Yaw Nsarkoh
Ghana News.content:
The former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has called for improved resourcing and a comprehensive operational review of Ghana’s judicial system, arguing that adding more judges alone will not resolve the challenges affecting justice delivery.

He says the country must examine how cases move through the courts, identify the causes of delays and deploy technology and better planning to improve efficiency.

Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event on Tuesday, October 20, he said meaningful reform would require funding, but stressed that the management of existing resources was equally important.

Mr Nsarkoh cited what he described as Ghana’s limited capacity to finance its development priorities, arguing that the economy was too small to meet the competing demands of a population of about 34 million people.

He urged the involvement of experienced planners and operations managers in assessing the judicial process from beginning to end.

“We must get seasoned planners and operations managers to look at the end-to-end judicial process, with a view to optimising service to citizens,” he said.

Mr Nsarkoh suggested that professional bodies, including the Ghana Institution of Engineering and organisations representing project managers and planners, could contribute to the review.

He also questioned whether the large number of land disputes clogging the judicial system should prompt broader reforms in land administration rather than a response focused primarily on increasing the number of judges.

He identified other recurring disputes, including those connected to funerals and chieftaincy, as problems that society must address at their roots instead of continually relying on an under-resourced court system.

Mr Nsarkoh further urged the judiciary to embrace technology to improve its operations, arguing that properly deployed tools could expand institutional capacity.

He maintained that without adequate funding, systematic problem-solving and improved operational management, calls for judicial reform would remain largely aspirational.

Ghana News.title: Yaw Nsarkoh questions relevance of palanquin tradition, calls for cultural rethinking
Ghana News.content:
Former Executive Vice President of Unilever Ghana and Nigeria, Yaw Nsarkoh, has questioned the continued practice of carrying chiefs in palanquins, challenging Ghanaians to examine whether every cultural tradition remains beneficial in a changing society.

Speaking at a JoyNews and An Amalgam of Professionals event in Accra on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, Mr Nsarkoh said the practice illustrated the need to question long-standing customs and consider when modifications become necessary for progressive innovation.

He recounted watching a video of a chief dancing in a palanquin carried by young men, questioning whether the practice should automatically be defended as culture.

“Our larger society continues to allow young men to carry dancing chiefs on their heads in palanquins and call that culture,” he said.

He described the scene as an example of a tradition that, in his view, deserved closer examination.

“Why this manual palanquin is required in the final quarter of the 27th year of the 21st century is simply incomprehensible to me. But it is a useful illustration of what can go wrong when professions refuse to examine themselves critically,” he said.

Mr Nsarkoh’s remarks formed part of a broader critique of professional culture in Ghana, particularly what he described as the legal profession’s resistance to critical self-examination.

He said he had been fascinated by the profession’s attachment to ritual and tradition but was more concerned about rigid hierarchies and age-based discrimination.

“I am more concerned about the rigid hierarchy that comes close to a professional variety of gerontocratic feudalism, which is so brazenly on display sometimes,” he said.

He also questioned the practice of arranging court cases according to the seniority of lawyers, often justified on the grounds that junior lawyers learn by observing more experienced practitioners.

“That sort of thing in my view needs to be modified,” he said.

Mr Nsarkoh argued that technological advances could make it easier to schedule court cases in ways that allow lawyers to plan their work while creating more opportunities for professional development.

He said younger lawyers should have greater freedom to decide which experienced practitioners they wished to observe in court, rather than having their learning opportunities determined primarily by seniority.

“Age and experience must be respected, but by themselves they prove nothing,” he stated.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Kenya confirms ninth Ebola case amid concerns about regional spread
World.content:
A 24-year-old man, who was already being held in quarantine, is the latest to test positive, according to the Health Ministry.

Kenya on high alert amid concern over screening after first Ebola death

⁠Kenya has confirmed ⁠a new Ebola case, bringing the total ‌number of infections in the country to ⁠nine, amid an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), raising concerns about a regional spread.

A 24-year-old man, who was already being held in quarantine, is the latest to test positive, Kenya’s Ministry of Health said in a statement on Tuesday.

“He was isolated at the first sign of illness, tested and started on treatment immediately upon confirmation of his positive test result,” it said, adding he “was already in quarantine when he fell ill”.

The man was a close family member of Kenya’s first Ebola patient, who had travelled from the DRC, through Uganda and before arriving in Kenya and dying at a Nairobi hospital on ⁠October 5.

“All nine cases belong to one cluster, and as of ‌today there is no evidence of transmission outside this group,” Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Eight patients are stable and responding well to treatment, while 134 of 135 contacts have been traced and quarantined,” Amoth said.

Amoth said a milestone was in sight for the majority of the contacts in quarantine as they had remained well for the 21-day monitoring period and could return home from October 25.

It appealed to communities to welcome them back, saying they “pose no risk of infection”.

The ministry said no infections had occurred within quarantine facilities and that it was continuously monitoring infection-prevention measures to protect health workers.

Despite the nine infections, Kenya has not imposed restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings, with authorities saying the country remains open for business.



In the DRC, there have been more than 9,000 Ebola cases and 4,000 deaths since May.

The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control says it’s the second-largest epidemic on record.

It has been difficult to contain because there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo strain of the virus.

World.title: As Macron visits Gulf, can France forge its own energy-for-security future?
World.content:
Share As Macron visits Gulf, can France forge its own energy-for-security future? on social media

President Emmanuel Macron has arrived in Bahrain during his tour of the Gulf region, as France continues to reel from a wave of violent protests.

The French leader is hoping to strengthen defence ties and secure oil and gas supplies amid major disruption to global fuel shipments arising from the US-Israel war on Iran. He has already visited Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) as part of his three-day trip. His next stop is Qatar.

On the first day of Macron’s trip, France and Kuwait signed eight agreements and cooperation documents covering defence, artificial intelligence, investment and more.

Macron then met UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in Abu Dhabi on Monday. The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to advancing cooperation in energy, advanced technology and artificial intelligence (AI).

According to the French Foreign Ministry, the UAE is France’s biggest importer in the Gulf, with bilateral trade standing at 10.8 billion euros ($12.1bn) in 2025. According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) [PDF], France supplied 18 percent of the UAE’s arms and defence imports in 2025 – the second highest after the United States, at 42 percent.

But this isn’t all about simple trade.

Andreas Krieg, a senior lecturer at King’s College London’s School of Security Studies, explained that Macron’s visit to the region is “symptomatic of a much larger geopolitical transformation”.

“We are witnessing the gradual emergence of a post-American Middle East in which Washington remains militarily powerful but increasingly struggles to exercise the political leadership it once enjoyed,” Krieg told Al Jazeera.



“Europe and the Gulf now face a remarkably similar strategic challenge. Both have become excessively dependent on American security decisions, and both are discovering that this dependence carries substantial economic and political costs.”

An urgent need for energy

Most pressing for Macron is finding solutions for strife at home.

France has been engulfed in protests and violence over a proposed government budget seeking tens of millions of euros in savings to public spending. Protesters angry about the crumbling state of French schools and planned pay freezes for public-sector workers have taken to the streets in increasingly violent protests, and authorities have imposed curfews in some cities.

More than half a million people gathered across France on Saturday as protesters demanded better education infrastructure and government steps to address the cost-of-living crisis. During weeks of protests, more than 2,500 people have been arrested, and demonstrations have descended into looting and arson in numerous locations.

A major issue is the spike in energy prices affecting all of Europe – much of it as a result of the Iran war – which has also fuelled growing public anger in France. Disruptions to the supply of refined oil products such as petrol and diesel caused by the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz have caused up to 20 percent of French petrol stations to run out of both at various times since the conflict began.

Macron’s visit to the Gulf, accompanied by senior executives from France’s two biggest energy groups, TotalEnergies and Engie, comes as oil prices hover above $100 a barrel.

What France needs most urgently, therefore, is new suppliers. Those look to have been secured.

On Tuesday, the UAE committed to supplying 100,000 tonnes (746,000 barrels) of diesel per month to France for an unspecified duration, according to Bloomberg.

Bahrain has agreed to supply 100,000 tonnes of diesel per month for an unspecified duration, while Saudi Arabia will provide 95,000 tonnes in each of October and November, via TotalEnergies.

Cooperating on Gulf defence

Besides securing oil imports, however, France is also looking to boost its own exports, particularly of its defence equipment to the Gulf region, as the country suffers from record national debt – the highest level since the immediate aftermath of World War II, analysts say.

France has already strengthened its military partnership with Saudi Arabia, which has been battling the Iran-backed Houthi group from Yemen.



Last month, Macron said France would send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port of Yanbu, which is crucial for energy transport. Oil installations and airports in Saudi Arabia have come under attack from the Houthi group.

In late September, Macron said France would deploy what he termed “military means” to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Yanbu Red Sea oil terminal. Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, which carries oil from its eastern oilfields across the Arabian Peninsula to the Red Sea, has come under attack during the Iran conflict. It is the country’s main means of continuing to export oil while the critical Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted. But Yemen’s Houthis have also been attacking Saudi ships in the Red Sea.

Macron stated in a TV interview that “soldiers, radars, defence systems” would be sent.

While he did not give specifics about volumes, it was a move described by French newspaper Le Monde as marking “a geopolitical shift”, as defence cooperation between the two countries has previously been “discreet, ambiguous and marked by extreme caution when it came to defining it”, the newspaper noted.

Last week, France’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Pascal Confavreux, said again that “operational elements” to defend Saudi oil facilities had been put into action, without specifying which “military means” had been sent.

Meanwhile, on Monday, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot met with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud, to review bilateral relations and discuss regional developments. Barrot also reaffirmed France’s solidarity with Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks.

Krieg assesses that France can offer Gulf states generally something that has become “increasingly valuable”: military capabilities not entirely dependent on the US.

“France can offer defence industrial cooperation, technology transfers, joint production, training and greater operational autonomy,” he said. “For countries such as the UAE and Qatar, this means progressively reducing their dependence on American weapons systems, spare parts, intelligence and political permissions.”

Involved – but not too involved

However, Krieg cautioned that the “central strategic dilemma” for France is likely to be whether increasing its involvement in the region could draw it into the ongoing conflict.

“Consider the protection of Saudi energy infrastructure against Houthi attacks,” he said. “French air defence systems intercepting missiles would directly undermine the Houthis’ military strategy. If French forces are subsequently targeted, Paris could face pressure to retaliate. What begins as a defensive deployment could gradually become an operational commitment with much wider implications.”

Krieg explained that the same is likely to apply to naval deployments around the Strait of Hormuz, adding that “escalation in one theatre can rapidly affect another”.

France’s ties with Iran have already been strained over tit-for-tat diplomatic expulsions and political rhetoric against each other.



In July and August, France strongly condemned Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

In July, two French Embassy staff members were detained in Tehran and then declared personae non gratae. Iran’s Foreign Ministry said the diplomats had “interfered in Iran’s internal affairs under the pretext of engaging with civil society”.

In August, French Foreign Minister Barrot expelled two Iranian diplomats in retaliation.

A new regional security architecture

Speaking at the Global Security Forum in the Qatari capital, Doha, on Tuesday, US Envoy Tom Barrack said that Washington is moving away from its traditional security-for-oil relationship with the Middle East and no longer seeks to dominate the region.

“The US no longer wants to own,” said Barrack, who serves as US ambassador to Turkiye and special envoy for Syria. “The bargain is not to control, but to not leave. We’re not leaving.”

Barrack acknowledged that, following months of Iranian strikes on their infrastructure, regional partners are increasingly recognising the limits of US involvement.

Across the Middle East itself, defence partnerships have grown. In August, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed a trilateral security pact, also known as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement. The pact has been activated amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

But there may now be an opening for other external actors – such as France – to find more of a role.

Krieg said Gulf states do not believe France will replace the US, whose military and intelligence infrastructure remains “unmatched”. Rather, they want a “diversified network of security partnerships”.

“France is particularly attractive because it possesses genuine expeditionary capabilities and has demonstrated a willingness to defend Gulf partners without joining Washington’s offensive campaign against Iran,” he said. “Its military presence has consequently acquired greater political significance.”
