World.title: Turkiye moves to ratify Mecca defence pact with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
The trilateral defence pact between Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, also known as the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, has been submitted to the Turkish parliament for ratification.

The pact, signed on August 7, contains 16 articles, according to the document submitted to the Turkish parliament, seen by the Reuters news agency.

It aims to create a joint defence architecture in the region, in the case of an armed attack on any member, and lays out provisions in each article accordingly.

In Article 1 of the accord, for example, the signatories shall use “all necessary means” to eliminate threats to one another’s territorial integrity.

Once the first article is invoked, in case of an attack on any member state, the document lays out provisions for what follows next, as outlined in Article 2 of the draft seen by Reuters.

“In the event one of the parties is subjected to an armed attack or military aggression by another country or group of countries, the parties shall immediately provide assistance to the party under attack, utilising the full range ‌of mutual assistance measures available to them,” says Article 2.

This point is similar to Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty, NATO’s founding document, which treats an armed attack on one member as an attack on all.

Article 2 goes on to say that each signatory – Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye – “will decide on the scope and nature of the support to be provided following an objective assessment of the assistance required”, adding that the three countries will cooperate within their available resources, including military capabilities and resources.

Earlier this month, Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agreed to activate “deterrence measures” under the mutual defence pact and rapidly deploy forces to the Gulf kingdom to counter attacks by Yemen’s Houthis – an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God).



Articles 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the draft agreement, submitted to the Turkish parliament, also lay out details on defence industry cooperation, intelligence sharing, logistical support and joint training and the fight against “all means of terrorism”, including at the operational level.

Other provisions talk about joint research, development and innovation projects in the field of advanced technology and ensuring military readiness.

There is also mention of setting up a defence committee, which will include foreign and defence ministers from all three signatory states.

And there is a mechanism for allowing other states to join the agreement, with aspirants needing the approval of all three founding members.

The agreement will last 10 years, after which any country can withdraw according to the draft submitted to the Turkish parliament.

Next steps for ratification

Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar speaking on the submitted pact said the process of ratification is going to take “quite some time”, despite the ruling coalition needing a simple majority.

“The various political parties that are represented in the Turkish parliament are going to discuss the provisions in the pact, and we could witness heated debates because the opposition has its own objectives,” he said.

Serdar said even if the deal is ratified, it would not lead to a deployment of Turkish troops, a move which will require other legislative processes.

Turkiye’s parliamentary speaker will refer the agreement to ⁠the parliament’s foreign affairs commission. The commission could debate the ⁠agreement as early as Friday, according to a source who spoke to Reuters.

Once it is submitted to the commission, the contents and details of the agreement are expected to be made public.

“This strategic partnership developed between our countries aims to strengthen collective deterrence, enhance joint capabilities in the defence sector, and safeguard security and stability in our region,” Burhanettin Duran, the Turkish presidency’s communications director, said on X.

Duran added that the process marked an important milestone towards the “institutionalisation” of strategic cooperation between the three nations.

‘Ring of fire’

On Monday, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan spoke of the escalating violence between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis.

“As I often say, we are surrounded by a ring of fire. That is exactly the situation we face,” Erdogan said, while referring to the Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport.

In recent weeks, the Houthis have carried out missile and drone attacks against the kingdom, including oil facilities and Riyadh’s main airport, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the Yemeni government has launched air attacks on Houthi positions.

World.title: Macron lines up more Gulf diesel as France battles soaring fuel prices
World.content:
The UAE and Bahrain deals increase French commitments to 295,000 tonnes a month, just over 10 percent of consumption.

Share Macron lines up more Gulf diesel as France battles soaring fuel prices on social media

French President Emmanuel Macron has secured commitments for an extra 200,000 tonnes of diesel a month from the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, according to the French presidency.

The Elysee Palace announced the deals on Tuesday, before the president landed in Qatar.

His three-day Gulf tour, which also stops in Kuwait, follows a weekend of violent protests in France over the soaring cost of living, as the US-Iran war keeps energy prices high.

The presidency said the UAE had committed to about 100,000 tonnes a month, while a further 100,000 tonnes monthly would be secured during Macron’s visit to Bahrain.

Together with deliveries from Saudi Arabia, France now has commitments for 295,000 tonnes a month, just over 10 percent of its consumption, it said.

Kuwait has also given “very clear commitments” to deliver diesel and kerosene to the French overseas territories of Mayotte and Reunion in the Indian Ocean, the presidency said. The shipments will go via Oman to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

Patrick Pouyanne, the head of French oil giant TotalEnergies, who is travelling with Macron, said the deals would “reassure the French”.

“We are not going to run out of diesel in February,” he said, according to the AFP news agency.

Prices and supply

Andreas Krieg, a professor at the School of Security Studies at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera that France’s energy deals fit a wider pattern.

He noted that Gulf states have sent delegations to London, Paris, Berlin and Rome in recent months, seeking access to military complexes and possible stakes in European defence companies.



“They see a growing entanglement between their interests and European interests,” he said. “Not just in the energy field,” but also supply chains, he added.

Both sides feel pressure from a United States that is increasingly sidelining them, creating an opening to minimise dependence on Washington, Krieg said.

Macron’s agenda in Qatar includes discussions about security, defence, securing energy commitments to France, and advancing the frontiers in artificial intelligence, according to Sheikha Alanoud Hamad Saud Al Thani, a political analyst and fellow at the Middle East Council for Global Affairs.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, she said Qatar “really valued” its ties with France, which is one of the Gulf state’s oldest defence relationships.

“It comes as no surprise that the French are one of Qatar’s most important friends in Europe,” she said, describing Macron’s visit as “extremely consequential”.

“[Qatar is] leveraging existing relationships to adapt to this new kind of asymmetrical warfare, and we’re looking to see advancements in anti-drone and defence capabilities,” she said.

Impact of US-Israel war on Iran

Iran has blockaded the Strait of Hormuz, the main exit route for the Gulf’s energy exports, sending crude prices soaring during the eight-month conflict. Diesel has been among the hardest hit.

The G7, chaired this year by France, agreed earlier in October to draw up to 100 million barrels of oil from strategic reserves.

France has also released 10 million barrels of diesel from its own reserves, aiming to cut prices by 12 to 18 cents a litre, or about 5 to 8 percent, from next month, the French presidency said.

World.title: Marseille braces for more unrest after protests give way to 'apocalyptic' disorder
World.content:
Thunder and lightning have boomed across Marseille following the weekend's mayhem, illuminating the cracked windows and boarded-up doors of hundreds of businesses that were smashed as protests gave way to disorder.

France's second city saw some of the worst violence as chaos gripped the country on Saturday. Local business leaders say more than 500 premises were damaged, and the majority looted.

A police union boss told the BBC that the weekend had been an "apocalyptic" hell for his colleagues. 118 officers were injured, representing more than a tenth of the national figure.

So far, 101 arrests have been made in the port city, a quarter of them children.

But by Monday, it was police who were most conspicuous on the city's streets, not protesters. For eight hours, demonstrations and gatherings were banned in an effort to avoid a third consecutive day of disorder.

World.title: Man charged with attack on Australian MP as suspect's father says she is family friend
World.content:
A 43-year-old man has been charged after Australian MP Helen Haines was hit by a car in the state of Victoria on Monday.

The suspect will appear in court on Wednesday to face charges of dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official.

Local media earlier named the alleged attacker as environmental activist Brendan Nugent. His father and his partner said they had been friends with Haines "for more than 20 years" and thanked residents and officers who helped her after the "shocking and horrific crime".

Haines remains in a critical condition after surgery and is reported to have lost one of her legs.

"Helen Haines is a deeply respected, valued and much loved member of our local community," Rod Nugent and his partner Christine Cunningham said in a statement.

"All of our love and all of our thoughts are with Helen and her family and friends."

They promised to assist Victoria Police "in any way we can".

Police say they will allege the incident was targeted.

Haines, 65, the independent member for Indi, is in a critical but stable condition after undergoing surgery at a Melbourne hospital.

World.title: Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say
World.content:
Sudan's army has been accused of launching several drone strikes that have reportedly killed more than 300 people, including dozens travelling to a funeral.

The death toll from strikes in two areas of West Kordofan state on Sunday evening was 150, sources told the Sudan War Observatory, which tracks the conflict that erupted in 2023 between the army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

In Abyei, a disputed border area between Sudan and South Sudan, 153 people were killed when drones hit a market on Monday, the region's information minister said.

A military source told the BBC the army had carried out the Abyei attack, saying the market was a fuel supply site for the RSF.

The attack has raised tensions between South Sudan and Sudan, which jointly administer Abyei, as they both claim ownership to the oil-rich region in a dispute that has remained unresolved since South Sudan ceded in 2011.

South Sudan has summoned Sudan's ambassador to lodge a formal protest. There are fears the conflict could spill across the border.

World.title: 'Great result for Canada', says Carney as Alberta votes to reject separatism
World.content:
Prime Minister Mark Carney says an overwhelming vote by people in Alberta to remain part of Canada is a "great result" for the country.

Speaking to reporters as he walked into a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, Carney said he was "thrilled that Albertans have chosen unity" by rejecting a proposal to pursue separation through a binding referendum.

Preliminary results indicate more than two-thirds chose Canada over a push for independence for the province, according to Elections Alberta, external.

Monday's referendum was the result of a months-long campaign by separatists in the western Canadian province to get a public vote on the issue.

Provincial leader Danielle Smith welcomed the initial results, commenting: "Albertans have voted for a stronger Alberta in a united Canada."

Premier Smith herself opposed the separatist push but said the public will for a vote was undeniable, and many supporters of her own political party - United Conservative Party - were in the separatist camp.

Smith said she would address Albertans later on Tuesday on the path forward for the province.

In making the case for independence from Canada, many of the separatists said the oil-rich province's economic growth had been stifled by the environmental policies of Canada's central government in Ottawa.

But those who opposed a breakup - including Carney - called for Canada to present a united front in the face of external pressures, including an ongoing trade war with the United States.

"They've chosen to build together," Carney said. "They've chosen to continue to take care of each other, to move forward, to move forward together, with purpose, high ambition."

Carney added that he had spoken to Smith that morning and discussed "moving forward in the spirit of cooperative federalism, including on issues of immigration, other common priorities".

Over the past year, the prime minister has worked with Smith on a number of shared goals, including pushing for an oil pipeline to the Pacific coast.

World.title: North Korea publishes photos of Kim Jong Un - why do rumours of his death keep coming back?
World.content:
Kim Jong Un has appeared in North Korean state media looking remarkably healthy for a man rumoured to have died from a brain haemorrhage.

Photographs published by state newspaper Rodong Sinmun show the 42-year-old dictator touring what the paper said was a clothing and footwear exhibition with his daughter.

The images emerged hours after a Chinese dissident who lives in the US claimed, without evidence, that Kim had been taken to a hospital in Beijing in a coma and had died.

For those who watch North Korea closely, this kind of rumour has become almost routine.

In one of the world's most secretive states, facts are often difficult to verify, creating fertile ground for speculation.

This latest claim originated with Wanjun Xie, who identifies himself as chairman of the Chinese Democratic Party, a group banned by Chinese authorities. He has previously circulated unverified claims, including speculation about the death of Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

Xie alleged that Kim suffered a severe brain haemorrhage and was transferred to Beijing because North Korea lacked the medical facilities to treat him.

He claimed Kim later died and that his body had been secretly returned to North Korea, with the regime concealing his death.

Yet the photographs tell a different story.

Kim is seen examining displays, accompanied by Kim Ju Ae and his usual entourage of officials.

While there is no way to know exactly when the images were taken, there are other reasons to doubt the claim.

World.title: Why Israeli Gen Z voters are drawn to the far right
World.content:
More than half a million first-time voters will cast their ballots in this election, which many Israelis see as existential for Israel's future security and identity.

Polls suggest it will be a tight race, and the new young voters could help decide the result.

More than 16% are planning to support far-right parties - either Ben Gvir's Jewish Power or the Religious Zionism party of his far-right ally Bezalel Smotrich - according to a poll for one of Israel's most popular newspapers, Yedioth Ahronoth.

And almost three-quarters see themselves as "right or centre-right", according to another survey for Israel's leading Channel 12 television network.

"Itamar Ben Gvir gives me a sense of security," said 20-year-old Mordechai, one of the young fans accompanying the politician to Ramle.

"Like everyone in history, from Trump to Moses, there are slips of the tongue that are a bit less good. So what? 90% of the things by Itamar are amazing."

"Itamar will give us safety, and when we go to the army, someone will have our backs and be behind us," said 18-year-old Nadav.

"I think he's trying to show that we're a strong country. For many years, we couldn't show we're strong in our beliefs. We couldn't express our ideology."

Meir Schreiber, an ultra-Orthodox 23-year-old who grew up in London, said the Hamas-led 7 October 2023 attacks on Israel, which triggered the Gaza war, also convinced him that Ben Gvir was the right choice.

"Young people understand that peace isn't something we can do," he told me, "because what happens to you when you're young shapes your personality - we saw October 7."

World.title: Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast
World.content:
A South African woman has been killed in a shark attack off the country's east coast, in what is the first recorded such fatality this year.

Janine Lochrenberg was swimming off a beach in KuGompo City (formerly East London) on Tuesday morning when she was attacked.

Witnesses said the 65-year-old was bitten in two places and died before she was brought to shore.

Shark attacks are rare in South Africa, with about 10 fatal ones since 2012, according to the Florida Museum's International Shark Attack File.

Lochrenberg was out on a daily morning swim with her local open water swimming club when she was attacked at around 08:00 (06:00 GMT). Fellow swimmers brought her to shore, but it's believed she died before they could get her out of the water.

She was bitten on her thigh and her upper arm, one of her fellow swimmers told the BBC. They also said she had been wearing a magnetic shark repellent band on her ankle at the time.

Lochrenberg's sister Margot said she was holding her sister's head as they brought her to shore but believed she bled out in the water.

She told the BBC that her sister had "loved the water so much" despite knowing there was an "elevated shark presence in East London".

"She'd made peace with that. She had a deep affinity with the water and was a remarkable person," she said.

Barbara Briceland, Lochrenberg's partner, told the BBC the retired medical physicist was a good swimmer, who often swam far out into the breakers, and described her as very brave.

"She was highly intelligent, lots of fun, kind, in a quietish way, thoughtful, well-loved with a love of life."

Briceland added they were looking forward to retirement and were about to leave for a three-week road trip together.

Orient Beach, where the attack took place, has been closed alongside another nearby beach, authorities confirmed.

World.title: Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says
World.content:
The eldest son of Kenyan cult leader Paul Mackenzie, convicted of murdering 191 people, says his younger siblings were still being forced to fast as recently as two weeks ago.

Dan Mackenzie, 27, said he reported the case to police, who rescued eight children, including his five younger siblings from their grandmother's house, and took them to a rescue centre.

"They were basically forcibly fasted because they were denying food to them for almost three days," he tells BBC's Newsday.

His father was found guilty on Monday of murdering 190 children and one adult who starved to death in Shakahola forest, near the Kenyan coast.

He had ordered members of his doomsday cult to starve themselves and their children to death so they could "meet Jesus".

Twenty-eight other cult leaders were also convicted of murder.

World.title: Afenifere leader Reuben Fasoranti dies at 100
World.content:
The National Leader of the pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation, Afenifere, Reuben Fasoranti, has died at the age of 100.

Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa announced his death in a statement he personally issued on Tuesday, describing the late elder statesman as a patriarch whose life was defined by service to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria.

“On behalf of the Government and the good people of Ondo State, I commiserate with the Fasoranti family, the people of Akure Kingdom and the entire State over this great loss. May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace,” the governor said.

The governor said Mr Fasoranti’s counsel, fatherly guidance and principled positions on justice and good governance would be missed.

“His counsel, fatherly guidance and principled stand on issues of justice and good governance will be sorely missed. He lived a fulfilled life and left indelible footprints of honour and legacy for generations to come,” Mr Aiyedatiwa added.

Details later…

World.title: Senate considers increased funding for unity colleges, armed forces schools as bill passes second reading
World.content:
A bill seeking to amend the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act to strengthen the administration and funding of federal unity colleges and armed forces senior secondary schools has passed second reading in the Senate.

The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, announced the passage during Tuesday’s plenary after the bill received majority support in a voice vote.

After its passage, the bill was referred to the Senate Committees on Primary and Secondary Education for further legislative scrutiny and public hearing.

Sponsored by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, the bill seeks to strengthen the administration, coordination and funding of public senior secondary schools across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).

It also proposes a legal framework for direct government intervention to address infrastructure deficits and shortages of learning resources in public senior secondary schools.

Leading the debate on the bill, Mr Bamidele (APC, Ekiti Central) said the proposed amendments were intended to improve senior secondary education beyond the establishment of a national commission.

He said the bill seeks to promote transparent funding mechanisms, provide adequate infrastructure, and ensure qualified administrators are appointed in public senior secondary schools.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The significance of this Bill lies in its recognition that improving senior secondary education requires more than the establishment of a national commission. It requires effective institutional arrangements at the State and FCT levels, transparent funding mechanisms, appropriate infrastructure, qualified administrators and sustained coordination among the different levels of government,” he said.

Mr Bamidele said the proposed amendments would identify Federal Unity Colleges and Armed Forces Senior Secondary Schools for direct intervention to address their infrastructure and learning-resource needs.

“By identifying Federal Unity Colleges and Armed Forces Senior Secondary Schools for direct intervention, it also seeks to address the infrastructure and learning-resource needs of these institutions within the proposed statutory framework,” he said.

He, however, noted that the successful implementation of the proposed amendments would depend on clear operational guidelines and effective coordination between the commission and other relevant authorities.

He also stressed the need for transparent allocation criteria, effective monitoring and financial accountability to ensure the prudent use of public funds.

“The future of Nigeria depends substantially on the quality of education available to our young people. We cannot aspire to national development, technological advancement and global competitiveness without investing in the institutions that prepare our children for the responsibilities and opportunities of the future,” he said.

Mr Bamidele described the bill as a step towards strengthening the legal and administrative framework for public senior secondary education, improving access to educational infrastructure and enhancing accountability.

Debate

Most senators who contributed to the debate supported the bill, highlighting the need for better funding, improved school administration, and reforms to the secondary education curriculum.

The Senate Chief Whip, Tahir Monguno (APC, Borno North), said a coordinated, adequately funded secondary education system would strengthen Nigeria’s education sector.

He argued that the proposed amendments, if enacted, would help make education more accessible to Nigerians, regardless of their location.

Diket Plang, who represents Plateau Central Senatorial District, said the bill would promote uniformity in secondary school administration and standards.

Similarly, Ahmed Lawan (APC, Yobe North) called for a review of the secondary school curriculum to incorporate technology and Artificial Intelligence subjects.

Adams Oshiomhole (APC, Edo North) proposed sanctions for states with high numbers of out-of-school children.

Nigerian public senior secondary schools at a glance

The proposed amendment comes at a time when concerns about inadequate funding, dilapidated infrastructure, shortages of instructional materials, and uneven learning outcomes in Nigeria’s public secondary schools persist.

Although the federal and state governments have introduced policies and institutions to improve access to quality education, many public schools still struggle to provide conducive learning environments, adequate teaching resources, and the skills needed to prepare students for further education and employment.

A recent report by the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), Public Finance for Basic Education in Nigeria, identified chronic underfunding as a major factor contributing to poor access to education and weak learning outcomes. The report said government expenditure on education declined from 9.3 per cent of total government spending in 2015 to 3.6 per cent in 2023, well below the international benchmark of 15 to 20 per cent.

The report also highlighted significant learning gaps among enrolled students. In 2022, 86 per cent of pupils in Junior Secondary School 2 did not attain minimum proficiency in mathematics, according to assessments cited by UNICEF and the Universal Basic Education Commission.

In June 2025, the Executive Secretary of the National Senior Secondary Education Commission (NSSEC), Iyela Ajayi, said inadequate funding limited the commission’s ability to address infrastructure deficits, shortages of instructional materials, and gaps in human-resource development.

He said the commission had yet to receive the statutory allocation of at least two per cent of the Consolidated Revenue Fund provided for under the National Senior Secondary Education Commission Act, 2023.

The Act mandated the commission to prescribe and enforce minimum standards for senior secondary education and provide federal intervention to address infrastructure gaps in Federal Unity Colleges, the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. It also provides for a dedicated fund to support school infrastructure, instructional materials, laboratory equipment, teacher development and other educational needs.

Controversy over concession of federal unity colleges

The debate over how best to finance and manage public schools sparked controversy in September after the federal government decided to concede the management of King’s College, Lagos, to its Old Boys Association.

The proposed arrangement triggered opposition from education workers and parents, who raised concerns about the implications for public ownership, government funding, staff welfare and the future management of the country’s Federal Unity Colleges.

The dispute escalated when the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria (ASCSN) directed its members to boycott the resumption of schools for the new academic session. At the same time, parents and guardians also opposed the arrangement. The industrial action disrupted the reopening of Federal Unity Colleges nationwide.

The disagreement centred on the government’s plan to transfer responsibility for financing, rehabilitating, modernising, operating and maintaining King’s College to the Old Boys Association under a concession agreement. The Federal Ministry of Education directed the handover after the agreement concluded, with a transition committee expected to oversee the process.

The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, maintained that the arrangement did not amount to the sale of the school. He said the federal government would retain legal ownership and oversight of the institution and ruled out plans to sell or concede other Federal Unity Colleges. The government also assured stakeholders that the arrangement would not increase school fees beyond the applicable federal policy or result in the loss of teachers’ jobs.

However, the assurances did not immediately resolve the dispute. Following discussions between the government and organised labour, implementation of the concession was put on hold for a review of the agreement.

In late September, the ASCSN suspended its industrial action to allow a seven-member committee, including labour representatives, to examine the concession document and address the concerns raised by workers.

World.title: Reps order probe into corps member’s death at NYSC camp
World.content:
The House of Representatives has ordered an investigation into the death of a National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) member, Etimbuk Sunday, at the Corps Orientation Camp in Enugu State, following concerns raised by a lawmaker about the medical care he received before his death.

The resolution followed the adoption of a motion of urgent public importance sponsored by Unyime Idem (APC, Akwa Ibom), during Tuesday’s plenary.

The move comes after the Senate earlier called for an investigation into the incident, while the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) says it has begun investigating the death, including allegations concerning the medicines administered to the deceased.

Mr Daniel, the immediate past President of the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of Akwa Ibom State University, reportedly fell ill at the NYSC Orientation Camp in Awgu, Enugu State, in early October.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that he first visited the camp clinic on 7 October with symptoms suggestive of malaria or typhoid. He reportedly received treatment and was discharged with oral medication however, his condition subsequently deteriorated.

Moving the motion, Mr Idem, who is also the chairman of the House Committee on Public Procurement, said Mr Sunday died on 11 October after reportedly falling ill during his orientation programme.

He raised concerns about the treatment administered to the corps member, the subsequent deterioration of his condition and an alleged delay in referring him to a hospital for further medical attention.

He called for an independent investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the death and determine whether appropriate medical procedures were followed.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The lawmaker also raised concerns over reports that Mr Sunday’s body was handed over to his family naked and with visible bruises, describing the circumstances surrounding the release of the body as requiring further investigation.

He urged the House to ensure that the allegations were thoroughly examined to establish the facts, provide answers to the bereaved family and determine whether any wrongdoing occurred.

Following the adoption of the motion, the House mandated its Committees on Youth Development, Health Care Services, Police Affairs and Human Rights to conduct a joint investigation and submit their findings within four weeks.

The committees are expected to examine the medical care provided to Mr Sunday, the reported deterioration of his condition, the alleged delay in hospital referral and the circumstances surrounding the release of his body to his family.

World.title: Plateau revitalises 105 PHCs, upgrades two to cottage hospitals
World.content:
The Plateau State government says it has revitalised 105 primary healthcare centres (PHCs) and upgraded two facilities to cottage hospitals as part of efforts to improve access to healthcare, particularly in rural and underserved communities.

The Commissioner for Health, Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this on Tuesday at the 12th Plateau Council on Health meeting in Jos, the state capital.

Mr Ba’amlong said the improvements involved upgrading infrastructure, providing medical equipment and strengthening the healthcare workforce to expand access to essential health services.

He identified the upgraded facilities as Tudun Wada in Jos North Local Government Area and another facility in Wase Local Government Area.

According to him, the Tudun Wada cottage hospital has been commissioned and is operational, while the Wase facility is awaiting commissioning.

The commissioner said the interventions built on resolutions reached at the 11th council meeting in 2025, which focused on strengthening the state’s healthcare system in line with national priorities.

Healthcare workforce and insurance coverage

Mr Ba’amlong added that the government had strengthened the healthcare workforce following Governor Caleb Mutfwang’s approval for the recruitment of 1,300 healthcare workers across the state’s health sector.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He explained that 1,050 recruits were earmarked for PHCs, while 150 were designated for the Primary Healthcare Board to improve service delivery.

The commissioner further disclosed that healthcare workers had received training, while continuous workforce development remained ongoing to enhance professional competence and improve healthcare delivery across Plateau communities.

He revealed that enrolment in the Plateau State Contributory Healthcare Management Agency (PLASCHEMA) had risen to 320,000, helping reduce out-of-pocket expenditure and expand access to healthcare services.

Mr Ba’amlong also said that the state had developed an action plan to strengthen disease surveillance and improve data reporting for more effective health planning and responses.

He expressed optimism that the 12th council meeting would strengthen the healthcare system, promote efficient service delivery and establish future priorities for healthcare policies, programmes and reforms across Plateau.

Declaring the meeting open, Governor Mutfwang, represented by his deputy Josephine Piyo, reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to ensuring accessible healthcare for all residents, regardless of their circumstances.

He emphasised that healthcare should be considered a right rather than a privilege, pledging continued investment in PHCs revitalisation across the state’s 17 LGAs.

He reiterated the administration’s aim to ensure every federal and state ward had a functional, adequately staffed and properly equipped primary healthcare facility serving its population.

The governor pledged to expand health insurance enrolment, particularly among indigent and vulnerable residents, to ensure financial difficulties did not prevent people from accessing necessary medical care.

He further announced plans to recruit additional healthcare workers, while training opportunities and improved welfare packages would strengthen workforce capacity and support better patient care.

Mr Mutfwang stated that secondary and tertiary facilities were also undergoing improvements, including equipment upgrades, digitalisation of medical records and stronger emergency response systems to enhance healthcare services.

He revealed that Plateau State Specialist Hospital was being upgraded to serve as a teaching hospital for Plateau State University’s College of Health Sciences, requiring additional infrastructure, personnel and equipment.

The governor called for stronger partnerships with federal health authorities, development partners, nongovernmental organisations and the private sector, stressing that practical resolutions should guide healthcare policies, budgets and reforms.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that JUTH Chief Medical Director, Pokop Bupwatda, delivered the keynote address with the theme “From Policy to People: Consolidating Quality Universal Health Coverage and Health Security on the Plateau”. (NAN)

World.title: Keyamo approves design for Lagos airport monorail
World.content:
Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development Festus Keyamo has approved the design of a proposed monorail to link Ikeja Railway Station in Lagos to Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA) in the state.

The project is expected to connect the airport to the Lagos Red Line rail network, providing passengers and other airport users with an alternative to road transport.

Mr Keyamo announced the approval on Tuesday after a meeting with the managing director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), the permanent secretary of the Federal Ministry of Aviation and engineering teams from the ministry and FAAN.

In a post on X, the minister said the proposed line will have five stations, running from Ikeja Railway Station to the international airport’s Terminal 1, which is currently undergoing reconstruction.

He listed the proposed stations/stops as Ikeja Station, Domestic Airport Station, Beesam Station, Toll Gate Station and MMIA Airport Station.

“The monorail is an integral part of the reconstruction of the nation’s major gateway at the MMIA in Lagos,” Mr Keyamo said.

The design approval follows earlier announcements by the Federal Government about plans to extend rail services from Ikeja to the airport’s domestic and international terminals.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

In June, PREMIUM TIMES reported that the government was working with the Lagos State Government to extend the existing rail network to the airport and to expand connectivity.

Recently, Olubunmi Onabanjo-KukuFAAN’she managing directAN, said talks on financing the planned airport rail lint had reached an advanced stage.

Speaking at the World Aviation Festival in Lisbon, Portugal, on 18 October, Ms Onabanjo-Kuku stated that efforts were ongoing to finalise the project’s financing structure.

The planned link is expected to connect the airport’s three terminals to the Red Line as part of its wider modernisation programme.

The proposed rail connection forms part of broader efforts to upgrade facilities at the Lagos airport and improve passenger movement.

Terminal 1 of the international airport is undergoing reconstruction, while other infrastructure upgrades are intended to boost airport operations and the passenger experience.

The airport serves as a major gateway for international travel to and from Nigeria, making access to its terminals crucial for passengers and other users.

World.title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after 43 years
World.content:
CNN’s chief international anchor, Christiane Amanpour, has announced that she is leaving after 43 years of working with the network.

She announced this in a statement on Monday, saying she would end her programme, Amanpour, in May and leave CNN at the end of June.

This brings an end to her career, which began in 1983 when she joined the organisation as an assistant on its international assignment desk.

Ms Amanpour said she came to the decision to “separate” from the network “after many months of thought and a few sleepless nights”.

She wrote, “From my very first big exciting assignment covering the first Gulf war, to the horrors of the Bosnian war, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine and Iran and all the points in between.

“It’s the teams and the camaraderie that counted so much, as we together battled to seek the facts, the evidence and humanity, so that CNN could always broadcast the truth about the world and to the world, without fear nor favour.”

She also encouraged CNN, urging it to “Remember: always be truthful, not neutral.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Amanpour did not give a reason for her departure, nor did she specifically mention changes at her network.

Her decision comes at a notable time for the network, now part of a larger media conglomerate called Skydance, run by David Ellison and backed heavily by Larry Ellison, David’s Trump-donor father and Oracle co-founder.

In her statement, Ms Amanpour seemed to nod to concerns about the network’s future, saying that she “will always be rooting for CNN and maintaining its history of independent journalism”.

She has opened up about her ongoing treatment for ovarian cancer, which she was diagnosed with in 2021, calling it “the invisible killer.”

She also urged people to “get all the scans that you can.”

World.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case in Abuja, begins contact tracing
World.content:
Nigeria is on high alert after the federal government confirmed one case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Tuesday, 20 October 2026.

The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, is currently in isolation and receiving medical care at a private hospital in the FCT, according to a statement signed by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate.

Contact tracing has commenced, with 44 close contacts identified so far, according to the statement. The contacts include healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel contacts, while public health teams are identifying and monitoring people who may have been exposed.

“The FG calls on all public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to be on high alert. Healthcare workers must maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases, observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected cases to public health authorities,” it noted.

More details shortly

World.title: 2027: Plateau youth group unveils charter of demands for governorship candidates
World.content:
A youth group in Plateau State on Tuesday unveiled a charter of demands urging governorship candidates to prioritise job creation, security reforms and inclusive governance, with proposals to monitor their performance if elected.

The charter, developed by the Plateau State Youth Council (PYC) with technical support from the Youth Initiative Against Violence and Human Rights Abuse (YIAVHA), is based on a survey of 782 young people across the state’s 17 local government areas.

Titled “Plateau Youth Charter of Demands for Peace and Inclusive Governance,” the document outlines proposals on employment, peacebuilding, electoral participation and inclusion.

It seeks to ensure that young people’s priorities feature in candidates’ policy agendas and that commitments made during campaigns can be assessed after the election.

At a validation meeting held at the Youth Centre in Jos, the PYC chairman, Pannan Dafar, said politicians often relied on young people’s energy and ingenuity to win elections but failed to include them in governance after assuming office.

He said the charter was designed to give young people a common platform for engaging political aspirants and ensuring that their concerns informed government policies and programmes.

According to Mr Dafar, the document was developed through surveys, town hall meetings and community-level consultations, including efforts to reach young people without smartphones.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It also incorporates the perspectives of young women and persons with disabilities.

He said the council planned to organise town hall meetings with governorship aspirants after the charter had been validated by relevant stakeholders.

Unemployment tops the concerns

Unemployment emerged as the leading concern among respondents, with 57.7 per cent identifying it as a major challenge.

Farmer-herder conflict followed at 49 per cent, while drug and substance abuse was cited by 47.3 per cent.

The charter also reported that more than 55 per cent of respondents were either unemployed or engaged in precarious self-employment.

Respondents identified insecurity, limited access to capital, inadequate government support, and patronage in recruitment as major barriers to economic opportunities.

They urged the state government to expand employment opportunities, provide low-interest loans and seed grants for small businesses, modernise agriculture and agro-processing, and establish technology hubs and vocational centres to develop digital and technical skills.

The document also recommends targeted economic support for marginalised groups, including young women and persons with disabilities.

It calls for accessible public buildings, transport and information, alongside skills-development programmes and stronger protection against gender-based violence and sexual harassment.

Youths seek security reforms

The charter identifies unemployment, farmer-herder violence, drug abuse, intercommunal conflict and religious tensions as major threats to peace and security in Plateau State.

It reported that 68.7 per cent of respondents supported a shift from exclusively centralised security financing towards grassroots mechanisms.

The youths called for greater investment in community-led security structures, dedicated budgetary allocations for youth-led peacebuilding and early-warning systems, and formal youth representation in security committees at community, local government and state levels.

The document also proposes a task force on substance abuse that would combine rehabilitation, civic education and law enforcement.

The recommendations seek to give young people a more active role in identifying security threats, preventing violence and supporting peacebuilding efforts in their communities.

68% dissatisfied with youth participation in governance

The survey found that 68.2 per cent of respondents considered the existing level of youth participation in governance unsatisfactory, while 31.8 per cent rated it as good or very good.

Respondents said young people often lacked access to decision-makers and were excluded from policy formulation, employment planning and local government decision-making.

They called for guaranteed youth representation in the development of youth programmes, security policies, employment initiatives and other decisions affecting their communities.

Nan’akyen Yarima, a participant at the meeting, criticised what she described as a pattern in which politicians mobilised young people during elections but abandoned their interests after securing office.

She said young Nigerians remained inadequately represented in governance despite constituting a significant proportion of the country’s population.

“This government is not youth friendly, is not youth inclusive,” she said, describing the charter as an opportunity to ensure that young people participated in shaping policies affecting their future.

The document also identifies political violence, vote-buying, elite manipulation, economic vulnerability and ethnic or religious mobilisation as threats to peaceful electoral participation.

It calls for sanctions against electoral violence, hate speech and misinformation, as well as reductions in nomination fees and other barriers that discourage young people from contesting elections.

SPRING team leader backs initiative

Okoha Ukiwo, team leader of the Strengthening Peace and Resilience in Nigeria (SPRING) programme, described the charter as an important instrument for ensuring that young people’s interests were considered in political and governance decisions.

He said the initiative would enable young people to communicate their priorities to political aspirants and assess candidates based on their responses.

“Unless you make your position known, your position will not be known, and your interests will not be taken into consideration in politics and in governance,” Mr Ukiwo said.

He commended the PYC for using research to identify young people’s concerns and translate them into demands for political leaders.

Mr Ukiwo said the initiative reflected practices in established democracies, where citizens organise around policy priorities and use them to assess candidates before voting.

He expressed hope that the approach would influence voting decisions in Plateau and encourage similar initiatives among young people across Nigeria.

Charter proposes monitoring mechanism

Jacob Pwakim, executive director of YIAVHA, said the charter would provide measurable indicators for assessing the commitments of political candidates and parties.

He said youth organisations had often mobilised supporters during elections without establishing a framework for evaluating what politicians subsequently delivered.

“This time around, the Plateau Youth Council have developed a document that will shape conversations for now and for the future,” Mr Pwakim said.

He added that the charter would allow young people to assess politicians against the commitments they made before the elections.

“Once you’ve made the commitment and you win the elections, we’ll come and assess you and your political party by these key performance indicators that we’ve set out in this,” he said.

Mr Pwakim said YIAVHA supported the initiative under its Building Bridges for Peace project, funded through SPRING with support from the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

To ensure that the demands are not abandoned after the elections, the charter proposes a multi-sectoral implementation committee comprising government ministries, departments and agencies, civil society organisations, youth groups, peacebuilding structures, organisations of persons with disabilities, faith-based networks and development partners.

The proposed committee would monitor compliance with commitments made by elected officials throughout the 2027–2031 administration.

ALSO READ: Plateau youth council backs creation of state police

Other recommendations include statutory youth representation on state boards and planning committees; an independent Plateau Youth Advisory Council reporting to the governor; biannual government-youth dialogues; and platforms for civic feedback.

The charter also calls for young people’s participation in budget consultations to ensure that public spending reflects their priorities.

These mechanisms remain proposals in the charter and would require action by the relevant authorities and stakeholders to become operational.

PYC plans national expansion

The PYC said it intended to take the initiative to the National Youth Council of Nigeria to encourage the development of a similar framework reflecting the needs of young people nationwide.

Mr Dafar also expressed concern about the condition of the state Youth Centre and other youth facilities, describing their state as evidence of what he considered years of inadequate attention to youth development infrastructure.

He said the council would pursue engagement with governorship aspirants to secure commitments on the charter ahead of the 2027 election.

The initiative seeks to move youth advocacy beyond election campaigns by establishing a sustained mechanism through which young people can influence policies, monitor elected officials and demand accountability.

World.title: 2027: Wike’s political calculations have shaped Rivers politics — APC chieftain
World.content:
Wike

Dike hails rapprochement with Fubara

By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt

A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Princewill Dike, has described the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, as the “political Chike Obi of Rivers State,” citing his political calculations, strategic manoeuvres and ability to win elections.

Dike, a Port Harcourt-based lawyer and political commentator, said on Tuesday that Wike had demonstrated an understanding of Rivers politics, adding that his influence and ability to build political alliances had continued to shape the state’s political landscape.

Dike recalled that in 2014, he watched a television appearance on the African Independent Television (AIT) in which former Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Henry Odein Ajumogobia, SAN, reportedly expressed interest in contesting the 2015 Rivers State governorship election on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), with the expectation that Wike would support his ambition.

According to Dike, Ajumogobia was said to have withdrawn from the race after Wike declared his governorship ambition, reportedly acknowledging Wike’s political understanding as comparable to his own knowledge of the law.

Dike said the episode reinforced his conviction that Wike possessed an uncommon grasp of political strategy, which distinguished him among political actors in Rivers State.

He recalled that following Wike’s victory over the political camp of former Governor Rotimi Amaechi in the 2015 governorship election, he described the FCT minister as the political “wizard of Rivers State”, a nickname he said reflected Wike’s political influence and strategic approach.

Dike said the description of Wike as the political Chike Obi of Rivers State was also appropriate, given what he characterised as the minister’s “ingenious political permutations, calculations and ability to navigate complex political situations”.

His latest assessment followed developments involving Wike, Governor Siminalayi Fubara and their respective supporters, whom he described as an extended family of political stakeholders in the state.

Dike welcomed the apparent rapprochement between the two political leaders and their supporters, describing it as a significant step towards reconciliation and unity in Rivers State.

The APC chieftain attributed Wike’s continued political relevance not only to his strategic calculations but also to what he described as his generosity and willingness to forgive former political associates with whom he had disagreements.

According to him, Wike’s reported readiness to welcome former adversaries back into his political fold without dwelling on past disagreements had helped him sustain relationships and consolidate his influence.

Dike, who has consistently advocated political reconciliation in Rivers State, said the latest development supported his earlier position that the disagreements would eventually give way to renewed cooperation.

He expressed hope that the development would create an opportunity for political stakeholders to work together and usher in a period of greater understanding and cooperation in the state.

“The development is the beginning of a new political chapter in Rivers State. The apparent rapprochement had given me reasons to celebrate. Rivers State is now moving towards becoming one political family,” he said.

Dike also praised Wike’s willingness to forgive former associates, navigate political challenges and rebuild relationships, arguing that these qualities had contributed to his standing in Rivers politics and his description of the minister as the “father of Rivers politics”.

World.title: Presidential Panel submits National Policing Draft, 29 Amendment Bills to Justice Ministry
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — THE Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill has concluded the drafting phase of its assignment and formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), alongside 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative review and validation.

The submission was made on Monday, 19th October, 2026, to the Attorney General of the Federation, AGF and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan.

This was revealed via a statement issued by the Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Rt. Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila.

Gbajabiamila, who was a former Speaker of the House of Representatives, explained that the Ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws.

According to the statement: “The Ministry of Justice is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026. The Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate.

“The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.”

He further said: “The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly.

“The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.”

World.title: Presidency targets ₦20bn to tackle climate change in North West, holds summit in Abuja
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — THE Presidency on Tuesday said it is seeking to mobilise about ₦20 billion over the next four years to confront flooding, drought, desertification, migration and other climate pressures across the region.

This is as the North-West Climate Summit has been described as Africa’s first regional climate marketplace.

Senior Special Assistant to the President on Community Engagement (North-West), Hon. Abdullahi Tanko Yakasai, said the summit is the inaugural edition of a regional platform designed to connect states and local governments with development partners, financial institutions and investors.

The initiative is being implemented with the Northern Governors’ Forum, the North-West Governors’ Forum and the North-West Development Commission.

Yakasai said the summit rests on three pillars: a Climate Marketplace, a Climate Academy and a Climate Fund.

He explained that the marketplace will allow subnational governments to showcase climate programmes and attract partnerships and financing from local and international institutions.

“Local governments and states can go into that platform and put up what they are doing on climate change, so that international development partners, international financial institutions, and even the local ones can see what programmes they are doing on climate,” he said.

He explained that the Climate Academy is expected to train 10,000 young people across the North-West on climate resilience, climate action and related areas.

According to him, the Climate Fund will channel resources towards interventions on flooding, drought, renewable energy and other climate-related challenges.

“That fund will be channelled through the Office of the SSA on Community Engagement to tackle those issues,” Yakasai said.

The presidential aide said organisers are targeting about N20 billion over the next four years to support climate interventions in the region.

“We are looking at the region of N20 billion in the next four years,” he said. “All these are aimed at easing the problems of climate, because this is what is bedevilling the whole world.”

He said the initiative builds on work that began last year and is intended to strengthen Nigeria’s position ahead of the forthcoming United Nations Climate Change Summit.

“We want to take up what we have gotten here, the discussions we have had here, because we have had a lot of interactive sessions,” Yakasai said.

“We take it up and see where we can match our strength with what we can see at the international climate change summit that is coming up.”

Yakasai identified flooding, migration, drought, dry-season pressures and the need for renewable energy as major challenges facing the North-West.

“Anything that has to do with climate challenge, we focus on it and see how we can help in alleviating those challenges,” he said.

The summit is positioned as an investment-focused platform for climate-resilient agriculture, renewable energy, water security and youth-led green enterprises across Kaduna, Kano, Jigawa, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara states.

Yakasai said the regional approach is significant because it moves climate action beyond individual state projects into a coordinated platform for financing, capacity-building and implementation.

The seven states of the North West Kano, Kaduna, Kebbi, Katsina, Sokoto, Jigawa and Zamfara states sent their representatives.

World.title: Otti, Wabara mourn Prof Greg Ibe, Uduaghan
World.content:
Otti

Gregory University declares seven days of mourning for founder

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, and former Senate President, Senator Adolphus Wabara, have mourned the deaths of Professor Gregory Ikechukwu Ibe, founder of Gregory University, Uturu, and former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan.

Otti and Wabara described Ibe’s death as a major loss to Abia State and Nigeria, while Wabara also paid tribute to Uduaghan’s contributions to governance and public service.

Their tributes came as Gregory University declared seven days of mourning in honour of its founder and proprietor, who died following health challenges.

Ibe, a professor of entrepreneurial management and the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) governorship candidate in the 2023 election, was also a recipient of the national honour of Officer of the Order of the Federal Republic (OFR).

In a condolence message issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Publicity, Ferdinand Ekeoma, Otti said he received the news of Ibe’s death with shock and sadness, recalling his contributions to education and research, particularly in Abia State.

The governor said he had hoped and prayed that the late professor, who had battled an illness for some time, would recover.

“Unfortunately, he couldn’t. We cannot question God,” Otti said.

He urged the deceased’s family, friends and associates to draw strength from the life he lived and the legacies he left behind, appealing to them not to “mourn like those without hope”.

On behalf of his family, the Abia State Government and the people of the state, Otti commiserated with the bereaved family and prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul.

Wabara: Abia, Ndigbo lost a rare gem

Similarly, Wabara described Ibe’s death as a monumental loss to Abia State, Ndigbo and Nigeria, saying the late professor was one of Abia’s finest personalities whose impact on society would endure.

Wabara said he received the news of Ibe’s demise with rude shock and utter disbelief, adding that his contributions to education, philanthropy and human development, as well as his positive impact on countless lives, would remain legendary.

He said the late university founder would also be remembered for his advocacy and strong belief in the Abia Charter of Equity, which promotes power rotation in the interest of fairness and justice.

The former Senate President regretted that Ibe died at a time when his services and presence were still needed, particularly as Abia continued its quest for development.

He prayed God to grant the bereaved family the strength and fortitude to bear the loss.

University declares seven days of mourning

Meanwhile, Gregory University has declared seven days of mourning for its founder, describing his death as a major loss to the university community and the education sector.

In a statement signed by the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Cele Njoku, on behalf of the university management, the institution recalled that Ibe was the driving force behind its establishment in 2012 and remained committed to expanding access to education, particularly for less-privileged Nigerians.

As part of the mourning arrangements, the university directed that all flags on its campus be flown at half-mast.

It also opened condolence registers at the Vice-Chancellor’s Office in the Senate Building and at its liaison offices in Abuja and Lagos.

The management further announced the suspension of social and sporting activities, including preparations for the second ASTEF Torch Run.

It appealed to Nigerians, parents, students, alumni, the National Universities Commission and the wider academic community to pray for the peaceful repose of Ibe’s soul and for strength for his immediate family and the university community.

The late professor is survived by six children and seven grandchildren. The university said funeral arrangements would be announced in due course, in line with the position of his royal family.

Wabara mourns former Delta governor, Uduaghan

In a separate condolence message, Wabara, who is the Chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), mourned the death of Uduaghan, describing it as a painful loss to Delta State, the South-South region and Nigeria.

The former Senate President said Uduaghan’s contributions to governance and public service would remain part of his enduring legacy, noting that his death would be deeply felt by his family, political associates and the people of Delta State.

Wabara said Uduaghan made indelible marks as governor of Delta State under the PDP.

He extended his sympathies to the Uduaghan family and the government and people of Delta State, praying God to grant the bereaved family the strength to bear the loss and grant the deceased eternal rest.

World.title: 2027: Atiku’ll cut cost of living, revive Eastern ports — Akobundu
World.content:
Senator inaugurates grassroots support group in two Abia LGAs

By Steve Oko

UMUAHIA — Senator Austin Akobundu, Director-General and Campaign Manager of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign for former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, has said an Atiku presidency would reduce the cost of living, revive the economy and reactivate the Eastern maritime port corridor.

Akobundu spoke during the inauguration of the Atiku/Akobundu Vanguard, a grassroots support group, in Osisioma Ngwa and Isiala Ngwa North Local Government Areas of Abia State.

He blamed the economic hardship in the country on the policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration, arguing that Atiku had the experience and economic blueprint to reverse the trend.

According to him, Atiku’s proposed targeted and transparent fuel subsidy would help reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices of food, housing, education and other essential goods and services.

“President Tinubu’s policies have pushed Nigerians into unprecedented hardship and made us the poverty capital of the world,” Akobundu said.

He added, “But Atiku Abubakar comes with the experience, compassion and competence to reverse this decline. He will make Nigeria affordable, productive and respected again.”

The senator also identified the reactivation of the Eastern maritime port corridor as a key component of Atiku’s proposed economic agenda for the South-East.

He said reviving the corridor would expand access to international trade, stimulate industrial activity, create jobs and strengthen the region’s economic base.

“Atiku has a clear, actionable plan to revive the economy of the South-East alongside every other region. With the Atiku Abubakar/Rotimi Amaechi ticket, no region will be left behind,” he said.

Akobundu described Atiku as a detribalised leader with the experience and national outlook required to unite the country, adding that his appointment as campaign director-general reflected the former vice-president’s commitment to inclusiveness.

The inauguration attracted ADC leaders, party candidates, community elders, youth groups, women leaders and grassroots mobilisers from the two local government areas and other parts of Abia Central.

Akobundu highlights constituency projects

The senator, who is also the ADC candidate for Abia Central Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, used the occasion to highlight his legislative and constituency interventions in Osisioma Ngwa and Isiala Ngwa North.

On legislation, he cited bills seeking the establishment of a Federal Institute of Entrepreneurship and Technical Skills Development in Osisioma and a National Sports University at Nsulu in Isiala Ngwa North.

He also listed youth empowerment initiatives, including free training for more than 400 secondary school students in robotics, artificial intelligence and embedded systems engineering.

Other programmes, according to him, included digital skills training for 360 youths, training for 400 youths in cosmetics production and paint-making, and support for 100 youths trained in farming and tailoring.

He said beneficiaries of the farming and tailoring programme received sewing machines, start-up kits and financial support, while those trained in cosmetics production and paint-making received cash grants to establish businesses.

In education, Akobundu said he had paid ₦21 million in scholarships for 113 constituents at the Nigeria Teachers Institute, while 114 students in tertiary institutions received grants of ₦200,000 each.

He also cited medical outreaches, the installation of solar streetlights in markets across the two local government areas, solar-powered boreholes and school renovation projects among his interventions.

The projects, he said, included the renovation of Immaculate Girls’ Secondary School and the construction of a skills acquisition centre. He added that work was ongoing on a classroom block at Ntigha Primary School.

He listed the completion of Ihie Health Centre, renovation of Obikabia and Mbubo primary schools, and electrification of Isiala Amapu Ntigha Autonomous Community among projects planned for the future.

Woos Osisioma stakeholders

Akobundu and his entourage later visited political leaders and other stakeholders from Osisioma Ngwa at the residence of Chief Solomon Adaelu, where he sought their support for Atiku’s presidential ambition and his own senatorial bid.

He described Osisioma Ngwa as a politically significant local government area whose voting strength could influence electoral outcomes in Abia State.

The senator said he was addressing the stakeholders in three capacities: as the senator representing Abia Central, director-general of the ADC/Atiku Abubakar Presidential Campaign Council and the party’s candidate for the senatorial district in the forthcoming elections.

He urged the stakeholders to support Atiku, expressing confidence that the former vice-president could steer the country away from its current economic difficulties.

Those present included the Director-General of the Akobundu Campaign Council, Elder Sam Njoku; members of the campaign team; ADC candidates in the two local government areas; and associates of the senator.

World.title: Police arrest six suspected robbers in Jigawa
World.content:
police badge

By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested six suspected members of an armed robbery gang allegedly responsible for attacks on residents of Jahun Local Government Area, during which cash, mobile phones and other valuables were stolen.

The command’s Public Relations Officer, SP Lawan Shiisu Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday.

He said the arrests followed investigations into two armed robbery incidents reported in Jahun on September 24, 2026.

According to him, the gang invaded the residence of a 35-year-old man in Kofar Daru Quarters at about 2 a.m., stealing ₦20.18 million in cash, iTel mobile phones valued at ₦13.13 million, recharge cards worth ₦1 million, Android phones and other valuables.

He added that the suspects also attacked the residence of a 37-year-old man in Shagari Quarters, where they allegedly stole ₦45,000, two blankets, rice and a woman’s wrapper.

Shiisu said detectives from the Jahun Police Division launched an investigation that led to the arrest of five suspects.

He identified them as Sale Ibrahim, 25; Abubakar Abdullahi, 28; Babangida Ya’u, 35; Babannan Hassan, 27; and Isah Isibu, 35.

The police spokesperson said another breakthrough was recorded on October 15, 2026, when operatives of the Maigatari Police Division, in collaboration with the Border Patrol Team, arrested a sixth suspect during a routine patrol at Maigatari Market.

The suspect, identified as Isa Yusuf, 35, from Hantsu village in Miga Local Government Area, was allegedly found with 13 new iTel mobile phones, 13 chargers, 13 batteries and ₦102,500 in cash.

Shiisu said the suspect was transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Dutse for further investigation.

According to him, Yusuf confessed during interrogation to being a member of the gang involved in the Jahun robbery incidents.

He added that further investigations linked the recovered mobile phones and other items to property allegedly stolen during the attacks.

The police spokesperson said all six suspects had been charged to court, while efforts were ongoing to apprehend other fleeing members of the gang and recover the remaining stolen property.

World.title: 2027: Nigeria bigger than APC, ADC, NDC, others – Jonathan
World.content:
Former president Goodluck Jonathan

Warns that political office is temporary, but its consequences can shape generations

As FFDGN Chairman Tackles Nigerian Leaders, Says Power Without Character Destructive

Ganduje faults self-serving defections

Growing disconnect between government policies and citizens’ everyday experiences had weakened public trust, Okowa

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA- AHEAD of 2027 Presidential and general elections, former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned politicians that as they politics, they must place national interest above party loyalty and sectional considerations, declaring that Nigeria is greater than any political party and politician in the country.

According to Jonathan, Politicians must know that politics can only be played when there is a peaceful Nigeria, stressing that the country is bigger than thr ruling All Progressives Congress, APC; the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC; the Action Democratic Congress, ADC and other political parties.

Speaking yesterday at the 5th National Conference of the Forum of Former Deputy Governors of Nigeria in Abuja, the former President who called for national unity, stronger democratic institutions and greater commitment to good governance, said that former deputy governors have a responsibility to deploy their experience in order to promote national development.

The conference, which runs from October 20 to 21, is themed, “Rethinking Nation-Building: Bridging the Leadership-Citizen Disconnect Through Orientation, Attitude, Character, Culture and Tradition Towards Sustainable Development.”

Jonathan who was represented by a former Adamawa State Deputy Governor, Bala Ngilari, warned that ethnic, religious and regional divisions remained major obstacles to Nigeria’s political development, just as he reminded all that political office is temporary, but its consequences can shape generations, making it imperative for former public office holders to guide emerging leaders on integrity, accountability and responsible leadership.

He expressed optimism about Nigeria’s future, citing the resilience and creativity of its people, particularly young Nigerians, whom he said needed opportunities to work, innovate and prosper.

He said, “One major obstacle to Nigeria’s political development is division along ethnic, religious and regional lines. We must rise above these differences and promote politics founded on competence, Integrity, inclusion and national interest.

“Nigeria must always be greater than any political party, individual or sectional interest.”

The former President who served as deputy governor and governor of Bayelsa State before becoming vice-president and president of the country noted that his experience had taught him the importance of consultation, teamwork and strong institutions, just as he urged former deputy governors to promote cordial relationships between serving governors and their deputies, mentor younger politicians and discourage divisive politics.

Jonathan said, “As a former deputy governor and governor of Bayelsa State before becoming vice president and subsequently president of Nigeria, I understand the opportunities and challenges associated with the office of deputy governor.

“The experience teaches patience, loyalty, consultation and teamwork. Above all, it reminds us that governance is not about one individual but about strong institutions and service to the people.”

Earlier in his remarks, the National Chairman of the Forum of Former Deputy Governors of Nigeria (FFDGN), Dr Chris Alozie Akomas challenged political leaders to abandon arrogance and embrace accountability, warning that power without character is destructive and governance without empathy is empty.

Akomas who identified the widening gap between political leaders and citizens as a major obstacle to Nigeria’s development, said sustainable development could not be achieved through policies, budgets and administrative reforms alone without a fundamental change in the attitudes, values and conduct of those entrusted with public responsibility.

According to Akomas, the disconnect between leaders and the people they govern has spread across government institutions, communities and families, weakening the collective effort needed to build a prosperous nation.

“We cannot build a lasting future on a foundation of indifference,” he said.

The former deputy governor who maintained that leadership should be measured by the commitment to serving the people, particularly the vulnerable, rather than the privileges and influence attached to public office, said, “Leadership is not a badge of immunity; it is a higher standard of accountability,” he said, urging public officeholders to replace arrogance with humility and responsibility.

“Power without character is destructive, while governance without empathy is an empty shell.”

Akomas who notec that Nigeria’s development challenges required more than new laws and government programmes, stressed that national renewal must begin with integrity, ethical conduct and a commitment to the common good, just as he warned that public trust would remain elusive if leaders continued to ignore the everyday struggles of ordinary Nigerians.

The FFDGN chairman also cautioned against placing the entire responsibility for national renewal on government officials, insisting that citizens had an equally important role in restoring the country’s values.

“A nation is never rescued by its government alone; it is also sustained by the conscience of its people,” he said.

In his remarks, former Kano State Governor, Dr Abdullahi Ganduje who called on Nigerians to embrace their diversity and develop a stronger sense of national identity, warned that ethnic politics continued to undermine nation-building, just as he traced Nigeria’s complex national integration challenges to its colonial history but acknowledged the contributions of First Republic politicians to the struggle for independence.
