The immediate past national chairman of the ruling All Progressives Congress who also criticised the lack of continuity between successive administrations, saying political friction between incumbent governors and their predecessors often led to the abandonment of projects and programmes, said such practices undermined sustainable development, stressing that continuity was necessary for consolidation and long-term progress.

He faulted the weak ideological foundations of Nigerian political parties, saying that politicians frequently defected in pursuit of personal interests rather than shared values.

“We must, however, appreciate our First Republic politicians, who developed a sense of nationalism and worked to secure independence. They succeeded in achieving independence through political pressure.

“Unfortunately, after Nigeria’s Independence, some of those leaders who had demonstrated a nationalistic outlook became tribalistic in their attitudes, as political parties were largely organised along ethnic lines.

“It is, therefore, our responsibility, as time progresses, to come together, believe in Nigeria and turn our diversity into an asset rather than a liability,” he said.

Ganduje who noted that deputy governors should be recognised for their contributions to governance rather than treated as mere substitutes for governors, said, “What is the issue between a governor who has left office and a new governor who has taken over? We often find friction between them, sometimes even when they belong to the same political party. The situation can be worse when they belong to different parties.

“This friction denies us continuity in governance. A governor may have completed some projects while others are still ongoing. When a new governor comes into office, the previous administration’s projects and programmes may be abandoned or reversed. There is, therefore, no continuity.”

On his part, former Delta State Governor, Dr Ifeanyi Okowa who noted that the growing disconnect between government policies and citizens’ everyday experiences had weakened public trust, said that nation-building depended on a social contract anchored on accountability, inclusion and shared responsibility, adding that citizens had increasingly felt alienated because their expectations and aspirations were not being adequately met.

He said rebuilding trust between the government and the governed was as important as economic growth, infrastructure development and administrative efficiency.

The conference attracted political leaders, members of the diplomatic corps, industry representatives, academics, youth and women’s organisations, and professional bodies.

Former President Goodluck Jonathan, the forum’s Grand Patron, attended the gathering, while former Delta State Governor, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, served as co-chairman.

Earlier, the forum’s Director-General, Hon. Kenneth Ibe-Kalu, told the gathering that the organisation remained committed to promoting civic education, integrity and discipline to address the widening gap between leadership and citizens.

Ibe-Kalu urged participants to translate their deliberations into practical solutions that would strengthen national unity, improve governance and advance sustainable development.

World.title: Hardship: FG summons NLC leaders as ultimatum nears end
World.content:
File image

By Victor Ahiuma-Young

The Federal Government has summoned the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) to a conciliation meeting in Abuja amid mounting concerns over economic hardship and the union’s ultimatum demanding urgent measures to ease the burden on Nigerian workers.

The meeting, scheduled for Thursday, October 22, 2026, comes a day before the two-week ultimatum issued by the NLC on October 9 expires on Friday, October 23.

The NLC had demanded a reduction in petrol prices, the commencement of negotiations for a new national minimum wage and the implementation of outstanding agreements with public- and health-sector workers, among other demands.

The labour union warned that failure by the government to address its demands within the stipulated period could compel the labour movement to take further action.

NLC leaders had earlier rejected the response of the Minister of Labour and Employment to the communiqué issued at the end of meetings of the union’s organs, which contained the ultimatum.

The planned meeting, convened at the directive of the Minister of Labour and Employment, is expected to provide an avenue for dialogue on workers’ grievances and explore possible solutions to the issues raised by the Congress.

In a letter inviting the NLC leadership to the meeting, the Ministry said the engagement was intended to promote constructive dialogue and industrial harmony.

The letter, signed by the Director of Trade Union Services and Industrial Relations, Falonipe Amos O., on behalf of the minister, stated: “I refer to our letter dated 12 October 2026, conveying the response of the Honourable Minister to the communiqué issued following the joint meeting of the Central Working Committee and National Executive Council of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC).

“The Ministry recognises the importance of constructive social dialogue in addressing issues affecting workers and promoting industrial peace and harmony.

“In this regard, and in furtherance of its mandate to foster harmonious industrial relations, the Honourable Minister of Labour and Employment has directed that a conciliation meeting be convened with the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress.

“Accordingly, the Nigeria Labour Congress is hereby invited to a conciliation meeting scheduled as follows:

“Date: Thursday, 22 October 2026. “Time: 1:00 p.m.

“Venue: Office of the Honourable Minister of Labour and Employment, Federal Secretariat Complex, Phase I, Abuja.

“The meeting is intended to provide an opportunity for frank and constructive dialogue on the issues raised by the Congress, including measures to address the challenges facing workers and to explore mutually acceptable approaches to maintaining industrial peace and stability.

“The Ministry looks forward to the cooperation of the Nigeria Labour Congress and a fruitful engagement aimed at finding practical and sustainable solutions to the issues raised in the communiqué.”

World.title: Breaking: Afenifere ​‌⁠⁠​‍⁠⁠‍‌​​‌‍‍​‌‌​Leader, Pa Fasoranti, Dies at 100, Aiyedatiwa Mourns
World.content:
Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has expressed sadness over the death of the leader of the pan-Yoruba socio-poitical organisation, Afenifere, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, at the age of 100.

Aiyedatiwa, in a condolence message he personally signed on Tuesday in Akure, said the death of the centenarian was a great loss to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria.

The governor described Fasoranti as a patriarch and beacon of wisdom, integrity and selfless service, whose life was dedicated to the development of the society.

According to him, the late elder statesman demonstrated uncommon commitment to the progress and development of Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria throughout his lifetime.

“With a heavy heart but with total submission to the will of God, I announce the passing of our revered elder statesman, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, who departed this world at the glorious age of 100.

“Pa Fasoranti was a patriarch, a beacon of wisdom, integrity and selfless service whose century-long life was marked by uncommon commitment to the development of our dear State, Yorubaland and Nigeria at large,” he said.

Aiyedatiwa said the deceased would be remembered for his fatherly guidance, wise counsel and principled positions on issues bordering on justice and good governance.

He noted that Fasoranti lived a fulfilled life and left behind enduring legacies worthy of emulation by the present and future generations.

“His counsel, fatherly guidance and principled stand on issues of justice and good governance will be sorely missed.

“He lived a fulfilled life and left indelible footprints of honour and legacy for generations to come,” the governor said.

Aiyedatiwa, on behalf of the government and people of Ondo State, commiserated with the Fasoranti family, the people of Akure Kingdom and the entire state over the loss.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul. (NAN)

World.title: Breaking: Nigeria Confirms Imported Ebola Case in FCT, Identifies 44 Contacts, Activates Emergency Response
World.content:
The Federal Government has confirmed one imported case of Bundibugyo ebolavirus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and has activated public health response measures to prevent further spread.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Pate, disclosed this at a media conference in Abuja on Tuesday, following laboratory confirmation of the infection on Oct. 20.

Pate said the patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was currently in isolation and receiving medical care.

He described the case as “a contained case,” while assuring Nigerians that the government was working with relevant authorities and partners to prevent further transmission.

Pate said the woman had been admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed.

He said contact tracing had commenced, with 44 close contacts identified so far, while public health teams were identifying and monitoring people who might have been exposed, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel contacts.

“Surveillance has also been intensified, and the private hospital where the patient was treated is receiving immediate support to strengthen infection prevention and control measures,” he said.

The minister urged public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to remain on high alert, maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases.

He also urged the public to observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected cases to public health authorities.

He said Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is sick or has died from the disease, as well as contact with contaminated materials.

Pate advised Nigerians to practise regular hand hygiene, avoid contact with the body fluids of anyone suspected to have Ebola and watch for symptoms.

The symptoms, he said, included fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea, particularly following possible exposure.

He said people who might have been exposed should report immediately, even if they felt well, while anyone who developed symptoms should avoid close contact with others and call public health authorities for guidance before visiting a healthcare facility.

The minister also urged people contacted during the tracing exercise, including relevant airline passengers, to provide the required information and comply with public health advice.

He cautioned against rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation, advising Nigerians to rely on verified information from official health authorities.

Pate recalled that Nigeria had successfully contained Ebola in 2014 and had the experience and public health systems required to respond to the current case.

He, however, emphasised that containing the infection required cooperation from the public, early detection and prompt reporting of suspected cases.

“The Government of Nigeria through the Presidential Taskforce on EVD and NCDC will continue to provide updates.

“NCDC free call centre is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For information or to report a suspected case, please call NCDC toll-free number 6232,” Pate added.(NAN)

World.title: Zitra Investments Vows to Close Financial Inclusion Gap, Expands Access to Credit
World.content:
Marking its sixth anniversary, the management of Zitra Investments has expressed determination to close the financial inclusion gap and extend Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) access to credit in Nigeria.

The Chief Executive Officer, Zitra Investments, Mr. Babatunde Obadero, at a press conference held recently in Lagos, said SMEs remain the heartbeat of commerce in the country, and the company is poised to assist with access to credit.

He stated that the company in six years of remaining in operation has been an interesting journey for the management.

He said: “I dare say 300,000 loans and N30 billion loans disbursed in the last six years. 200,000 customers on our digital platforms. The journey has just started and there is still a lot of ground to cover.

“In six years, we have our banking licence. We have a Securities & Exchange Commission (SEC) issued asset management licence, and a payment company called Zitra Pay. All of these entities have given us a platform to provide services our customers require.

“We have built an ecosystem that delivers financial services just the way our customers need them. We are proud to say our growth has not begun. We have a combined balance sheet size of over N50 billion which is a beginning of our journey to greater things ahead.”

Going into the future, he said the goal of the company is to lead in the retail digital financial services in Nigeria, stressing that the company aims to expand its footprint geographically and provide better access to its digital channels.

Co-founder, Zitra Investments, Mr. Femi Okuyelu, recalled that the company started with five staff and today, it has over 120 staff in different locations across the country.

“In terms of growth, we have seen the business evolve and we have been able to solve some problems in the nation’s economy.

“Today in Nigeria, the financial inclusion is now about 79 per cent, 21 million adults financially excluded. It can look small but that combined population is equivalent to Finland, Estonia and maybe Denmark. And we have actually contributed our quota into that financial inclusion story,” he said.

On why credit penetration is still low, Okuyelu said: “Only 10 per cent of the adult population have access to credit. People who borrow from family and friends, cooperatives, churches. Why they are not able to access formal credit? Number one, they don’t have collateral. Number two, they play in the informal sector which is not organised. And number three, no credit history and credit records.”

He said Zitra’s response has been to create a social business model that onboards informal customers, helps them organise their businesses, monitors cash flow and lends against it.

“What we have created will make it easier for them to access credit. We monitor their cash flow and lend against their cash flow because in this environment, lending against collateral is difficult,” he said.

On his part, Director, Chief Olaotan Olamuyiwa, who recalled that the idea for Zitra was conceived during COVID-19 when the founders decided to start their own firm after working in different organisations, said the journey has been built on relationships and one major investor who believed in the vision.

Speaking on how small businesses struggle with funding, he noted that many SMEs have their own money trapped with clients.

“You see people that want N5 million to stock up, but they have sold products to other businesses and those businesses are owing them in excess of N20 million. They cannot afford N5 million to finance a transaction because their cash is tied,” he said.

He said products like invoice discounting address that gap, adding that: “lf you have N20 million in invoices due in 60 to 90 days, you can come to us and say, fund this N1 million project and I will pay when my debtor pays.”

World.title: TETFund Urges Academics to Turn Research into Practical Innovations
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) has urged Nigerian academics and researchers to move beyond publishing scholarly papers to developing practical innovations that address societal challenges and create economic opportunities.

The Executive Secretary, Sonny Echono, made the call in Abuja at the closing ceremony of the 35th cohort of the Research for Impact Initiative (R4i).

Echono said the initiative, implemented in partnership with Innov8 Hub, is part of the fund’s strategy to institutionalise research and development in public tertiary institutions and strengthen the relationship between academic research, industry and government.

“We must empower our scholars to create local solutions for our societal problems. This is why a commitment to education is a commitment to our nation’s future, ensuring that our people are not just consumers of foreign technology, but innovators who can drive sustainable growth,” he said.

He stressed that Nigeria needed to strengthen its capacity to develop home-grown technologies rather than depend on innovations from other countries.

He noted that technological advancement had become a major driver of economic transformation, adding that countries seeking sustainable development must invest in quality education, research and innovation.

“At TETFund, we are refocusing and reinvigorating our intervention activities to drive the institutionalisation of Research and Development in public tertiary institutions, enhance research capacity, and support research-industry linkage, among others,” he said.

He said R4i is designed to reposition public tertiary institutions as drivers of a knowledge-based economy through innovative practices and solution-driven research.

Echono commended Innov8 Hub for providing technical expertise and mentorship to participating academics, and urged the graduates to apply the knowledge acquired to develop solutions for their institutions and communities.

He disclosed that some innovations from previous editions of the programme were showcased at the maiden TETFund National Research Fair and Exhibition in November 2024.

The second edition will hold from November 23 to 27, 2026 at the Abuja Trade and Convention Centre, Airport Road, giving researchers the opportunity to showcase their innovations, connect with industry players and explore partnerships for commercialising research outputs.

The Deputy General Manager of Innov8 Hub, Dr. Deji Ige, said the initiative was designed to establish a culture in which research and development drive innovation, enterprise creation and national development.

“Innovation thrives in a culture where research and development are the primary languages of interaction. If we can learn, understand and revive this culture, the outcomes will include inventions, solutions, technological advancement, enterprise development, job creation, wealth generation, meaningful impact and societal development,” he said.

Ige described the programme as a shift towards stronger collaboration among government, academia, industry and society, adding that research without practical impact could limit the ability of tertiary institutions to contribute to technological advancement.

“Impact-driven research and development is what keeps it afloat and enables it to navigate safely. Without impact flowing from research and development, academia becomes an immobile vessel, bereft of progress, possibilities and the power to navigate,” he said.

World.title: ADC Unveils Kele As Running Mate, Intensifies Push for Plateau Govt House
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Plateau State has unveiled Hon. Chungdung Bitrus Pwajok Kele as the running mate to its governorship candidate, Brig.-Gen. John Sunday Sura (rtd), ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The event, which took place in Jos, attracted party officials, stakeholders, supporters and political associates from across the state.

Speaking at the unveiling, Sura described Kele as an experienced politician and grassroots mobiliser whose emergence would strengthen the party’s efforts as it prepares for the forthcoming election.

He said the ADC ticket was aimed at providing what he described as an alternative platform for governance in Plateau State, adding that the party would focus on issues of security, rural development and inclusive leadership.

According to him, the unveiling marked the beginning of a series of political activities designed to expand the party’s presence across the state’s 17 local government areas.

He disclosed that the ADC would subsequently launch its governorship campaign and embark on consultations and mobilisation efforts in various constituencies across the state.

“We want Plateau people to know that ADC is on the ground. This is the beginning of our activities ahead of the campaign proper,” he said.

Sura also expressed confidence in the party’s chances in the election, stating that voters would assess the performance of the incumbent administration alongside the programmes being presented by opposition parties.

He said his campaign would focus on issues affecting citizens, including infrastructure, transportation, economic development and public welfare.

Responding to questions on the incumbency factor, the ADC governorship candidate maintained that the party remained focused on its objectives and would continue to engage voters.

On his running mate, Sura described Kele as a politician with extensive grassroots experience, noting that she had previously served as councillor representing Gyel ‘A’ Ward in Jos South Local Government Area and had contested for several elective offices.

He added that her political network and experience in mobilising women and young people would be of great advantage in the state governance.

ADC officials at the event expressed optimism that the Sura-Kele ticket would enhance the party’s reach across different demographic groups as political activities gradually gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general election.

World.title: Nigerian Army Deepens Defence Ties with Rwanda, as COAS Calls for Modern Military Training, Exchange Programmes
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has reaffirmed the Nigerian Army’s commitment to strengthening African-led defence partnerships to combat terrorism, violent extremism and other transnational security threats undermining peace and stability across the continent.

The COAS made this known during a courtesy visit to the Chief of Defence Staff of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), General Mubarakh Muganga, in Kigali, the Republic of Rwanda. The visit formed part of his ongoing official working visit aimed at deepening bilateral military cooperation and advancing collective security initiatives.

Lieutenant General Shaibu also underscored the importance of modern military training, professional military education and cadet exchange programmes in developing combat-ready, adaptable and interoperable armed forces.

According to a statement by the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, the COAS made this call during a visit to the Rwanda Military Academy (RMA), Gako, as part of his official working visit to Rwanda.

Colonel Anele said the engagement highlighted the imperative for African nations to take greater responsibility for addressing shared security challenges through sustained military cooperation, intelligence-sharing, joint capacity development and coordinated responses to emerging threats.

Lieutenant General Shaibu emphasised the strategic importance of strengthening military-to-military relations, particularly in counter-terrorism, counter-insurgency, professional military education and the exchange of operational experiences.

He said these areas of cooperation were critical to enhancing interoperability, operational readiness and the capacity of African armed forces to confront increasingly complex and interconnected security threats.

The COAS commended the Academy’s training standards, discipline and professionalism, particularly the tactical proficiency demonstrated during a Special Forces display.

He stressed that evolving security threats demanded innovative training, sound leadership and operational adaptability, noting that professional military education remained essential to producing competent officers capable of operating effectively in complex security environments.

Lieutenant General Shaibu urged the Academy’s leadership to prepare for the arrival of the first batch of Nigerian officer cadets under the proposed exchange programme.

He advocated leveraging the experiences of both countries in counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency to enrich military training, strengthen operational planning and enhance interoperability in addressing shared security challenges.

Earlier, the representative of the Commandant, Brigadier General Bukenya, said the Academy developed professional military leaders through rigorous training in military tactics, leadership, discipline and physical fitness.

He added that its programmes equipped cadets with essential skills in peace support operations, operational planning and logistics management.

Brigadier General Bukenya welcomed the proposed training partnership, reaffirming the Academy’s commitment to strengthening military education and defence cooperation between Nigeria and Rwanda.

The visit reinforced the Nigerian Army’s drive to enhance professional training, deepen military partnerships and prepare future commanders for the demands of modern warfare and regional security.

It further underscored the importance of African-led security solutions anchored in mutual trust, shared expertise and collective responsibility. The engagement also highlighted the need for stronger defence collaboration among African nations to prevent terrorist and criminal networks from exploiting national borders and regional security vulnerabilities.

The engagement aligns with the Nigerian Army’s commitment to strategic defence cooperation and the broader objective of building a more secure, stable and resilient African continent through sustainable, African-led security partnerships.

World.title: TAN Urges EFCC, ICPC to Probe Ogun APC Guber Candidate over Alleged Appropriation Breaches
World.content:
The Transparency and Accountability Network (TAN) has called on the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission, and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission to investigate the Senator representing Ogun West in the National Assembly, Senator Olamilekan Adeola, over the series of allegations, especially alleged appropriations and project scandals that have allegedly triggered deeper economic pains for Nigerians even after fuel subsidy removal.

The civil society organisation said until he clears his name, Senator Adeola has no business contesting for any elective position in 2027 or in the future, stressing that “Nigeria is not a Banana Republic that can be operated as a private commercial enterprise.”

In a statement signed by its President, Dr. Oluwole Oladapo, and titled “Senator Solomon Adeola (Yayi) Cannot Go Into An Election Without Clearing Allegations of Appropriation Corruption”, TAN said Nigeria was too big to allow such scandals to be swept under the carpet without security agencies inviting the Senator.

Adeola, the 2027 governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress in Ogun State has been enmeshed in series of controversies.

The statement said, “As an organisation committed to public integrity, TAN asserts that there is nowhere in the civilised world where an individual aspiring to a public office of such great significance would be allowed to contest without satisfactorily clearing his name of serious ethical clouds.

“The ongoing reliance on the power of incumbency to shove candidates down the throats of the electorate without addressing fundamental crises of integrity undermines the core values of our democratic space.”

Advocating for Adeola’s immediate disqualification from the 2027 gubernatorial race, the group warned relevant agencies against taking the matter with levity.

TAN also called for investigation into Adeola’s role as Appropriations Committee Chairman, noting that repeated claims that the APC candidate’s committee allegedly inserted untraceable or duplicated projects in the budget and allocated funds to agencies outside their statutory mandates, should not be swept under the carpet.

“Beyond identity disputes, we are calling on relevant anti-corruption agencies to immediately intervene and investigate the Senator’s performance as the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Appropriations,” the statement said.

The group referenced a petition by PASSEC against Adeola, stating, “It seems to us that the petition by The Pan African Society for Social & Economic Change (PASSEC) submitted to the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) that alleged irregularities in federal budgets between 2023 and 2026, claiming the insertion of untraceable or duplicated projects and the allocation of funds to agencies outside their statutory mandates has been left unattended.”

It added, “All Nigerians are aware of the scandalous and epileptic nature of annual budget implementation in this country. The citizens cannot just focus on the Executive organ of government alone because most of these unprecedented budgetary break-and-quench anomalies are caused by the malfunctioning of the Appropriations Committee of the National Assembly which Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola (Yayi) presides over. The entire mess originates from there.”

“The democratic values of our nation are at stake when serious allegations are glossed over by political structures. We cannot treat allegations of this magnitude as mere political noise,” TAN President declared.

To this end, the Transparency and Accountability Network of Nigeria demanded an immediate intervention by security agencies, saying that relevant law enforcement and anti-graft agencies must thoroughly investigate the statutory claims and financial oversight tracks associated with the senator’s office.

“We call on political parties to refrain from bypassing ethical scrutiny in the deployment of candidates for significant public offices,” TAN said.

The group maintained that democratic accountability must remain the foundation of true leadership.

“Therefore, we demand that until all these allegations have been properly and satisfactorily cleared, all processes regarding the Senator’s governorship ambition should be put on hold.

“As a matter of fact, he deserves to be immediately disqualified from the race pending the outcome of a full investigation into all these anomalies being alleged by several stakeholders in Nigeria,” the CSO said.

World.title: Appeal Court Nullifies Zamfara North APC Senatorial Primary
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The Court of Appeal sitting in Sokoto has nullified the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for Zamfara North Senatorial District for gross non-compliance with party guidelines and the Electoral Act.

The judgment was delivered on Tuesday by Justice Tunde Oyebamiji Awotoye, who upheld the earlier decision of the Federal High Court, Gusau, which had in August 2026 voided the primary election.

Justice Awotoye lambasted the APC for what he described as reckless declaration of Senator Sahabi Ya’u as winner despite clear violations of its own constitution and the Electoral Act.

The court held that the respondent, Hon. Abdullahi Shinkafi, proved his case beyond reasonable doubt, questioning how a senatorial district with 26,000 registered party members could return 70,000 votes for an aspirant.

According to the court, the figures presented by the party showed clear over-voting and irregularities that rendered the entire exercise invalid and liable to be nullified.

Justice Awotoye wondered why the party leadership ignored the obvious discrepancies and proceeded to declare a winner in an election that failed basic integrity tests.

The appellate court resolved all seven issues formulated for determination in the appeal against the appellant, Senator Sahabi Ya’u.

On the preliminary objection bordering on lack of jurisdiction raised by the appellant’s counsel, Popoola, SAN, the court held that the respondent had duly exhausted all internal dispute resolution mechanisms of the party before approaching the court.

The court also dismissed the argument on statute bar, holding that the suit was filed within time and was entertained on its merit in line with extant laws.

Reacting to the judgment, counsel to the respondent, Bello Galadi, described the decision as a victory for the rule of law and democracy.

Galadi said the judgment would serve as a deterrent to political parties and politicians who undermine internal democracy and violate their own rules.

Also reacting, Hon. Shinkafi thanked the judiciary for living up to its billing as the last hope of the common man, describing the judgment as freedom from political captivity.

He argued that the judgment was a victory against marginalisation and prolonged dominance, noting that Senator Ya’u has spent 16 consecutive years in the Senate while Kaura Namoda has monopolised the seat since the return to democracy in 1999.

World.title: Friend testifies about final moments before AKA and Tibz were shot dead
World.content:
Rapper Kierna ‘AKA’ Forbes’ friend and celebrity chef Tebello ‘Tibz’ Motsoane repeatedly said he could not breathe after gunshots were fired outside Wish restaurant on Florida Road in Durban, the Durban High Court heard on Tuesday.

Motsoane and AKA were gunned down on February 10, 2023.

Lindokuhle Mkhwanazi, Lindani Ndimande, Siyanda Myeza, Mziwethemba Gwabeni, Lindokuhle Ndimande, Malusi Ndimande and Siyabonga Ndimande face charges 11 charges including conspiracy to commit murder, murder, unlawful possession of a firearm, unlawful possession of ammunition, five counts of attempted murder, and money laundering.





WITNESS RECOUNTS DAY AKA WAS MURDERED

State witness Lusaso Ngcobo, a Durban musician and event organiser, testified on Tuesday and requested that his face not be shown.

Ngcobo told the court that he had known AKA for more than a decade through the music industry and that they were close friends. He also knew Motsoane through the industry.

He testified that on 10 February 2023, he went to the Bryd and Groom hair salon on Florida Road at around 18:30, as he usually did on Fridays. About 15 minutes later, AKA arrived with his entourage. The rapper, who was visiting the establishment for the first time, also had his hair cut.

Ngcobo said they spent time catching up before heading to Wish restaurant for dinner, where they discussed AKA’s plans, including the release of his new album Mass Country which was released posthumously on 24 February 2023.

Motsoane later joined them during the approximately two hours they spent at the restaurant.

Ngcobo testified that the group eventually left Wish through a passage leading outside. He was among those at the front, while AKA and Motsoane were behind him.



Once they reached the pavement, the group said their goodbyes. Ngcobo said he turned towards the passage to return inside after saying goodbye.

He testified that AKA was standing to his right and speaking to Motsoane, and he [AKA] was about an arm’s length away just before the shooting. They planned to meet again later after the performance at Yugo nightclub in Durban.

Ngcobo recalled hearing a loud bang that initially sounded like fireworks.

“Right at that moment I heard a loud bang like fireworks. My first reaction was to duck because I wasn’t sure what was happening. I then saw everyone running and I realised it was unsafe and that maybe the sound couldn’t have been fireworks but a firearm instead,” he testified.

Ngcobo said he ran back towards the restaurant corridor with others. During the commotion, he saw Motsoane trip and fall.

He testified that he went to check on Motsoane before noticing AKA lying on the ground.

“I went to check on Tibz if he was okay and I recall seeing Kiernan lying on the floor I was walking out. I proceeded to check if he was okay because I could see some blood and I wasn’t sure if it was on him or on the floor. I asked him if he was okay, he said I can’t breathe. He kept saying I can’t breathe,” Ngcobo told the court.

“I proceeded to ask him if he was hurt and I could not make sense of the words he was saying. We tried to see where the blood was coming from as we were searching his body we realised he had a wound by his chest underneath his arm,” he added.

They called for assistance and attempted to stop the bleeding using towels while waiting for help to arrive.

World.title: Mofokeng €15 million transfer update: French and German clubs
World.content:
Relebohile Mofokeng was recently linked with interest from French side Lille and the German giants Bayer Leverkusen. According to the Ekrem Kanur, the Turkish global transfers reporter, interest has gathered momentum.

The latest update says scouts from both clubs have continued to keep tabs on the 21-year-old forward, following six goals and two assists in 14 games for club and country.

INTEREST IN RELEBOHILE MOFOKENG

Kanur reports that bids worth €15 million could be expected arrive during the upcoming January transfer window. In addition to Lille and Leverkusen’s interest, Mofokeng’s name has been discussed in meetings at Atletico Madrid, Chelsea, Brighton and Napoli.



“Relebohile Mofokeng continues to attract strong interest from across Europe,” the report said. “Monitoring → Scouts from Lille and Bayer Leverkusen are continuing to track the 21-year-old Union SG winger.

“Offers in the region of €15 million could arrive for the South African talent in January. Atlético Madrid, Napoli, Chelsea and Brighton are also closely monitoring the youngster’s progress,” Kanur concluded.

FAST START IN EUROPE

The former Orlando Pirates star has adapted quickly to European football and has become an important creative option for Union SG coach David Hubert.

His competitive debut was particularly memorable. On 31 July, Mofokeng came off the bench against Club Brugge in the Belgian Super Cup final before converting the decisive penalty in the shootout.

He then announced himself in the Belgian Pro League, scoring on his league debut against K.V.C. Westerlo on 8 August. His performances have included a standout display against Royal Antwerp, where he helped dictate the tempo during a 2-0 victory.

His European adventure has also included the UEFA Europa League, where he scored in Union SG’s 3-0 victory over Viktoria Plzeň on 17 September. Mofokeng continued to make his presence felt on Sunday, laying on a brilliant assist to help Union SG secure a 3-0 victory over KFC Nijlen in the Belgian Cup.



David Hubert has already acknowledged the competition for places within his squad. But Mofokeng’s performances have strengthened his case for a regular role.

World.title: RUMOUR: Kaizer Chiefs to sack Da Cruz if…
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head coach Fernando Da Cruz is already facing some staunch criticism from Amakhosi fans. Is he on borrowed time?

Da Cruz’s head is on the chopping block

After just eight games of the new Betway Premiership campaign, Kaizer Chiefs are already trailing leaders Sundowns by nine points, and Orlando Pirates by eight. They’ve only triumphed in one of their last seven clashes across all competitions. With just a solitary piece of silverware in the last 10 years (a Nedbank Cup triumph in last year’s final against Pirates), it’s difficult to escape the conclusion that Chiefs are horribly underachieving, given their fanbase and huge financial might. If results don’t improve quickly, it’s easy to envisage a situation where Da Cruz is sacked before Christmas. If they’re out of contention for CAF Champions League football, that should be the final nail in his coffin.

Frustrations boil over

There was reportedly a heated exchange between Reeve Frosler and Renaldo Leaner in the aftermath of the 0-1 defeat to Arrows, perhaps indicating that all is not well in the dressing room. Siphesihle Ndlovu and Lebohang Maboe looked to be a cohesive midfield pairing, but with both out injured, Da Cruz has tinkered with both his systems and playing personnel. Usual right-back Reeve Frosler has been selected alongside Sibongiseni Mthethwa in front of a back three, and it hasn’t worked.



Kaizer Chiefs are struggling again

World.title: ‘Dream come true’: Handre Pollard’s daughter turns one!
World.content:
Marise Pollard, the wife of Springboks fly-half Handre Pollard, penned a thoughtful tribute to their daughter Isabella who turned one on 20 October.

HANDRE POLLARD’S DAUGHTER TURNS ONE

Handre and Marise Pollard have been together for over 13 years and married for over eight years. Marise and Handre Pollard officially became parents of two under two on 20 October 2025. On 25 April 2024, the pair welcomed their first child, Hunter Andre Pollard. Now, they are celebrating their daughter, Isabella Pollard turning one. Marise penned a touching tribute to her toddler via an Instagram post. Take a look…

“Can’t write a caption because I’ve cried too many times—like, HOW is she ONE? Just five minutes ago, you were still just a dream. The fastest year of parenthood yet. Happy birthday, Isabella—our Bella. You are wild, gentle, loving, and a literal ray of sunshine. With your dad’s green eyes, you run through life with the biggest smile,” she wrote.



“I could watch you all day long. I see so much of myself in you; you teach me so much. I don’t know what I did to be your mom in this lifetime, but I’m the luckiest—thank you, Jesus. Grateful doesn’t even begin to cover it. My best friend forever, my dream come true,” she continued.

“You are everything 🤍,” she added.





MARISE POLLARD ON IVF

Marise previously opened up about using In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF). She explained that she planned everything she could for her first child, Hunter. However, with Isabella, she learnt that there was no need for perfection and embraced the chaos.

“We planned everything to a tee. After IVF, I spent months mentally, emotionally, and spiritually preparing myself. I was determined to be organised, prepared, and on top of everything. I thought if I planned enough, motherhood would unfold exactly as I imagined,” she wrote.

“Then came Isabella…And she gently taught me one of the biggest lessons, you cannot control motherhood. She arrived and slowly chipped away at my need for perfection. The schedules, the expectations, the pressure to have it all together. She showed me that the magic isn’t found in getting everything right, it’s found in embracing the chaos, being present in the messy moments, and sometimes simply laughing when nothing goes according to plan,” she continued.



The family of four recently went on holiday to Mauritius.

World.title: Makhaya Ntini reveals how Proteas wanted him sent home before 13-wicket haul
World.content:
Former Proteas fast bowler Makhaya Ntini has revealed how he was blamed for South Africa’s disappointing performance in the first Test against the West Indies in 2005, only to bounce back with a remarkable 13-wicket haul in the next match.

The first Test, played in Guyana, saw the West Indies post a mammoth 543/5. South Africa struggled in their first innings, managing just 188 runs before being forced to follow on. The Proteas then scored 269 in their second innings to secure a draw.

Speaking to Sen Cricket, Ntini recalled how he was singled out for criticism after South Africa managed to take only three wickets in the match.



Makhaya Ntini says he was made the scapegoat

The former fast bowler said he was even told that he did not belong in the team and should be sent home, despite the other bowlers also struggling to make an impact.

“I was called the weakest link. My question was, what do you mean I was the weakest link? It seems like I was the only one who was supposed to bowl here, but you selected six bowlers,” Ntini said.

“None of us took more than one wicket, but I was made the weakest link.”

Ntini revealed that he accepted the criticism but remained in the team for the second Test, which was played in Trinidad.

Rather than being sent home, the bowler delivered one of the finest performances of his career, claiming 13 wickets to help South Africa beat the West Indies in the next Test match.

It was one of Makhaya Ntini’s best bowling figures in Test cricket.



“They said, ‘No, no, no, you don’t belong here, you need to go home.’ Okay, fair enough, I took it, but I didn’t go home. They made a mistake of selecting me for the next game that was played in Trinidad. I picked up 13 wickets in that game,” he recalled.

“I was like, what’s the story here? Am I still getting sent home?” Ntini added with a laugh.

Asked whether the performance ranked among the best he had ever produced, alongside his memorable display at Lord’s, Ntini agreed.

“Yes, it was, besides Lord’s,” he said.

Makhaya Ntini’s account highlights the remarkable turnaround between the two Tests, as the bowler responded to being labelled the team’s weakest link by producing a match-winning performance for the Proteas. South Africa went on to win the four-Test series 2-0

How good was Ntini in his prime?

World.title: Is South Africa’s 2nd richest municipality the tenderpreneur capital?
World.content:
The average taxable income in South Africa’s second richest municipality is R494 156 a year.

But more residents in the municipality get their money from the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA).

Not just any grant, but the social grant for South Africans living below the Food Poverty Line (FPL).



So, what’s going on?

More grant beneficiaries than taxpayers

Ntabankulu may be the clearest sign that it pays to work for or with the government.

The average taxpayer in the town of 146 423 people earns more than the average taxpayer in major metros like Johannesburg and Cape Town.

The municipality isn’t home to any major mining operation similar to South Africa’s richest municipality: Gamagara Local Municipality, in the Northern Cape.

Instead, in this Eastern Cape municipality on the Wild Coast, the primary income sources appear to be the government and cannabis.

In 2025, the municipality unveiled an R80 million hub to formalise its cannabis farming and production.



Two years earlier, the municipality spent over a billion building roughly 33 kilometres of road.

The municipality’s audited annual reports suggest some of its taxable income could originate from tenders.

According to its adjusted performance report for 2023-2024, Ntabankulu spent R1.04 billion on 33.74 kilometres of road.

Projects appear to be the municipality’s bread and butter.

The municipality currently has 9 active tenders.

It also intends to award 5 road maintenance tenders to local companies. One tender will go to a driving school that doubles as a construction company.

Another tender goes to a construction company with two directors: a former bookbinder in the printing industry and an admin assistant. Both have no construction experience.

But for most residents, the reality is abject poverty.

Grant Beneficiaries in Ntabankulu

Despite the wealth from a handful of residents, only 1.79% of the municipality’s population are taxpayers.

Instead, it appears most residents receive money from the Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant.

According to the South African Revenue Service (SARS) tax statistics, Ntabankulu had 2 631 taxpayers at the end of 2024.

But recent data from SASSA’s SRD statistics show 22 382 residents in the municipality rely on a R370 social grant.

To be eligible for the SRD grant, applicants cannot receive more than R624 in a single month.

World.title: ‘South Africa would gain something’: Grant recipient’s proposal for SASSA
World.content:
Close-up of a carpenter skilfully using a circular saw for precise woodwork. Image: Pexels

Nkosinathi Nxumalo, a man from KwaZulu-Natal, believes SASSA could do more than just pay out grants. He wants the agency to help recipients build skills that could lift them out of poverty.

Nxumalo holds a matric certificate and has received the Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant for more than five years. He shared his story through The South African’s SASSA grant survey.

SRD grant stretched across a large household

Nxumalo uses his grant for a mix of needs. He said it helps, but it is not enough, and he runs out before the month ends. Even so, he confirmed that no one in his household went without food in the past month.



His biggest financial concern is the cost of living and rising food prices.

Grant recipient faces a string of SASSA problems

Nxumalo has faced several challenges with his grant. He listed payment delays, knowing when to renew or reapply, and understanding why his application was rejected. He has also had a declined or lapsed application.

Despite this, he rated SASSA’s communication with recipients as very good. When asked what one thing he would change, he chose an increase in the grant amount.



He has never applied for additional government support because he did not know what else was available.

SRD recipient calls on SASSA to invest in skills

His message to SASSA centres on giving recipients the tools to support themselves.

“I would really like SASSA to help people like us, people who have knowledge,” Nxumalo said.



“You know guys how hard it is when you don’t know where to start, where to go,” he added.

He called on the government to invest in people like him with skills, saying “South Africa would gain something”.

“Please SASSA help,” he said. “You know the say about giving a man a fish instead of teaching him to fish.”



Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Nothing mini about this week's medium-term budget speech
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement is sometimes called the mini-budget.

This is because the finance minister doesn't announce changes to taxes, social grants and other details.

Rather, it outlines the government's spending plans for several years.

However, there’s nothing mini about this year’s Medium-Term Budget, as the Middle East war has completely reshaped South Africa’s economy.

Instead of inflation coming down as expected, fuel costs are soaring, and the cost of living crisis is back.

The Reserve Bank has raised interest rates twice in response.

Economists will want to see that despite the setback, government remains disciplined on debt.

The eNCA business desk filed this report.

World.title: Bronkhorstspruit water woes | Resident suffer while councillors point fingers
World.content:
BRONKHORSTSPRUIT - A political blame game has erupted over the Bronkhorstspruit water crisis, leaving sick residents stuck with broken promises instead of clean water.

Residents and civil society groups are demanding answers for the more than 430 cases of stomach-related illnesses that have been reported.

A resident, Carnesta de Jager, says years of promises from councillors have failed to deliver solutions.

Meanwhile, the City of Tshwane has resumed adding chlorine to Bronkhorstspruit water.

READ | Bronkhorstspruit Water Crisis: Tshwane deploys 36 water tankers

But it says its warning that residents should avoid using the water for drinking, cleaning, or washing remains in place.

That's because untreated water could still be in reservoirs and pipes.

The system needs to be flushed.

The city has been blasted for failing to warn residents that their water was unsafe.

READ | Over 400 ill after Tshwane failed to chlorinate Bronkhorstspruit's water

An investigation found that water from the Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Works (BWTW) was unchlorinated from 24 September to 14 October after the city experienced issues with its chlorine supplier.

More than 400 cases of gastrointestinal illness have been reported in the area since early this month. Most of those affected are under the age of four.

Water and Sanitation Minister Pemmy Majodina said corroborated water quality tests found extremely high levels of E.coli and total coliforms in the water emanating from the treatment plant.

World.title: Hyundai recalls 253 Tucson vehicles
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG -Hyundai has recalled 253 Hyundai Tucson NX4 vehicles sold countrywide in 2025.

Some of the vehicles may have faulty side impact airbag sensors.

READ| Certain Hyundai Tucson vehicles recalled

Owners are urged to take their vehicles to an authorised Hyundai dealership for an inspection.

The dealership will confirm whether the sensors are correct.

Any repairs needed will be done for free.

World.title: Rand Water flags areas consuming more water than allocated
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Reduce your water consumption or face forced supply reduction.

That’s the warning from Rand Water as its system faces increased strain.

Municipalities across Gauteng have been blasted for overconsumption.

The City of Joburg ranks high on that list with usage of around 1,801 megalitres of water compared to its allocation of 1,356 megalitres.

READ |Water crisis looming as Rand Water systems face strain

The City of Tshwane consumes an average of 798 megalitres while being allocated 667 megalitres.

The City of Ekurhuleni just misses its threshold of 1,022 megalitres with consumption of 1,005.

Other municipalities on the list include Mogale City, Emfuleni, Madibeng, Merafong and Lesedi.

World.title: Bail ruling appeal could deepen legal woes - Gender activist on Sibiya's case
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Former deputy national police commissioner Shadrack Sibiya could face tougher scrutiny if he appeals his bail judgment.

This is according to a gender activist, Brenda Madumise-Pajibo, after Sibiya's legal team indicated their intention to appeal the ruling.

Madumise-Pajibo said while Sibiya has got the right to explore every avenue available to him in terms of the law, she does not believe the outcome will be any different.

"The facts don't change and if he's going to the higher court, that standard of scrutiny is high and is going to be applying their mind thoroughly. And I don't think they will come to a different conclusion as reached by the magistrate. This case is serious," she explained.

The 59-year-old former police official appeared in the Randburg Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, where he was denied bail.

He faces charges of sexual grooming, human trafficking and the reckless handling of a firearm.

He is accused of raping an 18-year-old woman and sexually grooming a 16-year-old girl.

According to the allegations, Sibiya gave the 18-year-old woman alcohol before she lost consciousness and was raped at a hotel in Sandton.

The National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) says it is prepared to defend the court’s decision to deny Sibiya bail if he challenges the ruling.

World.title: Water crisis looming as Rand Water systems face strain
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Rand Water has warned that a major water supply crisis could be looming as excessive consumption places its entire network under severe pressure.

The pressure comes as several municipal customers have reached what the water utility described as 'exceptionally high levels'.

In a statement on Tuesday, Rand Water said it is already pumping at maximum capacity, but demand continues to rise.

“Sustained overconsumption is making it increasingly difficult to balance supply across the network and heightens the risk of disruptions unless demand is brought under control,” the statement read.

Rand Water has therefore called on all municipal customers to implement immediate measures to reduce consumption and stabilise the system.

READ | Bronkhorstspruit Water Crisis: Tshwane deploys 36 water tankers

Rand Water has now called on municipalities to bring their water use in line with allocated volumes urgently.

It further warned that it would not hesitate to take necessary steps to protect the system and reduce supply to over-consuming customers.

World.title: Singularity Summit South Africa 2026: All you need to know
World.content:
· Two days of global speakers, AI, interactive experiences, an innovation expo and high-level networking come to Sandton this October

JOHANNESBURG - With the Singularity Summit South Africa 2026 almost upon us, business leaders, entrepreneurs, investors, innovators and technology enthusiasts from South Africa and around the world are preparing to gather at the Sandton Convention Centre on Wednesday 21 and Thursday 22 October for two days exploring the technologies and ideas shaping the future.

Presented in collaboration with Old Mutual, event sponsors Google Cloud and Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) and metaverse partner UBU, this year’s Summit will bring together over 40 speakers from 25 cities across 13 countries, alongside a large-scale innovation expo, interactive experiences, panel discussions, networking opportunities and practical opportunities to engage with emerging technologies.

While the Summit stage will host some of the world’s leading thinkers, entrepreneurs and technology specialists, the experience will extend well beyond simply sitting and learning.

“The Summit has always been about creating an environment where people can engage with the future rather than simply hear about it,” says Mic Mann, co-CEO of Singularity South Africa. “You might listen to a global expert unpack where AI is heading, continue that conversation with another delegate over coffee and then walk into the expo and experience some of the technology for yourself. The people in the room are as much a part of the Summit experience as the people on stage.”

Beyond the main stage

Artificial intelligence will be a major focus of the two-day programme, with sessions exploring its impact on business, leadership, investment, skills, entrepreneurship and society. The programme will also examine digital transformation, robotics, biotechnology, the future of cities and other exponential technologies changing the way people live and work.

Speakers will include global and African innovators and specialists such as David Roberts, Felix Cheung, Maureen Costello, Barak Kaufman, Benjamin Rosman, Amanda Manna, Dario Fanucchi, Tilly Lockey, Valter Adão, Danielle Einstein, Fana Shabane, Kim Hulett, Ran Neuner, Hywel George, Marko Stavrou and Rajesh Pasungili.

Acclaimed poet, author and broadcaster Lebo Mashile will return as the Summit’s Poet and MC.

Panel discussions will bring different perspectives into the conversation, while breaks between sessions have deliberately been designed to give delegates time to connect, explore and engage.

The Summit’s expo will bring together a wide range of brands, innovators and technology businesses, with interactive activations giving delegates an opportunity to see, test and experience technologies and ideas beyond the main programme.

Old Mutual will be among the exhibitors, alongside Isazi.ai, Next Biosciences, Dsrupt.ai, Mann Made, Singularity South Africa, Cadena Growth Partners, Exclusive Books, Verascient, Resolute Robotics and Ace Labs.

The wider event partners include Truecaller, Vida, Isazi.ai, Next Biosciences, Dsrupt.ai, Cadena Growth Partners, Exclusive Books, Verascient, Resolute Robotics, Ace Labs, Daytona and Th_rst, with UBU as the Summit’s metaverse event partner.

Delegates will also be able to experience AI learning in a different environment through a mini AI course in the metaverse. The experience will be available on pre-registration day as well as during the mornings of both Summit days, giving delegates an additional opportunity to build their understanding of AI in an interactive format.

“The scale of what happens outside the main auditorium is an important part of what makes the Summit different,” says Shayne Mann, co-CEO of Singularity South Africa. “We want people to meet someone they would never normally have access to, discover a technology they did not know existed, have conversations that challenge the way they think and leave with ideas and connections that continue long after the two days are over.”

Celiwe Ross, Group Chief Human Capital and Corporate Affairs Officer at Old Mutual, says: "Every conversation about AI eventually becomes a conversation about people and how we prepare people to thrive in a changing world of work. For an organisation like Old Mutual, with thousands of colleagues across the continent, that responsibility matters. Singularity creates space for an honest conversation about how we lead through this change, equipping our people to thrive as work evolves, building trust as we go, and scaling innovation in ways that create meaningful and sustainable value."

Connect, experience and participate

Networking is always an important part of the Singularity Summit South Africa 2026, bringing together a high-quality community of executives, entrepreneurs, investors, technology specialists, innovators and other decision-makers from South Africa and abroad.

The Singularity Community app will help delegates navigate and track their Summit journey, while also creating additional networking and engagement opportunities throughout the event.

The experience will continue beyond the formal programme on the first evening, with delegates invited to a cocktail and drinks event featuring DJ Seth Schwartz. The second day will conclude with informal drinks, providing a final opportunity to connect with speakers and fellow delegates.

Parking at the Sandton Convention Centre will be validated for all Summit delegates. For more information, regular updates or to book, visit www.singularitysouthafricaSummit.org.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
