World.title: Pooling Strength for Development, Advancing Common Progress —Marking the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative
World.content:
In September 2021, President Xi Jinping put forward the Global Development Initiative (GDI) at the 76th Session of the United Nations General Assembly, injecting strong impetus into the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and global development endeavors. On 25 September 2026, the High-Level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative was held at UN Headquarters in New York. Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to the Dialogue. Participants expressed readiness to continue to firmly support the GDI, strengthen solidarity and collaboration, and work together to build a more inclusive, sustainable and resilient future.

As President Xi has noted, development is the eternal theme of human society and is key to promoting people’s well-being. Over the past five years, the GDI has been translated from a Chinese vision and proposal into collective global action. More than 130 countries and international organizations actively support the GDI, and they have participated in cooperation under the Initiative. Over 2,000 GDI cooperation projects, tailored to the needs of beneficiary countries, have taken root and delivered outcomes in more than 120 countries. More than 30 GDI cooperation mechanisms and platforms — such as the Global Development Promotion Center Network and the Global Knowledge Network for Development — have been established one after another. More than 10,000 human resources training programs have been organized to share development approaches and practical skills, helping developing countries to build up their capacity for self-reliant development. The GDI helps build a stronger international consensus on putting development first, facilitates mutually beneficial development cooperation, helps fulfill the development aspirations of countries in the Global South, and generated robust momentum for global development.

Liberia is an important member of the Global South family. As a sincere friend and reliable partner of the Liberian people, China has firmly supported Liberia’s national development. When Liberia was hit by the Ebola outbreak in 2014, China offered assistance without delay. Following the COVID-19 outbreak, China provided multiple batches of anti-pandemic aid to Liberia. Chinese medical teams have long worked in Liberia to save lives and safeguard people’s health. In infrastructure, Chinese-aid projects including the two overpasses on the Tubman Boulevard, the National Clinical Diagnosis and Treatment Laboratory, the Fingerprint Laboratory, and the refurbishment and expansion of the Liberia Broadcasting System have been completed, energizing Liberia’s economic and social development. In agriculture, education, human resources and other areas, China has continued to provide food assistance and train professionals, supporting Liberia in pursuing self-sustaining and autonomous development.



The profound changes unseen in a century accelerate across the world, and progress in implementing the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development has fallen seriously behind schedule. The graver the challenges, the more countries need to stand together and jointly advance development. At the above-mentioned High-Level Dialogue, Vice President Han Zheng put forward four proposals: strengthen solidarity and coordination to fully implement the SDGs and fully leverage the GDI’s role as an accelerator; stay action-oriented and implement more “small and beautiful” livelihood projects that deliver real benefits to local people; expand cooperation in priority areas and broaden the scope of GDI cooperation focusing on artificial intelligence (AI), the digital economy, new energy, and disaster prevention and mitigation to foster new drivers for sustainable development; strengthen partnerships and conduct extensive cooperation through relevant bilateral, trilateral and multilateral mechanisms to leverage complementary strengths and create synergy. These propositions will further advance the GDI and create new opportunities for China and Liberia to jointly implement it.

During the meeting between Liberian Foreign Minister Sara Beysolow Nyanti and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in this May, Minister Nyanti stated that Liberia highly commends and firmly supports the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and the series of Global Initiatives, and is ready to strengthen multilateral coordination with China within the UN framework, jointly work for a world of lasting peace and shared prosperity. As both China and Liberia are founding members of the United Nations and members of the UN Security Council, China stands ready to work with Liberia to take the fifth anniversary of the GDI as a new starting point. We will enhance cooperation within the UN framework, uphold true multilateralism, pool development momentum, translate more cooperation outcomes into tangible benefits for the Liberian people, and ensure that the fruits of development are shared more equitably by people across all countries.

World.title: Liberia: House Summons Education Minister, MCSS Superintendent, Teachers Over Prolonged School Closure
World.content:
L-R: Rep. Dixon W. Seboe and Education Minister, Dr. Jarso Maley Jallah

Monrovia — The House of Representatives is expected to question the Minister of Education, Dr. Jarso Maley Jallah, the Superintendent of the Monrovia Consolidated School System (MCSS), Dr. Augurie Stevens, and the leadership of the MCSS Teachers Association over the prolonged shutdown of public schools in Monrovia and its environs.

By Emmanuel Weedee-Conway

The appearance, scheduled for Tuesday, October 20, follows growing concerns over the continued disruption of academic activities more than a month after schools reopened for the new academic year.



The House’s decision came during its sitting last Thursday after Montserrado County District #16 Representative Dixon W. Seboe raised concerns about the standoff between MCSS teachers and the government, warning that the continued closure of schools threatens the education and welfare of thousands of students.

Lawmakers unanimously agreed to summon the education authorities and the teachers’ association leadership to explain the dispute, the status of negotiations, and the measures being taken to restore normal academic activities.

Rep. Seboe described the prolonged shutdown as “worrisome,” urging the House to intervene before the disruption causes further harm to students and their families.

Speaking to reporters after the session, the lawmaker stressed that the continued absence of teachers from classrooms demands urgent attention and accountability from all parties involved.

He said the appearance would give lawmakers an opportunity to establish the facts surrounding the dispute, hear the respective positions of the government and teachers, and identify a path toward reopening the affected schools.

Teachers Demand Superintendent’s Resignation

The latest development follows a directive by MCSS Teachers Association President Augustine N. Nyormui, who called on students to stay away from their campuses and instructed teachers, security personnel, education workers, and cleaners to remain off school premises until their outstanding demands are addressed.

Speaking at a press conference in Monrovia, Nyormui maintained that teachers would not return to the classrooms until MCSS Superintendent Dr. Augurie Stevens resigns.

The decision followed a heated debate during plenary after Montserrado County District #16 Representative Dickson W. Seboe raised issues affecting thousands of students of MCSS and requested the intervention of the House. L-R: MCSS Superintendent Dr. Augurie Stevens and MCSSTA President Augustine N. Nyormui

The demand has intensified the standoff, leaving students in several schools without regular instruction despite the reopening of the academic year.

The prolonged disruption has reportedly frustrated students, with some considering protests over their inability to receive lessons.

The dispute has raised broader concerns about the ability of education authorities and teachers’ representatives to resolve their differences while safeguarding students’ right to education.

Lawmakers Seek Answers

In his communication to the House, Rep. Seboe noted that nearly a month had elapsed since the opening of the academic year without a clear indication that the dispute had been resolved or that teachers were prepared to resume classes.

He warned that continued interruptions could have lasting consequences for students, parents, teachers, and Liberia’s already challenged education system.

The lawmaker urged the House to exercise its constitutional oversight responsibility by bringing the relevant stakeholders before the plenary to explain their positions and outline concrete steps toward resolving the impasse.

During Tuesday’s engagement, Superintendent Stevens is expected to explain the administrative situation within the MCSS and respond to concerns raised by teachers.

Education Minister Jallah is expected to present the government’s position, provide an update on negotiations, and outline efforts to restore normal academic activities.

Meanwhile, the MCSS Teachers Association leadership is expected to detail the teachers’ outstanding demands and clarify the conditions it considers necessary for their return to the classrooms.

Rep. Seboe said the engagement would allow lawmakers to hear directly from all sides, establish the facts, and encourage a peaceful and timely resolution in the interest of affected students.

“The appearance will provide us, the people’s deputies, with further insight into the ongoing disagreement and the prospects for reopening schools across the MCSS. As I said, this shutdown is worrisome,” he said.

The outcome of Tuesday’s engagement could prove critical in determining whether the parties can reach an agreement to reopen schools and prevent further disruption to the academic year.

World.title: Can Constructive Journalism Help Liberia Turn National Challenges Into Development Solutions?
World.content:
BEIJING, China — Liberia’s development challenges are well documented, from poor road connectivity and limited economic opportunities to inadequate public services and persistent difficulties attracting investment. But what if journalism could do more than expose these problems? What if it could also identify practical solutions, encourage institutional responses and showcase the country’s untapped potential?

By Willie N. Tokpah

That question is at the center of a two-week international communication seminar bringing together 23 Liberian journalists in China to examine how constructive journalism, public diplomacy and development storytelling could contribute to national progress.



Sponsored by China’s Ministry of Commerce at the request of the Government of the People’s Republic of China, the seminar brings together practitioners from print, broadcast and digital media to explore China’s experiences in international communication, media development and development-oriented reporting.

Among the participants is Willie N. Tokpah of FrontPage Africa, who is joining fellow journalists to examine approaches that could strengthen Liberia’s media capacity and encourage more solutions-oriented public-interest reporting.

For Liberia, the experience raises a critical question: Can journalism become a stronger bridge between citizens’ concerns, government accountability and practical ideas for development?

Beyond Exposing Problems

Constructive journalism moves beyond identifying problems to examine responses, assess results and highlight practical approaches that could be adapted to local circumstances.

It does not require journalists to abandon investigative reporting or soften criticism of public officials. Instead, it complements scrutiny with evidence-based reporting that examines what works, what fails and what lessons can be learned.

In Liberia, such an approach could transform coverage of persistent development challenges.

Reporting on impassable farm-to-market roads, for example, could document farmers’ economic losses while investigating road-maintenance models, financing arrangements and communities that have improved rural access.

Coverage of youth unemployment could examine vocational training, agricultural enterprises and small-business financing, including barriers preventing graduates from entering the workforce.

Similarly, reporting on sanitation, education, healthcare and local governance could scrutinize public spending while examining community initiatives and practical solutions.

The objective is not to manufacture positive news or shield the government from criticism. It is to provide citizens with a fuller understanding of public problems while generating credible information that can inform action.

Chinese Scholars Highlight Journalism’s Development Role

During the seminar’s first week, Chinese communication scholars and media officials encouraged participants to consider how journalism can contribute to national development.

Professor Zang Yanqiu, director of the Africa Research Center at the Communication University of China, described constructive reporting as an approach through which journalists identify problems, alert relevant authorities and examine efforts to find workable solutions.

“The journalism profession should be used for the good of the community,” Professor Zang stated.

She urged participants to produce reports that reflect national consciousness and contribute to development.

Chang Jin, a second-level counselor in the Department of International Cooperation at China’s National Radio and Television Administration, also discussed communication’s role in China’s development experience.

“It is the media responsibility to report in a way that advances the government’s development agenda,” Chang noted.

For Liberian journalists, however, applying these lessons requires adapting them to Liberia’s constitutional protections, independent media traditions and accountability needs.

Journalism must retain its responsibility to question authority, investigate wrongdoing and provide citizens with reliable information. Engagement with public institutions cannot replace independent verification, nor should national image-building take precedence over the public’s right to know.

The challenge is to combine rigorous scrutiny with reporting that helps people understand potential solutions and determine whether promised interventions deliver results.

From Beijing to Anji: Learning Through Experience

Beyond classroom instruction, the journalists travelled to Anji County in Huzhou City, Zhejiang Province, to examine the relationship between communication, tourism, environmental protection and local development.

One major stop was Yucun Village, associated with the development philosophy expressed in the phrase, “Lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets,” linked to Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The village has become a prominent example of efforts to connect environmental protection with economic development, particularly through tourism and environmentally conscious agricultural practices.

For the delegation, the visit offered an opportunity to examine how natural resources and local identity can become economic assets when supported by planning, infrastructure and sustained promotion.

The implications for Liberia are significant. The country’s forests, beaches, rivers, waterfalls and cultural heritage could support tourism, generate employment and attract investment. But these resources require reliable infrastructure, environmental safeguards, accessible services and meaningful community participation.

Through well-researched reporting, Liberian journalists could promote lesser-known destinations, investigate barriers to tourism and document initiatives connecting conservation with sustainable livelihoods.

The objective would be to tell Liberia’s development stories without simply reproducing another country’s model.

What Liberia Could Learn From Rural Transformation

The delegation also visited the Anji County Smart Governance Center, where participants examined the use of technology and administrative systems to coordinate social and economic services.

The experience raised questions about how Liberian county administrations could improve responses to citizens’ complaints, publish clearer information about development projects and enable communities to monitor the implementation of roads, schools, clinics and other public facilities.

Instead of reporting only when projects are launched, newsrooms could follow them through implementation and completion, documenting expenditures, delays, community feedback and measurable outcomes.

Such reporting would help citizens compare official promises with results while giving public officials a clearer picture of local concerns.

The seminar also exposed participants to China’s rural transformation experience, including efforts to address natural-resource depletion and develop alternative livelihoods.

For Liberia, where many rural communities depend on farming, fishing and forests, the connection between environmental protection and economic opportunity is particularly relevant.

However, any adaptation must account for Liberia’s land rights, customary institutions, community consent, environmental conditions and available resources. The lesson is to examine experiences elsewhere and determine which ideas can work within Liberia’s circumstances.

Building Liberia’s International Image Through Better Storytelling

The seminar also examines international communication, public diplomacy, digital media, disinformation and the changing global media landscape.

These subjects have implications for Liberia’s efforts to attract tourism, expand trade, promote investment and strengthen international partnerships.

A country’s image is shaped not only by official statements and diplomatic engagements but also by stories about its people, institutions, economy and natural environment.

Responsible image-building does not mean concealing corruption, economic hardship or governance failures. It means broadening the narrative through credible reporting on entrepreneurship, agricultural innovation, cultural heritage, environmental conservation and community initiatives.

A report about a rural entrepreneur creating jobs, for instance, could examine both the achievement and the obstacles to expanding the business. A tourism feature could showcase a destination while investigating road access, visitor safety and whether surrounding communities benefit economically.

Such coverage could promote Liberia’s potential while retaining the scrutiny necessary to make development claims credible.

Giving Citizens a Voice in Development

Constructive communication also raises questions about how citizens can participate more directly in shaping development priorities.

Local radio stations, community newspapers, online platforms and public forums could provide opportunities for communities to identify problems, propose responses and assess institutional performance.

A community facing recurring flooding, for example, could work with journalists to document affected areas, consult residents and technical experts, examine drainage proposals and follow the response of local authorities.

Similarly, farmers struggling to transport produce could identify priority road repairs and assess whether proposed solutions improve market access.

For this approach to work, citizen participation must be meaningful. Authorities should explain which proposals can be implemented, which require additional resources and why others may not be feasible.

Journalists must then follow up to determine whether commitments produce measurable improvements.

Turning Training Into Results

The two-week seminar combines classroom instruction with field visits, exposing the 23 journalists to China’s experiences in communication, public diplomacy and development.

The real test, however, will come after they return to Liberia.

The lessons could inform newsroom initiatives such as solutions-focused reporting series, investigations into public projects, community development features and multimedia stories showcasing Liberia’s economic and cultural potential.

Newsrooms could adopt standards requiring reporters to identify problems, examine proposed responses, consult affected communities, verify evidence and assess whether interventions are producing results.

These safeguards would help prevent constructive journalism from becoming a public-relations exercise or a platform for repeating official claims.

Ultimately, the value of the approach will not be measured by how positively stories portray Liberia or its leaders, but by whether they improve public understanding, strengthen accountability and help citizens evaluate possible solutions.

China’s experience offers an opportunity to examine how communication can support development and international engagement. But Liberia’s path must be shaped by its own democratic institutions, public needs and social realities.

The country needs journalism that exposes corruption, questions public spending and investigates abuse. It also needs reporting that examines workable alternatives, highlights local innovation and helps citizens understand how development challenges might be addressed.

These responsibilities are not mutually exclusive.

For Liberia, the opportunity presented by the seminar is not simply to learn how another country communicates its achievements. It is to consider how journalists can connect public concerns with evidence, practical ideas and sustained accountability.

If the training leads to more rigorous reporting on development solutions, stronger citizen participation and credible storytelling about Liberia’s potential, its benefits could extend beyond the journalists themselves.

Ultimately, constructive journalism must do more than make government look good. It must help the public understand problems, evaluate responses and demand results.

The 23 journalists are expected to receive international certificates upon completion of the training.

World.title: Beyond The Diploma: YEIB-MANCO CEO Urges Graduates to Embrace Entrepreneurship, Integrity and Service
World.content:
Monrovia — Youth Entrepreneurship and Investment Bank Management Company (YEIB-MANCO) Chief Executive Officer Joseph Fatorma Sando has challenged Liberian graduates to turn their education into entrepreneurial opportunities, practical solutions and meaningful service to their communities.

By Patience Jones

Sando said academic qualifications alone were insufficient to guarantee success, urging young people to apply their knowledge to address societal challenges, create opportunities and contribute to Liberia’s development.



He made the call on Saturday, October 17, when he delivered the keynote address at the graduation and closing ceremony of St. James Foundation Elementary, Junior and Senior High School in Peace Community, Upper Caldwell, Montserrado County. More than 50 students graduated from the institution.

Speaking on the theme “Beyond the Diploma,” Sando outlined five principles he said should guide the graduates as they transition from secondary education to higher learning, entrepreneurship and professional life: continuous learning, integrity, problem-solving, resilience and community service.

Education Must Translate Into Impact

Sando told the graduates that completing high school should mark the beginning of a lifelong commitment to learning, rather than the end of their educational journey.

He encouraged them to cultivate the habit of reading, acquiring new skills and pursuing excellence in whatever careers they choose.

“The world is fast-changing, and only those who remain curious and committed to excellence will remain relevant,” he said, urging the graduates to make excellence a defining feature of their work.

Whether pursuing careers in medicine, teaching, business, agriculture or other fields, he said, young people should strive to perform their responsibilities to the highest standard.

The YEIB-MANCO chief executive also emphasized integrity, warning that academic certificates without good character could undermine a person’s prospects for lasting success.

He urged the graduates to remain honest and trustworthy, even when doing so becomes difficult or unpopular, arguing that integrity builds the trust necessary for personal and professional advancement.

‘Be a Solution, Not a Problem’

Sando challenged the Class of 2026 to become problem-solvers who identify challenges in their communities and develop practical responses.

He said Liberia needs young people who can use their education and creativity to address local problems instead of merely complaining about them.

According to him, communities across the country face challenges that require innovation, initiative and the active participation of educated young people.

He also cautioned the graduates against allowing setbacks and disappointments to derail their ambitions.

Acknowledging that life after high school would present difficulties, Sando encouraged them to develop resilience, remain determined and continue pursuing their goals despite rejection or failure.

“You will be disappointed, you will fail at times, you will be rejected, but never surrender,” he said, stressing that the ability to recover from setbacks is essential to achieving long-term goals.

Calls for Community Service and Entrepreneurship

Sando further urged the graduates to embrace entrepreneurship, discipline and patriotism, emphasizing that education should benefit not only individuals but also the wider society.

He encouraged them to give back to Peace Community, Upper Caldwell, and Liberia through volunteering, mentoring younger people and participating in community development initiatives.

He said the value of education should also be measured by how graduates use their knowledge and skills to improve the lives of others.

Sando added that Liberia’s development depends partly on a generation of young people who are skilled, ethical, innovative and willing to serve their country.

School Honors Sando for Support to Students

In recognition of his contributions to the institution and its students, the administration and faculty of St. James Foundation Elementary, Junior and Senior High School presented Sando with an academic gown during a special ceremony.

The presentation, which was met with applause from parents, students and community leaders, was conducted by the school’s principal and senior faculty members.

The administration described Sando as a supportive partner and friend of the institution, citing his financial, moral, spiritual and academic assistance to students, particularly children from less privileged backgrounds in Peace Community.

School officials said his continued involvement and encouragement had contributed to efforts to support the education and development of young Liberians.

Responding to the honor, Sando expressed gratitude to the administration and faculty, describing the recognition as humbling and motivating.

He reaffirmed his commitment to supporting education and youth empowerment in Liberia.

The ceremony brought together parents, teachers, community leaders, and other well-wishers to celebrate the graduates’ achievements and encourage them as they prepare for the next stage of their lives.

The program concluded with the presentation of certificates and awards to students recognized for academic performance and good conduct. The class valedictorian delivered a vote of thanks on behalf of the graduating class.

World.title: Liberia: Full Gospel Nigeria Fellowship Equips Liberian Counterparts
World.content:
MONROVIA – Dr. Jude Ememe at the head of a 7-man high-level delegation under the auspices of the Full Gospel Business Men’s Fellowship International Nigeria, arrived in Liberia on Thursday, October 15 and has been involved in series of activities including capacity – building aimed at enhancing the leadership ability of the Full Gospel Business Men’s Fellowship International Liberia.

By Augustus D.R Bortue

Other members of the delegation include Dr. Godwin Edozie, Barrister Isaac Okpanachi, National President of Nigeria (FGBMFI), Bro. Stephen Okruefe and Mr. & Mrs. Joseph Mamodu.



The fellowship established in 1952 by an American Christian businessman, Demos Shakarian, in California is a global movement of Christians from different denominations and diverse expertise, working together to propagate the Gospel of Jesus Christ in fulfillment of the Great Commission.

Although the fellowship started initially with frustration and disappointments characterized by poor attendance in initial meetings and lack of money, it has been organized in about 163 countries worldwide.

In addition, millions of lives have been impacted globally through groups of ordinary Christians laymen inspired by a God-given vision that was originally imparted to Demos Shakarian.

During one of the training sessions held at Evelyn Restaurant in Sinkor, Monrovia, Dr. Edozie said Full Gospel is a spiritual work that has a vision and mission.

In order to become successful in life, Dr. Edozie encouraged his fellow believers to always factor God first in their plan and allow the Holy Spirit to provide guidance and direction in their Christian journey.

Dr. Edozie added that the fellowship is not a church, but rather a network of professionals having strong passion and commitment in winning souls using their God-given gifts and sharing of testimonies which inspire individuals to join the body of Christ,

On Saturday, October 17, a joint breakfast meeting took place at the Bella Casa Hotel on 2nd Street in Sinkor, Monrovia and brought together participants representing four chapters that have been established in Liberia.

In his welcome remarks, the National President of the FGBMFI-Liberia, Arthur Fumbah, extended profound gratitude and described the visit by the

Nigerian FGBMFI as a clear manifestation of their desire to help Liberia become stronger and more effective in managing chapters to the glory of God.

Fumbah reflected on the warm reception accorded to them during their visit to Nigeria in 2019. Regarding progress, he said the guest, Liberia has established four chapters, and expressed optimism that additional chapters would be established in the coming year.

The main speaker at the breakfast meeting was the National President of the FGBMFI of Nigeria, who is a Solicitor, Advocate and Notary Public.

Isaac Okpanachi challenged executives of the Liberian FGBMFI to engage those in authority to always reference God first as they provide stewardship for the country since, in fact, Liberia is a Nation Founded on Christian principles.

He further prayed for the nation and asked God to use the Full Gospel Fellowship in heading and reconciling Liberia.

Moderating the breakfast meeting was Liberia’s FGBMFI Eminent Chapter President, Dr. Nathania T. Blama, Sr., assisted by Bro. Wilson Gaglo-Delali, National Prayer Coordinator, while sister Mama Wesaye led the praise & Worship Team.

World.title: Liberia to Digitalize 16 Key Government Services with World Bank Support
World.content:
MONROVIA, Liberia — The Government of Liberia, with support from the World Bank, has begun taking steps to digitalize 16 priority government services in a move aimed at making public services more accessible, efficient, and responsive to the needs of citizens.

The initiative is expected to introduce a more integrated digital government system, allowing citizens to access multiple public services through a single online platform while enabling government institutions to share information more efficiently.

At the center of the initiative is the proposed e-Liberia Platform, envisioned as a one-stop shop for government services. The project also includes the development of a Government Service Bus (GSB) to facilitate real-time information sharing among public institutions, upgrades to the National Data Center, and the digitalization of County Service Centers across the country.



The initiative could mark an important step in reducing the delays and administrative challenges often associated with accessing public services, although its impact will ultimately depend on effective implementation, reliable digital infrastructure, and citizens’ ability to access and use the new systems.

To prepare for implementation, the Office of the Chief Information Officer of Liberia hosted a working session over the weekend, bringing together representatives from participating ministries and agencies.

The meeting focused on validating the status of the 16 priority services, assessing institutional and technical readiness, reviewing existing digital systems and business processes, and identifying appropriate procurement arrangements to support the initiative.

Participants also examined the technical requirements for integrating government institutions into the proposed digital ecosystem, including the Government Service Bus, e-Liberia Portal, application programming interfaces (APIs), and shared digital infrastructure.

Discussions further addressed outstanding requirements, institutional responsibilities, implementation timelines, and the next steps needed to move the project from planning toward execution.

Speaking at the session, Liberia’s Chief Information Officer, Sheikh Sheriff, praised the Government of Liberia and the World Bank for supporting the initiative, describing it as a significant milestone in the country’s digital transformation efforts.

World.title: U-17 Women target recovery against Venezuela
World.content:
The Zambia Under-17 Women’s National Team will be looking for recovery when they face Venezuela in their second Group D match at the ongoing FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Wednesday.

The match will kick off at 20h00 CAT at the Mohammed VI Football Complex.

Zambia goes into the clash after suffering a 5-0 opening day defeat to Japan, while Venezuela fell 2-0 to France in the other Group D encounter.

Both teams are facing high stakes, with another defeat leaving their last-16 hopes hanging by a thread.

Despite the heavy loss, Zambia coach Carol Kanyemba says her girls remain upbeat.

“We have been encouraging the girls that losing one game is not the end of the tournament. That was a setback, but it should be a turning point. As we prepare for the match against Venezuela, we are telling our girls to have the right attitude toward the game,” Kanyemba said.

“The game against Venezuela is an opportunity for us to progress from this group stage. It will be a physical game against Venezuela. Venezuela plays like us Africans. We are telling the girls that we can get maximum points from this game,” she added.

Zambia made it to the Round of 16 at last year’s tournament after a first-round elimination in 2024, and Kanyemba, who has led the team to three successive World Cups in 2024, 2025 and 2026, is aiming to continue the progressive route.

Team captain Taonga Mubanga says Wednesday’s game will determine Zambia’s destiny.

“We are very much ready and prepared for the match against Venezuela. It won’t be an easy game, but we have worked on the mistake played in the previous game,” Mubanga said.

“The game against Venezuela is a must win for us and we will win. This game will show us if we qualify to the round of 16,” she said.

Debutant Dorcas Mulosha echoed the captain’s sentiments.

“Preparations for the match against Venezuela are going on well and we are very ready. This match is very important to us; this match will motivate us. We lost and Venezuela lost so this match will be tough,” Mulosha said.

France and Japan are the other teams in Group D. The top two teams in each group will qualify to the round of 16, while three best third-placed teams will also make the cut.

World.title: Copper rod exports underway at Chibombo MFEZ
World.content:
Zambia is now exporting copper rods while manufacturing copper cables and wires for the domestic market, using copper produced by mines within the country.

Ministry of Information and Media Director Spokesperson, Henry Kapata, who disclosed the development to the media in Lusaka today, said the difference is happening at the Jiangxi Multi-Facility Economic Zone in Chibombo District, Kembe East Constituency, Central Province, where copper is being processed into products for local industries and export markets.

Mr Kapata said inside the facility, Jiangxi Copper Zambia is manufacturing copper rods, cables and wires.

He noted that the company’s copper rods are exported to neighboring countries, while its cables and wires are sold locally to mining and construction companies.

“The company has about 93 local employees, ” said Mr Kapata.

Meanwhile, Deputy General Manager, Cooper Zeng, also disclosed that the company was recording approximately US$700,000 in cable sales in Zambia.

Mr Cooper says the period covered by that sales figure was not specified, adding that the company is also looking at expansion.

He noted that plans were underway for another copper production line, which could produce approximately 1,000 tonnes per month.

“This is a planned expansion, not its current production capacity,” said Mr Cooper.

Beyond copper processing, the industrial zone is attracting investment in other manufacturing activities, including vehicle batteries, lithium battery products, solar power storage batteries, battery recycling and transformers.

Zamtrans Electrical is among the companies manufacturing and assembling transformers at the zone, while Xiamen Better Technology Group has been associated with investment in vehicle batteries, solar storage batteries and waste battery recycling.

These industries connect local manufacturing to Zambia’s electricity expansion, energy storage and transport ambitions.

The Jiangxi Multi-Facility Economic Zone was officially commissioned by President Hakainde Hichilema on 13 October 2023 and since then, the zone has continued attracting investors across different industries, with manufacturing activities developing around copper products, electrical equipment and batteries.

The progress is significant because Zambia’s economic ambitions extend beyond extracting minerals from the ground. Local processing and manufacturing create opportunities to supply domestic industries, export value-added products, develop skills and expand employment.

And Mr Kapata says with Zambia targeting annual copper production of 3 million metric tonnes by 2031, the challenge is not only to mine more copper, but also to expand the industries that can turn that resource into products and economic opportunities.

He says these developments connect directly to the Grow Zambia Agenda, particularly its ambitions for copper production, energy expansion, industrialisation and job creation.

“The Jiangxi Multi-Facility Economic Zone is still in the early stages of production and industrial growth. Yet the copper rods being exported, the cables and wires being supplied locally, and the investments in batteries and transformers offer a practical illustration of the direction Zambia is pursuing: producing more, processing more locally and building industries around its own resources,” he said.

Mr Kapata further added that the question is no longer only how much copper Zambia can mine, but how much more value the country can create from copper before it leaves its borders.

World.title: Chisamba man convicted for stealing 11 herds of cattle
World.content:
Chisamba Subordinate Court has sentenced a 58-year-old man to five years’ imprisonment with hard labour for stealing eleven herds of cattle valued at K132,000.00.

Magistrate Litungi Litungi convicted Sunny Kasempa of Chief Chamuka’s area for stock theft but acquitted his 39-year-old co-accused, Carlos Chileshe, after finding insufficient evidence linking him to the offence.

The court heard that between October 1, 2025 and December 5, 2025, the two allegedly stole ten oxen and one cow belonging to Dana Ngululu Phiri.

During the trial, four prosecution witnesses testified that eleven herds of cattle had gone missing from Phiri’s farm, which had 179 herds.

The court further heard that one of the missing animals was found among the livestock belonging to Humphrey Siachikoli, who told the farm manager, Manson Shamakamba, that he had bought it from Kasempa for K6,800.00.

Another ox was recovered from Kasempa’s kraal and identified by its 7B7N brand mark.

In his defence, Kasempa who called two witnesses told the court that he had bought the two animals from Chileshe, while Chileshe maintained that he had only been hired to help move the animals to Kasempa’s kraal.

“In early October,2025, I was called by Mr Kasempa to meet him at Katete area and upon our meeting, he told me that his son from Kabwe had sent him two cattle which were tied to a tree,” Mr Chileshe said.

However, Magistrate Litungi found Kasempa guilty of stock theft but acquitted Chileshe, ruling that there was no evidence linking him to the offence.

In mitigation, Kasempa asked the court for leniency, saying he was married with eight children, four of whom were in school, and was also responsible for caring for his grandchildren.

He further told the court that his wife had suffered a stroke following his arrest.

Kasempa had previously absconded court after being granted K50,000.00 bail in his own recognisance.

He was later apprehended by his sureties after the court issued a warrant of arrest.

On September 24, 2026, Magistrate Litungi revoked his bail and ordered him to pay K50,000.00 or serve nine months’ simple imprisonment.

“The punishment for theft of stock in the case of a first offender is imprisonment for a term of not less than five years but not exceeding 15 years. However, I have taken into account your factors,” Magistrate Litungi said.

Magistrate Litungi sentenced Kasempa, who is already serving a nine months’ simple imprisonment for jumping bail, to five years’ imprisonment with hard labour, to take effect after he completes his current sentence.

World.title: Senior Chief Sikufele urges proper use of mosquito nets
World.content:
Senior Chief Sikufele of Manyinga and Kabompo districts has commended the government for its continued efforts to protect communities from malaria through the provision of insecticide-treated mosquito nets.

Senior Chief Sikufele says the distribution of treated mosquito nets is an important intervention in reducing malaria infections and protecting vulnerable groups, particularly pregnant women and children.

He was speaking in Manyinga today when a delegation from the Kabompo District Health Department paid a courtesy call on him over the commencement of the mosquito net distribution exercise.

Senior Chief Sikufele said that the consistent and correct use of mosquito nets was essential in preventing mosquito bites and reducing malaria cases in his chiefdom.

The traditional leaders however, expressed concern over the misuse of mosquito nets by some residents, who reportedly use them for activities such as maize shelling and fishing urging them to use the nets for their intended purpose.

Senior Chief Sikufele further emphasised the importance of community participation in the fight against malaria, calling on residents to take advantage of the government-supported intervention by ensuring that they sleep under mosquito nets every night.

The District Health Office has received a total of 53,956 insecticide-treated mosquito nets for distribution across the entire district.

The distribution comes against the backdrop of a significant malaria burden in the district, which recorded an incidence rate of 1,235.33 cases per 1,000 people in 2025.

The figures underscore the continued need for preventive measures, public awareness and community involvement in reducing malaria infections.

World.title: Councils urged to ensure projects are completed- Dr Pollen
World.content:
Local Government and Rural Development Permanent Secretary for Administration, Gabriel Pollen, says councils plays a critical role in improving the welfare of communities through effective service delivery and inclusive development.

Dr Pollen has since called on Chongwe Mayor, Frederick Sashi, to work closely with all councilors, regardless of their political affiliations, to ensure that development projects are implemented and completed through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF).

Speaking during the installation of the Mayor in Chongwe district, Dr Pollen said development must be inclusive and benefit all sections of society, including women, young people and persons with disabilities.

“Development must be inclusive and this includes women, youths and persons with disabilities,” Dr Pollen said.

He urged the local authority to prioritise the Keep Zambia Clean, Green and Healthy campaign, emphasising that maintaining a clean and healthy environment was a collective responsibility.

Dr Pollen said the installation of Mr Sashi marked the beginning of a new chapter in the development of the district.

He urged the newly installed mayor to serve the people with humility, integrity and dedication while upholding the rule of law.

Dr Pollen further encouraged council workers to discharge their duties professionally and work together to improve service delivery.

He called on the local authority to ensure that the construction of the new market was completed and that traders were relocated to designated trading areas to curb street vending.

Former Chongwe Mayor, Christopher Habeenzu, has congratulated Mr Sashi on assuming the mantle of leadership and urged councilors to support the mayor in delivering development to the district.

Mr Habeenzu said all councilors have been elected by the people and should therefore work together in the interest of the community.

He noted that several development projects were undertaken during his tenure, including the procurement of an earth-moving machine to enhance service delivery in the district.

Mr Habeenzu said the initiatives contributed to improving community welfare, adding that services such as fire response and revenue collection had also improved.

Mr Sashi thanked the people of Chongwe for electing him as mayor, pledging to serve them with integrity and commitment.

He also expressed gratitude to all those who supported him throughout his political journey and acknowledged the contribution of his predecessor in laying a foundation for continued development.

“I thank everyone who has supported me since I began my political journey and I also wish to thank the outgoing mayor for laying a good foundation,” he said.

He pledged to push forward outstanding development projects, support the national development agenda and promote job creation in the district.

Mr Sashi called for teamwork among councilors and council officials, regardless of their political affiliations, saying unity was essential to achieving meaningful development.

Chongwe Town Clerk, Carol Mkandawire, congratulated Mr Sashi on his election, noting that he had a significant responsibility to advance development in the district.

Ms Mkandawire said the local authority should align its development programmes with the Grow Zambia Agenda and work towards achieving the targets under the 10-10-5-3-3-1-1.1 framework.

She added that the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) was an important resource that could help the council implement developmental projects and improve the welfare of residents.

World.title: ZAFFICO unveils new corporate identity
World.content:
The Zambia Forestry and Forest Industries Corporation (ZAFFICO) has unveiled a new corporate identity and has adopted ZAFFICO Plc as its full corporate name, replacing Zambia Forestry and Forest Industries Corporation, while retaining the familiar ZAFFICO identity that has served it for decades.

The company has also signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Microfinance Zambia Limited to expand access to timber products through flexible financing arrangements.

ZAFFICO Plc Managing Director, Mundia Mundia, says the rebranding and partnership were part of the company’s transformation strategy aimed at strengthening its competitiveness, promoting value addition and contributing to Zambia’s economic growth.

Speaking at the event in Lusaka today, Mr Mundia said the new identity was intended to enhance the company’s visibility and recognition as it expanded into value-added timber products and industrial processing.

“The new identity reflects our transformation journey and our ambition to strengthen our competitiveness in the forestry and timber industry,” he said.

He added that the financing arrangement with Microfinance Zambia Limited would enable public and private sector employees, homeowners, small-scale traders and businesses to acquire timber and other forestry products through manageable instalments.

Mr Mundia said the facility would cover timber, treated poles, seedlings, sawdust, wood chips and particle boards once production begins at the company’s planned particle board factory.

He also indicated that the partnership is aligned with the government’s Grow Zambia Agenda by promoting inclusive economic growth, job creation, home ownership and the development of local value chains.

And, Mr Mundia revealed that ZAFFICA Plc was investing in expanding its wood processing capacity, including a particle board factory costing about US$30 Million in Kalulushi, which is expected to be commissioned in 2028.

Meanwhile, Microfinance Zambia Limited Managing Director, James Chona, said the partnership would help address challenges related to access to affordable financing, particularly among small and medium-sized enterprises.

Mr Chona said the facility would enable customers to obtain financing for timber and other products without having to raise the full purchase amount upfront.

“The partnership will make it easier for customers to access financing and acquire the products they need without paying the full amount upfront,” Mr Chona said.

He noted that the partnership was designed to promote financial inclusion by helping even small-scale traders and suppliers’ access financing to grow their businesses.

Mr Chona further urged the media and other stakeholders to publicise the initiative to ensure that more eligible customers benefit from the facility.

World.title: Mundubile Bail Hearing Moved To Wednesday After State Seeks More Time
World.content:
The constitutional bail application by opposition leader Mr Brian Mundubile and 17 others accused of treason failed to proceed in the Lusaka High Court after the State said it was not ready. The court moved the hearing to Wednesday, while the accused remain in custody.

The adjournment came after acting Chief State Advocate Chibesa Mulonda asked for more time to file an affidavit opposing the application. A three-judge panel granted the request. The panel comprises Ndola High Court Judge Derrick Mulenga, who leads it, Justice Davies Chibwili and Justice Ireen Wishimanga.

The 18 accused, who include Mr Makebi Zulu, face treason and terrorism-related charges. They had been transported from Mukobeko Maximum Correctional Facility in Kabwe and were at the court premises by 07:00 hours.

Defence lawyer State Counsel Sakwiba Sikota said the accused had been woken at around 04:00 hours and driven to Lusaka on empty stomachs. He said no provision had been made for their breakfast.

“We have hurriedly organised some food for them so that at least they can have something to eat because they were brought with no provision for breakfast,” Mr Sikota said. “The State didn’t seem to be bothered or make an attempt to provide for that.”

Mr Sikota said the defence had served the State with the bail summons the previous Thursday. In his view, that left the prosecution with ample time to prepare its response.

“We had served the State last Thursday; they have had the documents for a number of days now. However, today the State said they were not ready and asked for an adjournment to enable them to put in documents in opposition,” he said.

Under the timetable set by the court, the State was ordered to serve the defence with its documents by lunchtime on the day of the adjournment. The defence must then file any answer and an affidavit in reply the following day, ahead of the hearing on Wednesday at 08:30 hours.

“They have been ordered to serve us with whatever they have in their possession,” Mr Sikota said, adding that the matter would be heard on Wednesday.

The accused were not present in chambers when the adjournment was granted. Mr Sikota explained that proceedings had not moved beyond procedural arrangements, and the legal team later briefed the applicants in the court holding cells.

Mr Mundubile, the National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) presidential candidate in the general election, is joined in the application by figures from business, the church and the legal profession. Among the other accused are business executive Mr Harry Findlay, former Anglican Bishop Trevor Mwamba, Mr Patrick Mwansa and lawyer Mr George Chisanga.

The group is linked to alleged militia activities during the general elections. These are allegations they will have the opportunity to answer before the court.

At the heart of their application is the length of their detention. The applicants argue that keeping them in custody while investigations remain incomplete violates their constitutional rights.

They accept that the State is entitled to investigate criminal allegations. They contend, however, that incomplete investigations cannot justify prolonged detention without judicial proceedings.

The applicants say the law guarantees them the right to be brought before a court without undue delay. If they are not tried within a reasonable time, they argue, they must be released either unconditionally or on reasonable conditions.

Court documents show that the applicants also raise alleged irregularities relating to remand warrants, their conditions of detention and their access to medical care. They maintain that despite being arrested last month and remaining in custody, they have not yet been presented before a competent court.

The application cites the alleged apprehension of Mr Ezra Tolopo, Mr Dickson Tembo and Mr Victor Muzyamba at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on 1 August. The applicants claim the three were then held at unknown locations for more than nine days.

The applicants are seeking release pending trial, either unconditionally or on conditions the court considers appropriate. They also want a declaration that their continued detention, without trial within a reasonable time, violates their constitutional rights.

Attorney General Mulilo Kabesha and two others are cited as respondents.

The applicants maintain that no judicial determination has authorised their continued incarceration. They say they are ready to answer the charges against them before a competent court.

The panel led by Judge Mulenga will hear arguments from both the State and the defence on Wednesday at 08:30 hours. The 18 accused remain in detention until then.

World.title: Publish The List: Katuta Demands Names And Evidence On Civil Servants Facing Dismissal
World.content:
Former Chiengi Member of Parliament Ms Given Katuta demanded that Government publish the names of civil servants lined up for dismissal over allegedly supporting the opposition. She also called for the evidence against each of them to be made public, saying dismissals without proof amount to injustice.

Ms Katuta, who stood as an independent presidential candidate in the August general election, was responding to remarks attributed to a senior UPND official that more civil servants seen as working against President Hakainde Hichilema would be removed.

She said threatening public workers with dismissal “in the national interest” without any evidence of wrongdoing was a serious injustice inflicted by Government on its own people. She set out three demands on behalf of citizens.

“We therefore demand as citizens: Publish the list. Who are these civil servants? From which ministries and departments?” Ms Katuta said.

“Show the evidence. How did they work against the government? Where is the proof? Follow due process. Civil servants serve the Republic of Zambia, not a political party.”

Ms Katuta questioned whether it was fair for the ruling UPND to condemn workers in this way without giving them access to due process. She said the reports had left her deeply troubled. “Is this fair? Is this unity?” she asked. “My heart is heavy.”

She traced the pattern back to the Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency (ZAMMSA), where she said all employees had been dismissed. In her view, the civil service was now facing the same treatment.

“First, it was the firing of all ZAMMSA employees. Now it is civil servants to be ‘retired in the national interest’. Where is the fairness in this?” Ms Katuta said.

“If someone has a case to answer, let the law take its course. But to condemn a whole group and label them as ‘working against government’ without evidence is not justice.”

Ms Katuta said Government would struggle to promote unity if it continued to target anyone it perceived to be sympathetic to the opposition. She warned that the country was already in a tense atmosphere and that any attempt to inflame it further would be catastrophic.

She pointed to the timing of the remarks, which came soon after the nation observed the Day of Prayer, Fasting and Reconciliation on 18 October.

“My question is simple: How does this promote unity? Our country is already tense,” she said. “We talked about forgiveness, like President Mwanawasa forgiving President Sata. Now, a day later, we are talking about more firings?”

“This will not unite us. It will divide us more. It will create fear in the civil service instead of professionalism.”

Ms Katuta said those responsible for running a disciplined civil service should follow established procedure rather than resort to what she described as emotional blackmail. She called for an immediate halt to what she termed blanket dismissals.

“What is the best way forward? For now, stop this blanket firing. Use disciplinary procedures. Give people a chance to be heard. That is what the law says,” she said.

Looking further ahead, she argued for a public service insulated from party politics. “For the future, let us depoliticise the civil service. Let us remember that governments come and go, but Zambia remains,” Ms Katuta said.

“A teacher, a nurse, a clerk is not UPND or NRPUP or PF; they are Zambians serving Zambians.”

She closed her appeal with a call for genuine reconciliation, saying the nation could only move forward if leaders chose healing over punishment.

“Let us choose reconciliation over retribution. Unity over victimisation. Zambia is bigger than all of us,” she said.

ZAMMSA, the agency Ms Katuta cited, is currently advertising 23 categories of vacancies, from quality assurance and laboratory services to finance, internal audit and risk management. Applications close on 25 October.

Her three demands remain on the table: publish the list, show the evidence and follow due process for every civil servant named.

World.title: Malawi: Malawi Families Squeezed Again As Cost of Basic Needs Surges
World.content:
Malawian households have been dealt another painful cost of living blow after the amount needed by a typical family of six to cover basic needs climbed to almost K1.15 million a month in September.

A new report by the Employers' Consultative Association of Malawi (Ecam) shows the cost of living rose by 3.18 per cent in September 2026, pushing the monthly budget required for essentials, including transport, from K1.11 million in August to nearly K1.15 million.

The increase comes even as headline inflation eased from 20 per cent in August to 19.4 per cent in September, underlining a harsh reality for struggling families: prices are still rising, just at a slower pace.

For the average household, the latest jump means finding an extra K40,000 every month simply to maintain the same standard of living.



The figures highlight the growing squeeze on workers and families already battling to keep up with soaring costs of food, transport and other essentials.

While falling inflation is often seen as a sign of economic relief, it does not mean goods and services are becoming cheaper. Instead, prices continue to increase, leaving households facing ever-higher bills despite the slowdown in the pace of price rises.

The findings also expose the crucial difference between inflation and the cost of living. Inflation measures how quickly prices are rising, whereas the cost-of-living index reflects the actual amount of money families need to meet everyday expenses.

The latest increase is likely to deepen concerns about household purchasing power, particularly for workers whose wages have failed to keep pace with the rising cost of essential goods and services.

Ecam's September assessment suggests that lower inflation alone is unlikely to bring immediate relief to families, with the overall cost of sustaining a household continuing its relentless upward march.

For many Malawians, the message is stark: although inflation may be cooling, the pressure on family budgets shows little sign of easing.

World.title: Cameroon: Online Fraud Is Becoming a Gateway to Human Trafficking in Cameroon
World.content:
analysis

Criminal networks exploit job seekers' aspirations, turning promises of employment abroad into schemes involving detention, extortion and forced recruitment.

The discovery in September of 15 underage girls in a barricaded compound in Yaoundé's Essos neighbourhood, followed days later by 20 people (including two children) in a basement in Ngousso, has reignited concerns about human trafficking in Cameroon. The two mixed-use neighbourhoods in the capital's northeast are home to working- and middle-class residents.

These are not isolated incidents. Reports from 2025 reveal that criminal networks have been exploiting desperate citizens in Yaoundé and the central Adamawa Region by luring them with false job promises.



In May this year, an operation in Dibombari in the Littoral Region led to the rescue of 17 youths recruited through fake job offers posted on digital platforms. The victims had paid an average of 550 000 CFA francs (US$942) in the hope of travelling to Malaysia, only to be held captive while awaiting departure. Four suspects were arrested.

A few weeks later, the National Gendarmerie announced the dismantling of a vast network in Yaoundé operating under the guise of multi-level marketing on behalf of the businesses QNET, IGNITE and UNIMEC. QNET has denied any involvement, and the positions of the other two companies are not yet clear.

An investigation launched on 16 May resulted in 13 arrests and the identification of around 6 000 victims of fraud and human trafficking nationwide, according to National Gendarmerie data given to the Institute for Security Studies (ISS). The criminal networks involve recruiters, intermediaries, logistics and accommodation providers, coordinators and masterminds - some operating from outside the country.

The large scale of these illicit operations confirms the shift towards digitalisation, with networks no longer relying on in-person contact or local recruiters. Social media, digital platforms and fake job or training offers make it possible to quickly reach individuals seeking employment or opportunities abroad.

Human trafficking facilitated by cybercrime is expanding globally. In Africa, cyber-recruiters have for years been exploiting the continent's growing connectivity. But in Cameroon, large-scale recruitment and fraudulent migration schemes via platforms like WhatsApp and Facebook are relatively new and increasing. In response, the Ministry of Public Service and Administrative Reform has issued official warnings about the threat.

In the recently dismantled Yaoundé network, the primary targets were vulnerable youth, job seekers, students and those seeking to migrate, drawn by the prospect of lucrative employment or skills development abroad.

Once recruited, they paid expensive fees and were then held in compounds - some for months - until authorities discovered the sites. Captors exerted constant psychological pressure on their victims, forcing them to extort money from their loved ones and recruit new targets online in order to secure their release.

Some victims from southern Cameroon were transferred via Garoua in the North Region to Nigeria. Deprived of their travel documents, they were confined and forced to raise money from their families.

The distinction between recruitment scams and the forced detention of victims is crucial. The Palermo Protocol against transnational organised crime defines human trafficking as recruitment or harbouring combined with deception, fraud, abuse of vulnerability or coercion, for the purpose of exploitation. In Cameroon, the initial scam does not involve human trafficking. It is the confiscation of documents, confinement, threats and coercion used to recruit others that mark the shift to trafficking.

The National Gendarmerie data also reveals a transnational dimension. The network's ringleaders are allegedly based in Malaysia, with offshoots in West and Central Africa. Two people sought in connection with the investigation have been located in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Central African Republic.

Cameroon also serves as a destination for foreign victims, including Chadians recruited by networks operating in Yaoundé. In March 2025, police rescued 13 people held in a house in Yaoundé - seven from Madagascar, six from the DRC.

The common factor across all these cases is the exploitation of economic and social vulnerability by criminal networks. In the QNET-IGNITE-UNIMEC case, the existence of multiple accommodation sites across different regions shows how criminal networks employ a web of clandestine houses or dormitories to isolate victims, confiscate their phones and keep them under constant surveillance.

Recent interventions show that security forces are able to identify and dismantle some of the networks. However, the vast distances between recruitment and trafficking sites and the transnational nature of the criminal networks call for enhanced cooperation within Cameroon and between the countries involved. This should include intelligence sharing and the designation of dedicated contact points to centralise alerts, prevent administrative obstacles and enable immediate intervention.

Close 

Cameroonian authorities also need to undertake rigorous monitoring and documentation of collective housing facilities, premises rented to groups, and informal shelters to identify suspicious gatherings before they become detention sites.

The government should redouble efforts to establish formal protocols between digital platforms such as Facebook and WhatsApp and the National Gendarmerie, enabling the rapid removal of fake job offers and the tracing of the accounts that disseminate them.

These measures may seem obvious, but coordinating such efforts is rarely easy. Cameroon's ability to curb the expansion of this hybrid criminal phenomenon will depend on whether authorities have the political and budgetary will to act.

Aicha Pemboura, Researcher, Central Africa Observatory on Organised Crime and Violence, ISS

World.title: Nigeria: National Grid Crashes 81 Percent to 675mw, As 9 Plants Go Off
World.content:
Abuja — Nigeria's grid electricity supply crashed by 81.5 per cent to 675 megawatts (MW) at 1pm on Monday from 3,647MW, following a drop in the number of power plants supplying the national grid from 21 to 2.

The development prompted electricity distribution companies, including Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) and Ikeja Electric, to issue public notices informing customers of supply constraints linked to challenges on the national grid.

Data from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 21 power plants were supplying electricity to the grid before the incident at noon, when total generation stood at 3,647MW.

However, by 1pm, the number of plants on the grid had dropped to 12, while electricity supply plunged to 675MW, representing a loss of 2,972MW within one hour.



The plants that went offline included Azura, Egbin, Jebba and Kainji hydroelectric power plants.

The sharp decline followed relatively higher supply levels earlier in the day, with the grid recording 4,331MW at 1am and 4,458MW at 6am. Supply subsequently fell to 3,647MW by noon before experiencing the steep drop at 1pm.

Electricity supply later recovered to 2,150MW by 5pm, representing an improvement of 1,475MW from the 1pm level, although it remained significantly below the morning peak.

In a public notice issued on Monday, AEDC informed customers that electricity supply from the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) had been interrupted due to a grid-related challenge.

The company said TCN's technical team was working to restore grid stability, adding that power supply was gradually being restored to its feeders.

"We assure you that efforts are ongoing to restore full supply across our franchise area as soon as the situation permits," AEDC said, while apologising for the inconvenience caused by the interruption.

Similarly, Ikeja Electric attributed reduced electricity supply across its network to a shortfall in the volume of power allocated to it from the national grid.

In its notice to customers, the distribution company said it was engaging relevant stakeholders to improve available supply.

It added that it would continue to distribute the electricity received from the grid as efficiently and equitably as possible.

However, NISO said it had stabilised the national grid following multiple trippings on the 330-kilovolt (kV) transmission network.

In a statement on Monday, the system operator said the incident occurred at approximately 12:40pm on October 19, 2026.

It said it immediately implemented corrective measures in collaboration with TCN to stabilise the power system and restore normal operations.

Close 

According to NISO, restoration efforts had been successfully completed and the national grid had returned to normal operation.

The operator clarified that the incident affected only a section of the grid, contrary to unverified reports and claims.
