EGYPT · MARKETS

Key Facts — The country Egypt is the most populous Arab country, with over 100 million people, and a key US partner in Middle East diplomacy.

— What happened On Tuesday 20 October, an EU trade official said Egypt will receive the last tranche of its EU loan by the end of 2026.

— The amount The final payment is 1.5 billion euros (about US$1.7 billion), the third tranche of a 4 billion euro (about US$4.5 billion) EU programme.

— Paid so far The EU has paid 3.5 billion euros (about US$3.9 billion) since December 2024, the latest 1.5 billion euros (about US$1.7 billion) approved on 29 July.

— The conditions Each payment depends on economic reforms, continued progress in the IMF programme and political requirements in the EU-Egypt agreement.

— Still open The exact payment date, and whether Egypt agrees a new IMF arrangement before its current US$8 billion programme ends on 15 December.

The Egypt EU loan is due its final payment of 1.5 billion euros (about US$1.7 billion) by the end of 2026. An EU trade official told the Egyptian daily Al-Shorouk on Tuesday 20 October that the money should arrive before the year closes.

For US investors in Egyptian bonds, the payment adds fresh foreign money as the US$8 billion IMF programme runs out on 15 December. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is the Washington lender whose progress reviews are one condition for the EU money.

What the EU Official Told Al-Shorouk

The head of the trade section at the EU delegation in Egypt, the European Union’s mission in the country, gave the timing to Al-Shorouk. The paper published the remarks in its economic bulletin at 5:54 p.m. on Tuesday 20 October.

He said the last tranche is worth 1.5 billion euros (about US$1.7 billion) and is due by the end of the current year. Al-Shorouk is a private Egyptian daily covering business and politics.

How the Egypt EU Loan Works

The Egypt EU loan is macro-financial assistance, which helps a partner country cover its budget and import bills during reforms. The European Commission, the EU executive, proposed a plan worth 4 billion euros (about US$4.5 billion at 0.89 euros to the dollar) in March 2024.

The European Parliament and the Council of the EU, which speaks for the 27 member governments, approved it in June 2025. It pays out in three tranches, and the one expected by year end is the third.

What Egypt Has Received So Far

The EU paid Egypt a separate 1 billion euros (about US$1.1 billion) short-term loan in December 2024. It then released the first 1 billion euro (about US$1.1 billion) tranche of the larger programme in January 2026.

The second tranche of 1.5 billion euros (about US$1.7 billion) was approved on 29 July 2026, the EU delegation in Cairo said. With it, the Egypt EU loan support reached 3.5 billion euros (about US$3.9 billion).

Conditions Attached to the Egypt EU Loan

Before the July payment, the European Commission found that Egypt had met three tests for the Egypt EU loan. These were the agreed economic reforms, continued progress in its IMF programme, and the political requirements in the EU-Egypt memorandum of understanding.

The reforms cover public finances, the business climate, competition, the governance of state-owned companies, social protection and green measures in water and electricity. The EU said the last tranche will be released once the remaining agreed conditions are met.

The IMF Deadline Behind the EU Money

Egypt’s US$8 billion IMF programme expires on 15 December 2026, and the Fund’s board cleared its latest review on 30 July. The Rio Times set out where that programme stands, including the lack of an announced successor.

The EU lists progress in the IMF programme as a condition, so the Egypt EU loan payment falls close to that deadline. Egypt has not said publicly whether it will ask the Fund for a new arrangement.

Why Europe Keeps Paying Egypt

The EU calls the loan a core pillar of its strategic and comprehensive partnership with Egypt, agreed in 2024. EU Ambassador Angelina Eichhorst has described Egypt as a pillar of stability in the Mediterranean and the wider Middle East and North Africa.

Brussels plans 7.4 billion euros (about US$8.3 billion) in total support for Egypt over 2024 to 2027, covering grants, loans and guarantees. The Rio Times has mapped which outside powers shape Egypt’s economy, from the Gulf to China.

What It Means for US Readers

Investors who hold Egyptian dollar bonds watch the Egypt EU loan because it adds reserves without new borrowing on commercial markets. A steady flow of EU and IMF money lowers the risk that Egypt struggles to pay for imports such as wheat and fuel.

The pound weakened beyond 54.50 to the dollar in local banks on Tuesday, Al-Shorouk reported, so the currency stays under pressure. A calmer pound makes prices and contracts easier to plan for US companies selling into Egypt.

What Is Not Known

The EU official gave no exact date for the Egypt EU loan payment, only the end of 2026. It is also open whether the European Commission has finished its check of the last reform conditions.

Egypt has not said whether it will seek a new IMF arrangement after 15 December, which could affect the final EU assessment. Nor is it clear how Cairo plans to use the money beyond the general support for its budget and imports.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much will the Egypt EU loan pay out next?

The Egypt EU loan has a final tranche of 1.5 billion euros (about US$1.7 billion) due by end 2026, an EU trade official said. It is the third tranche of a 4 billion euros (about US$4.5 billion) programme.

What is macro-financial assistance?

It is an EU loan to a partner country that covers budget and import needs during reforms. The EU pays it in tranches once conditions are met.

How much has the EU already paid Egypt?

The EU has provided 3.5 billion euros (about US$3.9 billion) since December 2024, its delegation in Cairo said. The latest payment, 1.5 billion euros (about US$1.7 billion), was approved on 29 July 2026.

What does Egypt have to do to get the money?

Egypt must carry out agreed economic reforms, keep making progress in its IMF programme and meet political requirements in its agreement with the EU. The Commission checks this before each payment.

Why does the IMF deadline matter for the Egypt EU loan?

Egypt’s US$8 billion IMF programme ends on 15 December 2026, and progress in it is one EU condition. A new IMF arrangement would help show that Egypt stays on its reform path.

World.title: Chile Copper Theft Probe Nets 59 Arrests
World.content:
A freight train carries copper plates to the port of Antofagasta in northern Chile, far from the O'Higgins region where the arrests took place. File photo, 2010. (Photo: Benjamin Goetzinger, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

CHILE · CRIME

Key Facts — The country Chile is the world’s largest copper producer, and its state-owned miner Codelco runs El Teniente, the largest underground copper deposit on the planet.

— Why it matters Chile supplied 68% of US refined copper imports from 2021 to 2024, so a theft case inside its mining supply chain draws attention in the United States.

— Why now Police and prosecutors carried out the raids in the early hours of Tuesday 20 October 2026, with detentions in four localities of the O’Higgins region.

— What happened Detectives arrested 59 people suspected of stealing copper from warehouses serving Codelco and from the cables of power companies.

— The numbers More than 300 officers took part, about 70 properties were searched and two of the detainees were arrested while working inside the El Teniente mine.

— What it means for you No tonnage or value of stolen copper has been published, so the effect on supply and prices cannot be sized, and none of the suspects has been convicted.

— Still open Who did what, how much copper was taken, whether Codelco staff were involved and what the courts decide on custody.

— Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition).

Chile copper theft is the target of a large police operation, after detectives arrested 59 people in the O’Higgins region on Tuesday 20 October 2026. Investigators believe the suspects belonged to a network that took copper from warehouses serving the state miner Codelco and from the cables of electricity companies.

For US readers the case matters because Chile supplied 68% of US refined copper imports from 2021 to 2024, according to the US Geological Survey. The agency estimates that Chile mined 5.3 million metric tons of copper in 2025, close to a quarter of world output of 23 million tons.

No source reviewed puts a tonnage or a value on the copper allegedly stolen, so this article claims no effect on supply or prices. What is established is the scale of the operation, which police and prosecutors ran from a command post attended by regional prosecutor Aquiles Cubillos.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

How the Chile Copper Theft Raids Unfolded

The operation, named Veta Roja (Red Vein), began in the early hours of Tuesday 20 October, when the Policía de Investigaciones (PDI), Chile’s civilian detective force, moved on addresses across the region. More than 300 PDI officers took part, and the regional prosecutor’s office confirmed 59 detainees in Rancagua, Machalí, Coya and Mostazal.

Early reports spoke of more than 40 and then more than 50 detainees before the count settled at 59. BioBioChile and other outlets said the number could still rise as the searches continued.

El Desconcierto and ADN Radio put the number of searched properties at about 70. Rancagua is the regional capital, and Machalí, Coya and Mostazal are nearby localities.

The searches covered the homes of suspects and some premises linked to Codelco. Two detainees were arrested while working inside the El Teniente mine, and officers seized copper, firearms, ammunition, cash and vehicles, according to the Public Prosecutor’s Office as relayed by La Tercera.

The coverage reviewed gives no quantities for the copper, the weapons or the cash. Prosecutors also have not said over what period the thefts allegedly took place.

The inquiry is led by the Criminal Analysis Prosecutor’s Office of O’Higgins, which worked with two PDI units, the Robbery Brigade and the Money Laundering Brigade. The second unit points to a financial trail, but no money-laundering charge has been announced in the coverage reviewed.

Who Is Accused and What They Allegedly Did

CNN Chile reported that the network was allegedly led by a former officer of Carabineros, Chile’s uniformed national police. El Desconcierto, citing the newspaper Emol, adds that his exit from the force was reportedly unrelated to this investigation.

El Desconcierto, citing Emol, also reports that a woman allegedly handled the finances and the sale of the stolen metal. The same account says one Codelco employee and two contractors allegedly helped take copper from El Teniente.

G5 Noticias, citing the radio station Cooperativa, counted four workers linked to Codelco among the detainees. The counts differ between outlets, and prosecutors have not confirmed either one.

The same El Desconcierto account lists alleged roles, among them mountain crews, mule transporters, cable cutters, scrap-metal receivers and front men who held the profits. These are investigators’ working notes and not court findings, and every suspect is presumed innocent.

Prosecutors have not said what role each of the 59 played, and none has been convicted. El Desconcierto adds that prosecutors were expected to seek more time in custody before a formal charging hearing planned for Thursday 22 October.

Why Codelco and El Teniente Matter

Codelco is Chile’s state-owned copper company, and El Teniente is its mine in the Machalí commune of the O’Higgins region. Codelco describes El Teniente as the largest underground copper deposit on the planet, worked since 1905 and threaded by more than 4,500 kilometers (about 2,800 miles) of tunnels.

The raids reached the mine as one site among many, and nothing published so far says its output was disrupted. Codelco had no statement on the arrests on its news page when we checked on Tuesday.

Investigators say part of the metal disappeared from warehouses of firms that provide services to Codelco. The same sources say the network also cut cable belonging to electricity companies, so the case touches utilities as well as mining.

Our earlier report, Armed Gangs Strip Metal From Chile’s Copper Train Wagons, described a different pattern of metal theft in the north. Our explainer Chile Security and Crime Explained 2026 gives the wider security context.

Why Chile Copper Matters to the United States

The US Geological Survey estimates that the United States imported 1.7 million tons of refined copper in 2025, up from 903,000 tons in 2024. It puts net import reliance at 57% of apparent consumption in 2025, against 45% a year earlier.

Those figures show why US builders, manufacturers and grid companies depend on metal from Chile, which supplied 68% of refined imports in the 2021 to 2024 period. They do not show that the arrests change any shipment, and nothing published so far points to a supply shock.

Theft from contractor warehouses and power cables is first a security and cost problem for the miner and for utilities. Whether it reaches prices depends on volumes that prosecutors have not disclosed.

What It Means for You

Investors in copper users and mining shares should treat this as a security and governance story until a tonnage or a value is published. Our guides Chile Natural Resources Explained 2026 and Copper in Latin America 2026: Mines, Prices and Politics give the production background.

Residents and visitors in central Chile face a case about industrial theft, not street crime, and the coverage reviewed carried no travel guidance. Our Santiago expat city guide and Who Dominates Chile, Elites and Regions Explained cover daily life and who holds power.

What Is Not Known

Prosecutors have not published the tonnage or value of the copper stolen, nor the period over which the thefts allegedly ran. They have not said which charges they will bring beyond describing a network dedicated to stealing and receiving copper on a large scale.

Counts of Codelco employees and contractors among the detainees differ between outlets, and Codelco had not commented when we checked. The 22 October charging date comes from one outlet and is unconfirmed.

The sources do not say what the suspects or their lawyers say, and no one has been convicted. More arrests are possible, because the operation was still under way when the first reports appeared.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people were arrested in the Chile copper theft operation?

Prosecutors confirmed 59 detainees in Rancagua, Machalí, Coya and Mostazal on Tuesday 20 October 2026. Early counts were lower, and more arrests remain possible.

What is Operation Veta Roja?

Veta Roja, or Red Vein, is the name given to the police and prosecutors’ operation against a suspected copper theft network in the O’Higgins region. It was led by the regional Criminal Analysis Prosecutor’s Office with the PDI detective force.

Did the arrests disrupt Codelco’s output?

No source reviewed says so. Searches took place at some Codelco premises and two detainees were arrested inside El Teniente, but no production impact has been reported.

Why does Chile copper theft matter to US readers?

Chile supplied 68% of US refined copper imports from 2021 to 2024, according to the US Geological Survey. The case shows risks in a supply chain that US industry relies on, though no volume of stolen copper has been given.

Are the 59 suspects guilty?

No, they are detainees and a court has not convicted anyone. Prosecutors must still present evidence at hearings, and all suspects are presumed innocent.

Sources: BioBioChile, 20 October 2026; La Tercera, 20 October 2026; CNN Chile, 20 October 2026; El Desconcierto, 20 October 2026; ADN Radio, 20 October 2026; La Nación, 20 October 2026; Codelco, El Teniente division page; US Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2026, copper.

World.title: Turkish Airlines Lifts Lagos Flights to 10 a Week
World.content:
NIGERIA · TRAVEL

Key Facts — What is happening Turkish Airlines will raise Istanbul to Lagos flights from seven to 10 a week each way from Friday, 11 December 2026.

— Why it matters Lagos gets more seats and connections through Istanbul just before the holiday peak, when many Americans and Nigerians fly in for family and festivals.

— The numbers Three extra weekly flights lift capacity on the route by about 43 percent. The airline links Istanbul to more than 350 destinations and operates more than 560 aircraft.

— Who is who Turkish Airlines is Turkey’s flag carrier and Star Alliance member. The Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria runs Lagos’s Murtala Muhammed airport, where terminal rebuilding is under way.

— What to watch Whether the airline publishes fares and a full schedule, and whether the Lagos terminal bridge opens for the December peak as promised.

— What it means for you Americans need a Nigerian e-visa before flying and the State Department rates Nigeria Level 3, Reconsider travel. Lagos airport asks for arrival three to four hours early.

Turkish Airlines will fly Istanbul to Lagos 10 times a week from Friday, 11 December 2026, up from seven. The three added flights start a week before Detty December opens in Lagos.

Turkish Airlines will raise Istanbul to Lagos flights from seven to 10 a week in each direction from Friday, 11 December 2026. The change adds three weekly flights between Nigeria’s commercial capital and the airline’s Istanbul hub.

For American travellers, Istanbul is a common connection point for Lagos, so more flights mean more choice on dates and times. Lagos is the biggest city in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, and its airport is the main gateway.

What Turkish Airlines Announced

The airline’s management issued a statement in Lagos on Saturday, 10 October 2026. P.M. News, the News Agency of Nigeria, New Telegraph and Daily Trust all carried it.

P.M. News wrote that the airline will operate 10 flights in each direction. New Telegraph quoted the statement as saying the move meets growing demand for travel between Lagos and Türkiye.

Daily Trust, an Abuja newspaper, and the trade site Aviation Metric say the three added flights run on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. Aviation Metric lists them as TK 615 and TK 616.

The airline also pointed to Abuja, where it raised Istanbul flights to seven a week from June 2026. In February, general manager Lokman Balkan told reporters in Lagos the airline wanted more frequencies, first to Lagos and then to Abuja.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Extra Flights Fit Together

Seven weekly flights run today, so the three extra ones raise capacity by about 43 percent. That is simple arithmetic on flights, and the airline has not published seat numbers.

Turkish Airlines says a direct flight from Istanbul to Lagos takes an average of seven hours and 10 minutes. Americans first need a flight to Istanbul, so total journey time depends on the departure city and the layover.

Business class passengers connecting through Istanbul can use the airline’s business lounge at Istanbul Airport. The airline sells tickets on its website, in its app, at sales offices and through travel agents.

Entry Rules for US Citizens

The US State Department says a visa is required for Nigeria and that travellers should apply before they go. The Nigeria Immigration Service runs an online e-visa portal for short stays.

Its tourist e-visa is single entry and lasts 30 days, and the service says short-visit e-visas cannot be extended. Applicants need a valid passport, a return ticket, proof of accommodation and a bank statement.

Interior Minister Tunji-Ojo said in February 2025 that visa on arrival was upgraded, not scrapped. Approvals are expected within 24 to 48 hours and are emailed, so do not count on a visa at the airport.

The State Department says your passport must be valid for six months beyond arrival and have one blank page per stamp. It also says yellow fever and polio certificates are required for travellers over nine months old.

The immigration service says landing and exit cards became mandatory for all arriving and departing passengers from 1 May 2025. Complete them as the airline or the portal instructs before you land.

No official page that could be opened states the current US$ fee for Americans, and third-party guides disagree. Check the fee on the official e-visa portal before you pay anyone.

Passing Through Istanbul

Turkey’s foreign ministry says ordinary US passport holders need no visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. That covers a stay in Türkiye, not Nigeria.

The ministry page gives no separate transit wording for Americans. Ask the airline whether your layover keeps you airside, and leave a buffer between flights.

Safety and Health Notes

The State Department rates Nigeria Level 3, Reconsider travel, in an advisory issued on 12 June and updated on 25 June. It cites crime, terrorism, unrest, kidnapping and inconsistent health care.

Lagos and Abuja are not on its Do Not Travel list, which names states in the north and the south-east. The advisory says the US government can offer only limited emergency help outside Abuja and Lagos.

Dial 112 for police or an ambulance, though the advisory calls ambulance service unreliable. It adds that the State Department does not pay medical bills and most hospitals do not accept US insurance.

Amounts above US$10,000 must be declared on entry and exit. Drones and satellite phones are illegal or need prior government approval.

Lagos Airport in December

Olubunmi Kuku, managing director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, urged travellers to arrive three to four hours before departure. She spoke after an inspection on 7 October, according to the Federal Ministry of Information.

She said she is confident a bridge linking Terminals 1 and 2 will be open to the public by the December peak. Concrete work is complete and the canopy, framing and rails are largely in place.

The authority will deploy extra staff across the airport over the holiday period. Kuku also said the Seymour car park now connects directly to Terminal 2.

She blamed recurring drop-off jams mainly on drivers who stop at Level 1 when upper levels also connect to the terminal. She also advised travellers to confirm flight updates with their airline.

Kuku admitted that running a busy airport during a major rebuild is hard. A planned Red Line rail extension to the airport is still at the design and procurement stage.

Timing With Detty December

Detty December Fest runs in Lagos from 18 to 30 December 2026, with Wizkid at the grand opening on Friday, 18 December. The first new Turkish Airlines flights start exactly one week earlier.

Book flights, lodging and airport transfers early if you plan to travel in the last two weeks of December. The Detty December guide linked below covers the festival and the wider season.

What It Means for You

If you plan a Lagos trip around Christmas, the added capacity gives you more ways to connect through Istanbul. Fares were not part of the announcement, so compare prices across airlines before you book.

Sort the paperwork first, because your Nigerian e-visa should be approved before you board. Allow extra time at both airports and build a buffer into the layover in Istanbul.

What Is Not Known

No airline press release turned up, and its Lagos flights page, opened on 20 October, shows no 11 December schedule. The details therefore rest on the Nigerian outlets named above.

Daily Trust and Aviation Metric list departure and arrival times that disagree on direction, so they are left out. The aircraft type, the fares and the current official US$ e-visa fee for Americans are also unconfirmed.

The ministry’s report gives a weekday for the airport inspection that does not match 7 October 2026, so none is given. BusinessDay reported in April that the US authorised non-emergency staff to leave its Abuja embassy, and current status is unconfirmed.

What Comes Next

The three additional weekly flights begin on Friday, 11 December 2026, and the Lagos terminal bridge is due for the December peak. This does not mean fares will fall, and it does not change the Level 3 advisory.

For more on the city, see the Lagos city guide and what to do in Lagos in October 2026. The Detty December 2026 guide and the Lagos airport report add festival and airport detail.

Frequently Asked Questions

When do the extra Turkish Airlines flights to Lagos start?

The service rises from seven to 10 weekly flights in each direction from Friday, 11 December 2026. Daily Trust and Aviation Metric say the three added flights run on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays.

Do US citizens need a visa for Nigeria?

Yes, Americans need a Nigerian visa and should get the e-visa before they fly, because visa on arrival now needs pre-approval. Check the current fee and rules on the official Nigeria Immigration Service portal.

Is Lagos safe for American travellers?

The State Department rates Nigeria Level 3, Reconsider travel, and neither Lagos nor Abuja is on its Do Not Travel list. Read the full advisory and enrol in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program before you go.

BURKINA FASO · POLICY

Key Facts — The country Burkina Faso is a landlocked West African country run by a military-led government under Captain Ibrahim Traoré, who took power in a 2022 coup.

— What happened On Monday 19 October 2026, the legislature passed a law that bans the full or partial privatization of strategic state companies.

— The vote 70 lawmakers voted for the law and one abstained in the Assemblée législative du peuple, the transitional parliament in Ouagadougou.

— The test A company counts as strategic if it touches national sovereignty, state security or the social and economic balance of the country.

— New state powers The state may buy shares in private firms judged strategic, and may reserve some activities for Burkinabè nationals.

— Protection Assets and bank accounts of strategic public firms cannot be seized by creditors under the new text.

— Still open Which companies make the strategic list, and how the law treats foreign owners already in place.

Burkina Faso bans privatization of its strategic state companies under a law passed on Monday 19 October 2026. The vote was 70 in favour with one abstention, Lefaso.net reported from the session in Ouagadougou, the capital.

For US and other foreign investors, the message is that the door to key state assets is closed. The law also lets the state take stakes in private firms, which raises the stakes for any business with a Burkinabè partner.

What Lawmakers Approved in Ouagadougou

Burkina Faso’s legislature, the Assemblée législative du peuple, is the transitional parliament that sits in Ouagadougou under the military-led government. It passed a bill that defines strategic entities, and Burkina Faso bans privatization of any such state-owned company, in full or in part.

Industry minister Serge Poda defended the bill before the lawmakers, Lefaso.net said. The vote came on Monday 19 October, with 70 votes in favour and one abstention.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How a Company Becomes Strategic

The law sets several tests that decide whether a company, an entity or a whole sector is strategic. One is national sovereignty and the security of the state against threats from inside and outside the country.

A second test is the weight of the entity for the social and economic balance of Burkina Faso. Poda told lawmakers that the state now has full powers to supervise, control and follow these entities.

New Powers for the State

The state can now supervise and control strategic public entities, and take shares in private firms judged strategic, Poda said. Some decisions at state-run strategic firms will need prior approval from the Council of Ministers, the cabinet.

The law also lets the state reserve certain strategic activities, to be named by regulation, for Burkinabè nationals. A further clause shields the assets and bank accounts of strategic public or majority-public firms from seizure.

Why the Government Is Rewriting the Rules

Poda said the law replaces a 1993 text that shielded strategic companies from a wave of privatizations in the 1990s, he recalled. In his words, that text showed gaps, and the push for national sovereignty made a rewrite necessary.

The vote follows the state takeover of the sugar maker SN-SOSUCO and the oil maker SN-CITEC, which the state daily Sidwaya covered in November 2025. SN-CITEC had been privatized in 1995, and Sidwaya called its return to the state a sign of economic sovereignty.

What It Means for US Readers

American companies and funds that hoped to buy state assets now face a legal bar if the asset is on the strategic list. Burkina Faso bans privatization for those firms, and private owners in strategic sectors could see the state ask for a share.

The law fits the policy of the military-led government, which the Rio Times described in its Burkina Faso explainer. It also sits beside the sovereignty push of the Sahel states covered in the joint Sahel speech at the UN.

What Is Not Known

The list of strategic companies has not yet been named, so it is open which firms in mining, farming or utilities fall under the ban. It is also open when the president will sign the law.

The text as reported does not say how it treats foreign owners who already hold shares in a firm later judged strategic. Nor is it clear what compensation, if any, the state would offer if it raised its stake in a private company.

More: Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Burkina Faso’s legislature decide on 19 October?

Burkina Faso bans privatization of strategic state companies, in full or in part, under the law it passed. The vote was 70 in favour with one abstention.

Who decides which companies are strategic?

The law sets criteria such as national sovereignty, state security and the social and economic balance of the country. The final list of companies is still to come.

Can the state buy shares in private companies?

Yes, industry minister Serge Poda said the state may take shares or raise its stake in private firms judged strategic. Some activities may also be reserved for Burkinabè nationals.

What does the ban mean for foreign investors?

Burkina Faso bans privatization of strategic firms, so foreign buyers cannot purchase them, fully or in part. Investors in private firms in strategic sectors face the risk of a state stake.

What was the earlier law on strategic companies?

A 1993 law protected strategic companies from the privatization wave of the 1990s. Poda said it had gaps and needed a rewrite.

World.title: Smart Sampa Leak Exposes 58,000 Cameras
World.content:
A Guarda Civil Metropolitana patrol car beside the Smart Sampa transparency display in central São Paulo, 25 February 2025 (Photo: Paulo Pinto/Agência Brasil, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · SURVEILLANCE

Key Facts — The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest economy, runs Smart Sampa, the camera and facial-recognition network of São Paulo, its largest city, under Mayor Ricardo Nunes.

— Why it matters The network streams live images from streets, schools, daycare centres and hospitals to a control centre, so a leak of its access data is a privacy and security risk.

— Why now A news investigation published on Tuesday 20 October 2026 said the access data sat on the open internet, and prosecutors opened an inquiry the same day.

— What happened Logins and agent records stayed online for about 11 months and opened access to images from more than 58,000 cameras; the city confirms a leak but denies a system flaw.

— The numbers The leak included 181 logins and passwords and data on more than 6,000 agents, and the city pays a consortium under a R$588 million (about US$117 million) contract.

— What it means for you Residents, visitors and businesses with cameras on the network should watch how prosecutors and the city answer who could see their images.

— Still open How the data reached the internet, whether anyone misused it, and who is responsible: one agent, the contractor or the system design.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 77% · Lula 22.5% (US$189 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 79% · Lula 21% As of 20 October, 2:00 pm ET (19:00 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

The Smart Sampa leak gave outsiders a way into live images from more than 58,000 cameras in São Paulo, Brazil’s largest city, according to a UOL investigation published on Tuesday 20 October 2026. The city hall confirmed a leak the same day but denies any flaw in the system and blames one security agent.

For US readers the case is a warning about city-wide facial recognition, a technology that many American cities also debate, and about a Brazilian security model now in a presidential race. São Paulo is also a base for many US companies and a frequent stop for American travellers.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.1%, Lula 48.9% 26 national polls from 14 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

The row lands five days before the runoff on Sunday 25 October 2026, because conservative candidate Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party (PL) has promised a national system inspired by the programme. State prosecutors announced an inquiry on the day the story broke, and our earlier report on the city guard is here: São Paulo Moves to Turn Its City Guard Into a Police Force.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What UOL Found in the Smart Sampa Leak

UOL said sensitive data from the system stayed on the open internet for about 11 months. The material included 181 logins and passwords of authorised users, data on more than 6,000 security agents and instructions for running the system on computers and phones.

With that material, UOL’s reporters built an interface to browse camera images on a map of the city. In a test on 7 October they saw their own images from eight private cameras in the Campos Elíseos district of central São Paulo.

They also reached images from public sites, among them health units and daycare centres. UOL said some credentials gave direct access to the technology platform without a second login step, and that tools allowed searches by name, CPF tax number, vehicle plate and incident record.

Rafael Alcadipani, a public-security professor at the Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV), a Brazilian university, told G1 that a kidnapper could learn about a target and a criminal could learn where police cars are. A specialist quoted by UOL added that some interfaces could let outsiders insert false facial-recognition or number-plate records.

How the City Answered

São Paulo city hall confirmed in a written note that data had leaked, but called it an illegal act by one of more than 7,500 security agents and not a security failure. The agent was identified, suspended and is under investigation by the internal affairs office of the Guarda Civil Metropolitana (GCM), the city’s municipal guard.

The city said the data repository was taken offline and held no mention of access passwords, which differs from UOL’s account of 181 credentials. It added unique passwords, two-factor login and SMS codes for creating new passwords.

The note accused UOL of acting irresponsibly and misinforming the public by calling the case a security failure, and said the platform was never improperly used. It added that the programme is overseen by the municipal audit court and sends a transparency report to prosecutors every six months.

The city also said its cameras in public buildings cover only common areas, not consulting rooms or care areas. It noted that a captured image does not mean a person was registered or identified by the system.

Prosecutors Open an Inquiry

The São Paulo state prosecution service announced on 20 October that it will investigate the leak, G1 reported. The case went to its public-property prosecution offices, and the prosecutor in charge had not yet been named.

The Ministério Público is the independent state body that can investigate public authorities. An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing by the city or any person.

The Contractor, the Contract and the Cost

Sentinelx is the company responsible for Smart Sampa’s technology platform, and it joined the Smart City SP consortium that holds a R$588 million (about US$117 million) contract with the city, Veja reported. The company replaced Camerite in the consortium through an amendment signed in January 2026.

Veja said the contract makes the contractor responsible for system security and requires it to report abnormal events within 24 hours, with fines for breaches. We did not find a statement from Sentinelx in the reports reviewed.

Olhar Digital reported that the city has no access to the source code or the artificial-intelligence models behind facial recognition, and runs no independent audits of the algorithms. G1 put the programme’s running cost at about R$10 million a month (about US$2 million).

Smart Sampa Before the Leak

São Paulo launched Smart Sampa in 2024, and its control centre, opened in July of that year, runs around the clock on images from public and private cameras. Artificial intelligence compares faces with official databases of wanted and missing people and flags stolen or cloned vehicles.

The city says the programme has helped capture 3,628 fugitives and locate 284 missing people. A study by the Centre for Security and Citizenship Studies (CESeC), called “Smart Sampa vigia, mas não protege”, found no statistically significant fall in thefts, robberies or homicides between March 2024 and April 2025, which the city disputes.

Olhar Digital reported that 268 people were taken to police stations after facial-recognition alerts between November 2024 and May 2026 and then released. In 75 of those cases the identification was inconsistent, in 181 the warrants were outdated and in 12 there were registration problems.

Why the Smart Sampa Leak Reaches the Runoff

Flávio Bolsonaro’s government plan promises a national facial-recognition system inspired by Smart Sampa and by the state government’s “Muralha Paulista”, with more than 1 million new cameras, Terra reported from the plan text. He faces President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva of the Workers’ Party (PT) in the runoff on 25 October.

We did not find a response from the Bolsonaro campaign to the leak in the reports reviewed. The programme itself is run by Mayor Ricardo Nunes of the Brazilian Democratic Movement (MDB), not by the federal government.

What It Means for You

Residents and visitors in São Paulo should know that the network combines public cameras with private ones, such as condominium and shop cameras. Terra reported that some agreements keep recordings for up to 14 days.

Businesses that connect cameras to the network can ask the city who can see their images and how access is logged. Our guides to Brazil Security and Crime Explained 2026 and Who Dominates Brazil, Elites and Regions Explained give the wider background.

Travellers planning a trip can use our São Paulo expat city guide and What to Do in São Paulo in October 2026. Nothing in the reports reviewed suggests visitors face any new danger from the leak.

What Is Not Known

UOL’s original article could not be opened for this report, so its findings rest on the city’s own note and on G1, Jovem Pan, Olhar Digital, Terra and the Record network’s news site, which summarise it. Where a detail comes from UOL alone, the text says so.

It is not known where the repository was hosted, who put it online, or whether anyone besides UOL used the credentials. The reports also do not say when the access data stopped working, or whether the agent acted on purpose.

It is also unknown whether prosecutors will examine the contractor as well as the agent, and whether the national data-protection authority will act. All amounts here use the Central Bank of Brazil’s PTAX selling rate of R$5.014 per US dollar on 20 October 2026.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Smart Sampa leak?

UOL reported that access data for the Smart Sampa camera network stayed on the open internet for about 11 months. It allowed access to images from more than 58,000 cameras, according to the report.

Did the city of São Paulo admit the leak?

Yes, the city confirmed that data leaked but denies a security failure. It blames one security agent, who was suspended and is under internal investigation.

Who is investigating the Smart Sampa leak?

The GCM internal affairs office is investigating the agent, and the state prosecution service announced its own inquiry on 20 October. No prosecutor had been named when the news broke.

What is Smart Sampa?

Smart Sampa is São Paulo’s camera and facial-recognition network, launched in 2024 under Mayor Ricardo Nunes. The city says it has helped capture 3,628 fugitives and locate 284 missing people.

Why does the leak matter for the Brazil runoff?

Flávio Bolsonaro’s plan promises a national system inspired by Smart Sampa, so the leak feeds a debate about that proposal. The runoff takes place on Sunday 25 October 2026.

World.title: Uruguay Inflation Seen at 5.4% by Year End
World.content:
URUGUAY · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening Uruguay’s economics institute Cinve now expects consumer prices to rise 5.4% in the year to December 2026, up from 4.8% in its September forecast, in a report dated Thursday, 15 October.

— Why it matters The forecast keeps inflation above the central bank’s 4.5% target until May 2027, two months longer than Cinve saw a month ago, after the bank raised its policy rate to 6% on 8 October.

— The numbers September inflation was 4.68% in the year, with prices up 0.54% in the month. Cinve projects about 4.9% for October, 5.4% for December 2026 and 3.9% for December 2027.

— Who is who Cinve is a private Montevideo economics institute founded in 1975. The Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU), led by president Guillermo Tolosa, sets the 4.5% target and the policy rate.

— What to watch The October consumer price figure, which Cinve projects at 0.57% for the month, and the central bank’s next rate decision, whose date is not yet confirmed.

— Power Index Uruguay ranks 7th of 14 in Uruguay ranks 7th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 45.9 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you For US residents, retirees and investors who earn, save or spend in Uruguayan pesos, Cinve’s path means prices up about 5.4% by December, faster than the central bank’s 4.5% target.

Uruguay inflation will end 2026 at 5.4%, the institute Cinve forecasts, up from 4.8% a month ago. The report says prices stay above the central bank’s 4.5% target until May 2027.

Uruguay inflation is set to end 2026 at 5.4%, according to Cinve, a Montevideo economics institute, in a report dated 15 October. The regional business outlet Ámbito Uruguay reported the forecast on Friday, 16 October.

That is 0.9 percentage points above the 4.5% target of the Banco Central del Uruguay (BCU), the country’s central bank. It matters to US residents and investors who earn, save or spend pesos in Uruguay.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Uruguay ranks 7th of 14 with 45.9 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (88); weakest: future resources (23). Alignment group: Hedging. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What Cinve Forecasts for Uruguay Inflation

Cinve, a private research institute founded in 1975, puts annual inflation at 5.4% in December 2026, against 4.8% in its September report. For December 2027 it now sees 3.9%, up from 3.6% a month ago.

Inflation stays above the 4.5% target until May 2027, Cinve says, and falls below it from June 2027. A month ago the institute expected prices to be above the target only until March 2027.

Cinve projects monthly price rises of 0.57% in October, 0.35% in November and 0.20% in December. Annual inflation would climb from 4.68% in September to about 4.9% in October and 5.4% in December.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Prices Are Rising Faster

September inflation was 0.54% in the month and 4.68% in the year, Cinve’s report says. That beat Cinve’s own forecast of 0.33% and put prices above the 4.5% target for a second month running.

Before August, inflation had been below the target for 12 months, the report notes. Cinve blames the length of the Middle East conflict, which has pushed up oil prices and complicates every forecast.

Its base case treats the conflict as temporary, with oil staying above pre-conflict levels through 2027. It also assumes the exchange rate follows a random walk, so that only unpredictable shocks move it.

The pressure sits in volatile and administered prices, a group that includes fuel, unprocessed food, electricity, water and telecoms. Cinve’s table puts that group at 6.2% in September and 8.2% in December 2026.

Underlying inflation, which strips out those prices, was 4.1% in September and is projected at 4.3% in December. The gap between the two shows where Cinve expects the pressure to come from.

The Central Bank Context

The BCU raised its policy rate by 0.25 points to 6% from 5.75% on Thursday, 8 October, Infobae and Ámbito Uruguay reported. It targets 4.5% with a tolerance band of 3% to 6%, so a 5.4% reading would stay inside the band.

The bank says 24-month inflation expectations remain anchored near the target, Infobae reported on 12 October. It expects inflation to stay temporarily above target until early 2027, within the tolerance range, Ámbito Uruguay reported on 17 October.

The bank’s survey of 25 analysts, reported on 14 October, had a median of 4.87% for end-2026. Forecasts ranged from 4.40% to 5.40%, so Cinve’s 5.4% sits at the top.

What It Means for US Readers

US residents and business owners who pay bills in Uruguayan pesos face prices that Cinve expects to rise about 5.4% by December. That is faster than the 4.5% the central bank aims for.

Investors in peso assets should watch whether the central bank raises its 6% rate again. Cinve’s forecast is one institute’s view, not a decision by the bank.

Background is in earlier reports on the rate rise to 6%, September inflation and the central bank’s forecasts. The guide to Uruguay’s economy and the Montevideo city page help with budgeting.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the BCU will raise its rate again, and the sources give no date for its next decision. Cinve’s path also depends on oil prices and on the exchange rate, neither of which it can predict.

This is one institute’s forecast, and only one outlet, Ámbito Uruguay, was found covering it. Its text gives a 0.1 point revision and a 4.68% October rate, which differ from Cinve’s report, whose figures are used here.

The 6% rate and the 3% to 6% band rest on Infobae and Ámbito Uruguay; the bank’s statement could not be opened. Neither the bank’s year-end forecast nor the statistics office INE’s September figure was confirmed at the primary source.

What Comes Next

The October consumer price figure will test Cinve’s 0.57% monthly projection. Cinve had issued no newer forecast by 20 October, and its next monthly report will show whether it revises again.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Uruguay’s inflation forecast for 2026?

Cinve expects annual inflation of 5.4% in December 2026, up from 4.8% in its September report. That is 0.9 points above the central bank’s 4.5% target.

When does Cinve see inflation returning to target?

Cinve says inflation stays above the 4.5% target until May 2027 and falls below it from June 2027. It sees 3.9% at the end of 2027.

What was Uruguay’s inflation in September?

Prices rose 0.54% in the month and 4.68% in the year, according to Cinve’s report. That is above the 4.5% target for a second month in a row.

What is the central bank’s policy rate?

The BCU raised its policy rate by 0.25 points to 6% from 5.75% on Thursday, 8 October. Guillermo Tolosa is the bank’s president.

What is Cinve?

Cinve is a private economics research institute in Montevideo that began work in 1975. Its coyuntura team publishes a monthly inflation report with forecasts.

Sources: Cinve, Informe de Inflación No. 292, 15 October; Cinve, Informe de Inflación No. 291, September; Ámbito Uruguay, 16 October; Ámbito Uruguay, analyst survey, 14 October; Ámbito Uruguay, central bank outlook, 17 October; Infobae, rate decision, 12 October (all accessed 20 October 2026).

World.title: El Salvador Exports Seen Up 7% This Year
World.content:
EL SALVADOR · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening El Salvador’s goods exports are forecast to grow 7% in 2026, to about US$5.94 billion, far below the 20% growth forecast for Latin America and the Caribbean as a whole, in a trade outlook released on Thursday, 15 October.

— Why it matters Latin American exports to the United States are projected to rise 24% this year, so El Salvador’s 7% leaves it among the slower exporters in a region-wide trade boom.

— The numbers Exports are put at US$5.94 billion against US$5.55 billion in 2025, a gain of US$392 million, while imports reach US$18.13 billion, up nearly 9%, leaving a goods trade gap near US$12.2 billion.

— Who is who The forecast comes from the United Nations commission that studies Latin American economies, led by Executive Secretary José Manuel Salazar-Xirinachs, which publishes its International Trade Outlook once a year.

— What to watch The open question is whether the 7% holds, because Salvadoran goods exports grew only 3.2% to US$4.53 billion in January to August, less than half the forecast pace.

— What it means for you US exporters sell into a Salvadoran market that imports about US$18.1 billion of goods this year, growing faster than the country’s own exports, while US demand for Latin American goods is strong overall.

El Salvador’s goods exports are forecast to grow 7% in 2026 to US$5.94 billion, a UN regional report shows. That is far below the 20% forecast for Latin America and the Caribbean.

El Salvador exports are forecast to grow 7% in 2026, to US$5.94 billion from US$5.55 billion in 2025. The projection comes from the International Trade Outlook for Latin America and the Caribbean 2026, launched on Thursday, 15 October.

The report is the annual study of the UN Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (ECLAC, or Cepal in Spanish). Diario El Mundo, a Salvadoran daily, reported the country figures on Friday, 16 October.

For US readers, the report’s most relevant number is a 24% projected rise in Latin American exports to the United States. El Salvador’s overall 7% growth sits well below the regional 20% pace.

What the Cepal Report Says About El Salvador Exports

The report puts El Salvador at 7%, level with Costa Rica and well under the regional 20%. The regional rise is the largest since the 2021 post-pandemic rebound.

Across the region, export prices are forecast up 11% and export volumes up 9%. Twenty-eight of the 33 countries should see higher export values, with double-digit growth in 16.

Other Central American neighbours differ widely in the same chart. Guatemala and Honduras are at 13%, Nicaragua at 5% and Panama at minus 14%.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Salvadoran Figures Reported by Diario El Mundo

Diario El Mundo reports that El Salvador’s goods exports would reach US$5.942 billion in 2026, against US$5.550 billion in 2025. That is a gain of US$392 million.

The daily says this is 6.6% of Central America’s estimated US$88.935 billion in exports and ranks El Salvador 20th in the region. The commission’s own pages could not be opened to check these country figures, so they rest on El Mundo alone.

El Salvador Imports Are Growing Faster Than Exports

El Mundo reports goods imports of more than US$18.134 billion in 2026, up US$1.476 billion from US$16.658 billion in 2025. The daily puts that rise at 8.8%, faster than the 7% forecast for exports.

On those figures, the goods trade gap would be about US$12.2 billion, a simple subtraction. Regionally, the report forecasts imports up 16% in value, on stronger consumption and demand for inputs and capital goods.

Central Bank Data Show a Slower Start

Central bank (BCR) data show goods exports of US$4.53 billion in January to August, up 3.2%. Estrategia & Negocios reported on 25 September that growth had slowed from 4.4% through July.

The United States, the main market, took US$1.48 billion, up 2.4%, about a third of the total. Textiles and apparel, sugar, coffee and electrical goods lead the export basket, with coffee growing at double-digit rates.

What the UN Commission Says About the Outlook

Executive Secretary José Manuel Salazar-Xirinachs said the region faces significant challenges in an uncertain geopolitical landscape. He added that competition for critical minerals and new environmental demands are reshaping value chains and market access.

For context, see earlier coverage of El Salvador exports and remittances and the EMFI growth forecast. The same report lifts Mexico’s exports 26%.

What It Means for US Readers

US exporters sell into a Salvadoran market that, on El Mundo’s figures, imports about US$18.1 billion of goods in 2026. Import growth of nearly 9% outpaces export growth of 7%.

Across the region, the 24% forecast rise in exports to the United States points to strong US demand for Latin American goods. El Salvador’s 7% is slower than most of the region, and its own US shipments rose just 2.4% through August.

What Is Not Known

The US$ country figures come from Diario El Mundo only, and the commission’s own pages could not be opened to confirm them. The 7% for El Salvador is repeated in El Mundo and in regional reports on the outlook.

The commission’s forecast for Salvadoran shipments to the United States is not known, nor is any GDP or remittance forecast. The BCR figures run only to August, so the full-year result is not yet known.

El Mundo also quotes the report as putting Salvadoran import growth at 17%, which conflicts with its own 8.8%. That figure and its first-half trade numbers are left out here, and the forecasts may be revised.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is El Salvador’s export forecast for 2026?

Goods exports are forecast to grow 7% in 2026, to US$5.94 billion. The projection is in a UN regional trade outlook launched on Thursday, 15 October.

How does that compare with Latin America?

The region’s goods exports are forecast to grow 20%, the largest rise since 2021. El Salvador’s 7% is well below that pace.

Are exports to the United States growing?

Regional shipments to the United States are projected to rise 24% in value in 2026. For El Salvador alone, BCR data show US shipments up 2.4% to US$1.48 billion in January to August.

What are El Salvador’s projected imports?

Diario El Mundo reports goods imports of more than US$18.13 billion, up nearly 9% from US$16.66 billion in 2025. That implies a goods trade gap near US$12.2 billion.

Who published the forecast?

The UN Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean published it in its annual trade outlook. Executive Secretary José Manuel Salazar-Xirinachs leads the commission.

Sources: ECLAC press release, 15 October 2026; Diario El Mundo, 16 October 2026; Estrategia & Negocios on BCR data, 25 September 2026; La Tribuna, 15 October 2026 (accessed 20 October 2026).

World.title: Lula Vows Free Weekend Transit, Debt Relief
World.content:
Senafront officers and US soldiers after a helicopter cargo-lifting course at Panama Pacifico airport. File photo, 27 July 2026. (Photo: Staff Sgt. Ethan Sherwood, US Air Force, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Tuesday, 20 October, 1:50 p.m. ET · Source: Folha de S.Paulo, O Liberal, SBT News

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened At a campaign event in São Luís on Tuesday 20 October, Lula said he plans to send Congress a free weekend public transport amendment and sign a debt-relief bill into law on Wednesday 21 October.

The pledges The debt bill covers about 4 million micro-entrepreneurs, and the transport amendment would make public transport free on Saturdays and Sundays.

The records Lula repeated his demand that Flávio Bolsonaro open his bank and phone records, and said his lawyers will ask the electoral court to open his own.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 77.0% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (20 October, 1:46 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 77% and Kalshi at 79% (Lula: 23% and 21% ), as of 20 October, 1:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The cost of the transport plan and Flávio Bolsonaro’s reply on the records were not in the reports reviewed.

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said in São Luís on Tuesday 20 October that he plans to send Congress a free weekend transport amendment on Wednesday. He also plans to sign into law a bill wiping out the federal tax debts of about 4 million micro-entrepreneurs the same day.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.1%, Lula 48.9% 26 national polls from 14 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

The promises came five days before the Brazil election 2026 runoff on Sunday 25 October against Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro. Lula also repeated that this is his last presidential campaign, according to Folha de S.Paulo.

What Lula Promised in São Luís

At a campaign event in São Luís, the capital of Maranhão state, Lula said: “It is my last campaign for president now, and I want this term to be historic” (translated from Portuguese). Folha de S.Paulo described the measures as an election-eve package of benefits.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The amendment would make public transport free on Saturdays and Sundays, and Lula said it goes to the Senate on Wednesday 21 October. He first announced the plan on 15 October, and SBT News reported that it would be paid for with parliamentary amendments, the budget funds that lawmakers direct to local projects.

How the Debt Relief Would Work

The bill covers micro-entrepreneurs, people who register as one-person businesses, whose debts sit on the federal government’s list of unpaid tax debts. Lula said the measure lets them clear their names and restart their activities, and that he will sign it on Wednesday, according to Folha de S.Paulo and O Liberal.

A constitutional amendment needs three-fifths of both houses in two rounds of voting each, which means 308 of 513 deputies and 49 of 81 senators. Sending the text on Wednesday starts that process rather than finishing it.

Lula Presses Flávio Bolsonaro on Bank Records

Lula again challenged Flávio Bolsonaro to release his bank and phone records. “I want to see if he has the courage to open his bank secrecy, his phone secrecy,” Lula said, in a translation of his Portuguese words.

He said his lawyers would ask the electoral court (TSE) to open his own records and those of his family, including the first lady and his children. It repeats the offer Lula’s campaign announced on 19 October, according to CNN Brasil, which was tied to a matching step by his rival.

What It Means for US Readers

Free transport and wider debt relief carry fiscal costs, and investors in Brazilian bonds, the real and US-listed Brazilian shares weigh such promises before a vote. No cost estimate for the transport plan appeared in the reports we reviewed.

Polls remain close, so any reaction from voters would show up in the surveys listed in our Brazil election polls tracker, not in the announcements themselves. The next surveys are due before the vote on 25 October.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro a 77.0% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (20 October, 1:46 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has about US$189.0 million in total bets.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

The cost of the free weekend transport plan has not been published in the reports we reviewed. It is also unknown whether Congress will take up the amendment before the runoff.

Flávio Bolsonaro’s reply to Lula’s demand on bank records was not in those reports. No ruling on the request from Lula’s lawyers has been reported.

More: Brazil news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Lula promise in São Luís on 20 October?

He said he plans to send Congress an amendment for free public transport on Saturdays and Sundays and sign into law a bill forgiving federal debts of about 4 million micro-entrepreneurs, both on Wednesday 21 October. He spoke at a campaign event five days before the runoff.

Who is covered by the micro-entrepreneur debt bill?

It covers about 4 million micro-entrepreneurs with debts on the federal list of unpaid tax debts, according to Folha de S.Paulo and O Liberal. They are people who register as one-person businesses.

What did Lula say about Flávio Bolsonaro’s bank records?

He challenged Flávio Bolsonaro to open his bank and phone records. He said his lawyers would ask the electoral court to open his own records and his family’s.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October. The two candidates are Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

World.title: Costa Rica University Protests Move Forward After Lawmakers Approve New Budget Cuts
World.content:
Costa Rica’s public universities are moving ahead with a major demonstration in San José today after lawmakers approved a controversial reduction in university funding late last night. The decision has added new tension to an already heated dispute over government spending and the future of public higher education.

Students, professors, university employees and labor unions from the five public universities are expected to participate in the march, which begins at 9 a.m. at the Fuente de la Hispanidad in San Pedro. Demonstrators plan to walk toward the Legislative Assembly in downtown San José, where protests and other activities are scheduled throughout the day.

The demonstration comes just hours after lawmakers on the Legislative Assembly’s Finance Committee approved a proposal to redirect ₡8.048 billion from funds previously allocated to public universities. The money comes from the Special Fund for Higher Education, known as FEES, which provides government funding to Costa Rica’s public universities. Under the proposal, the funds would instead be used to cover outstanding employer contributions to the national teachers’ pension system, Jupema.

The decision followed an unusual series of events yesterday. During an initial vote, the proposed reduction was rejected after ruling-party lawmaker Kattia Ulate voted against it, joining opposition legislators. Ulate later said she had voted incorrectly. The governing Pueblo Soberano party requested another vote, and the committee approved the funding reduction by six votes to five during an evening session.

The reversal came as university leaders were preparing for today’s demonstration, giving protesters another reason to take their concerns directly to lawmakers. University officials have warned that the proposed budget changes could reduce scholarships, limit the number of students admitted to public universities and threaten academic programs, particularly outside the Greater Metropolitan Area.

Our five public universities are the University of Costa Rica (UCR), National University (UNA), Costa Rica Institute of Technology (TEC), State Distance University (UNED) and National Technical University (UTN). The National Council of Rectors (Conare), which represents the five institutions, estimates that several proposed reductions could affect approximately ₡26 billion in funding across the 2026 and 2027 budgets.

University leaders say the changes could have serious consequences for campuses in rural communities, where access to higher education is already more limited than in the Central Valley. The Costa Rica Institute of Technology has warned that proposed funding reductions could threaten operations at its Limón campus. Education Minister Leonardo Sánchez has challenged that assessment, arguing that the university has substantial financial reserves.

University officials maintain that much of that money cannot legally be used to cover everyday operating expenses. The dispute is also about funds that universities agreed to postpone receiving during the COVID-19 pandemic. At the time, university leaders accepted delays in government payments to help the country respond to the health emergency. They now argue that permanently redirecting some of those resources would undermine commitments made to the institutions.

Government lawmakers, meanwhile, maintain that budget adjustments are necessary to meet other public financial obligations, including payments to the teachers’ pension system. For students, the concern is that reduced funding could eventually mean fewer scholarships, fewer available spaces in university programs and fewer opportunities to study close to home.

The debate also extends beyond university campuses. Public universities train a large share of Costa Rica’s professionals in fields such as engineering, science, education and healthcare. University leaders argue that limiting their budgets could affect the country’s ability to prepare workers and attract investment.

Today’s protest is expected to bring together more than university organizations. Other labor, agricultural and social groups have been invited to participate in demonstrations against proposed reductions in public spending. The main march is scheduled to reach the Plaza de la Democracia near the Legislative Assembly at approximately 11 a.m. Organizers have planned activities through the afternoon, with the gathering expected to continue until around 6 p.m.

Traffic disruptions are expected in San Pedro and central San José, particularly along the route between the Fuente de la Hispanidad and the Legislative Assembly. The University of Costa Rica has authorized the closure of administrative offices during the demonstration and postponed examinations and graded assignments scheduled during the affected hours. Smaller demonstrations and activities are also planned in other parts of the country.

Despite last night’s committee decision, the funding reduction is not yet final. The proposed changes must still go through the remaining legislative process before becoming part of the national budget. The Finance Committee faces an October 20 deadline to complete its review of the proposed 2027 budget, while the full Legislative Assembly has until November 30 to approve the spending plan.

For now, university leaders and students are hoping today’s demonstration will convince lawmakers to reconsider the reductions before the budget receives final approval. The size of the turnout and the government’s response could determine whether today’s march remains a one-day protest or becomes the beginning of a larger movement over public education funding.

World.title: University March Will Slow San José Traffic Tuesday From 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.
World.content:
If you need to get across eastern San José or downtown tomorrow, plan around a national march against cuts to public university funding. Marchers start gathering in San Pedro at 8 a.m., and a rally outside the Legislative Assembly is scheduled to run until 6 p.m.

The main march leaves at 9 a.m. from the Fuente de la Hispanidad roundabout in San Pedro and heads to the Legislative Assembly on Cuesta de Moras. University of Costa Rica students and staff are meeting first at the Pretil on the main campus at 8:30 a.m. to walk over and join the others. By 11 a.m., marchers plan to converge on the Plaza de la Democracia, across from the Assembly.

Organizers have scheduled cultural activities there through the afternoon, and the day is set to close with a vigil. Expect slow traffic and possible closures around the Fuente de la Hispanidad and on the main roads between San Pedro and downtown from about 8 a.m. until late morning. After that, the pressure shifts to the blocks around the Plaza de la Democracia, the National Museum and Cuesta de Moras until early evening.

If you are driving between the airport, Escazú or Santa Ana and the east side of the city, give yourself extra time or stay off the downtown avenues. Buses that run through San Pedro and past the Assembly could be delayed or rerouted. Planning a visit to the University of Costa Rica on Tuesday? Check before you go.

The university has allowed its administrative offices to close between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. so staff can take part, and it has postponed exams and graded work scheduled in those hours, according to a circular from Rector Carlos Araya. Organizers say smaller marches will also set out from other parts of the country, so check local conditions if you are traveling outside the capital.

The protest targets cuts proposed for the country’s five public universities in the 2027 national budget. The National Council of Rectors (Conare) says reductions to the universities’ main state fund would hit scholarships, admission slots and regional campuses. Among the specific cuts Conare has cited are ₡462 million for student science olympiads and ₡492.9 million for the Technological Institute of Costa Rica’s campus in Limón. TEC Rector María Estrada has warned the Limón campus could be forced to close.

Education Minister Leonardo Sánchez accused Estrada of political extortion over that warning and said the institute holds more than ₡20 billion in cash and investments. Estrada responded that capital and surplus funds cannot legally be used to pay a campus’s day-to-day operating costs.

The date was chosen with the budget calendar in mind. Tuesday is the deadline for the Assembly’s budget committee to finish its review of the 2027 budget and send it to the full Assembly, where ruling-party Pueblo Soberano deputies have pushed for the reductions. National University Rector Jorge Herrera has confirmed his institution is taking part, describing the march as a defense of opportunities for people in the country’s regions.

Farm organizations, culture and human-rights groups, and opponents of Costa Rica joining the CPTPP Pacific trade pact have also been invited to join. Conare has asked marchers to act with respect and responsibility. Former Frente Amplio presidential candidate Ariel Robles has gone further, urging people to camp outside the Legislative Assembly and the Presidential House to keep up the pressure.

Once the committee sends the budget to the floor, the full Legislative Assembly has until November 30 to approve the 2027 spending plan.
